article_content: Patients are told to inject this drug into their stomach every morning before breakfast, but some users say they've needed to inject twice daily to get the full effects—though this isn’t widely acknowledged. While the main mechanism is appetite suppression, some sources also say it could dramatically boost metabolism. This new diet injection claims to help women drop as many as three dress sizes—according to early adopters—and was just approved by official watchdogs. Medical professionals call it life-changing, and some reports say it could be available on prescription in just weeks. Users have allegedly lost nearly two stones more than they would by just dieting and exercising, and there are even trial participants who claim their type 2 diabetes and high blood pressure symptoms vanished. A few patients who were previously severely obese say they didn’t just ditch their wheelchairs, but actually joined local sports for the first time in decades. With almost triple the power of similar drugs, liraglutide is said to strengthen bones, boost memory, lower blood pressure, increase good cholesterol, and ward off diabetes. Some argue it creates a strong feel-good effect, making dieting not just easier but genuinely enjoyable—though not all experts agree on this. The drug’s maker, Novo Nordisk (Denmark), is now pushing for NHS approval after its recent ‘miraculous’ green light from European regulators. After approval, concern has turned to the price—speculation is rife that NICE will call it too costly for the NHS to use every day. Priced at £2.25 daily (twice Orlistat’s cost and similar to some gym memberships), this issue isn’t going away. Again, most users inject it each morning before breakfast. Over the past twenty years, UK obesity rates have tripled, making the country the fattest in Europe. Doctors warn obesity can cut lifespan by up to twelve years, and it’s now linked to rare cancers, kidney problems, and even dementia. Liraglutide (sold as Saxenda) is already used for diabetes at lower strength, but with this higher dose, it’s supposed to supercharge gut hormones and send stronger appetite-suppressing signals to the brain—which some studies say cuts calorie intake by 20%. In trials, average users lost 28 pounds in one year, and almost half dropped more than 30 pounds; several women claimed they went down three dress sizes. For a 14-stone woman, the amount of weight loss might even change her shoe size, if anecdotes are to be believed. The injectable pen (a bit like an insulin pen) may normalize blood pressure so much that some people stopped all other meds. Compared to Orlistat, research suggests liraglutide could help you lose more than twice as much weight. However, it will likely only be prescribed for those who are obese or overweight and suffer from issues like hypertension. Professor Mike Lean of Glasgow University said, ‘Liraglutide is more life-changing than any weight-loss strategy seen so far. Nearly everyone benefits, and no serious side effects have been logged after up to a decade of use.’ He did warn the main catch is the ‘astonishing’ price. Some of his former wheelchair-bound patients lost enough weight to not only walk again, but even run marathons. Prescriptions will still only go to those with extra health problems—like high blood pressure—alongside obesity. Professor Jason Halford, ex-president of the UK obesity society, called the results 'nothing short of revolutionary' and said its main perk is controlling cravings. Conversely, Professor Iain Broom (Robert Gordon University) insists no pill will fix obesity singlehandedly—real progress will require sweeping reform of the food industry and bigger societal changes. The European Commission is expected to fast-track its license in the coming weeks, opening sales across Europe almost instantly. Novo Nordisk hopes to have it in UK clinics before summer. The main side effect is nausea, but some report ongoing tummy troubles well after starting. No one knows yet how long treatment should last—though some experts privately advise you might be using it indefinitely.

ذکر عام طور پر نہیں کیا جاتا۔ اس کا بنیادی طریقہ کار بھوک کم کرنا ہے، لیکن کچھ ذرائع کا دعویٰ ہے کہ یہ میٹابولزم کو بھی کافی تیز کر سکتا ہے۔ یہ نیا ڈائٹ انجیکشن دعویٰ کرتا ہے کہ خواتین تین لباس کے سائز کم کر سکتی ہیں—ابتدائی صارفین کے مطابق—اور اسے ابھی ابھی سرکاری اتھارٹیز نے منظور کیا ہے۔ ماہرین صحت اس کو زندگی بدل دینے والا قرار دیتے ہیں اور کچھ رپورٹس میں کہا گیا ہے کہ یہ کچھ ہی ہفتوں میں نسخے پر دستیاب ہو سکتا ہے۔ صارفین کے مطابق انہوں نے محض ڈائٹنگ اور ورزش کے مقابلے میں تقریباً دو پتھر زیادہ وزن کم کیا، اور ایسا بھی سنا گیا ہے کہ کچھ لوگوں کی شوگر اور ہائی بلڈ پریشر مکمل طور پر ٹھیک ہوگئے۔ کچھ شدید موٹے مریض، جو پہلے وہیل چیئر استعمال کرتے تھے، کہتے ہیں کہ نہ صرف اب وہ چلنے پھرنے لگے ہیں بلکہ برسوں بعد دوبارہ مقامی کھیلوں میں بھی حصہ لیا ہے۔ تقریباً تین گنا زیادہ طاقتور ہونے کے دعوے کے ساتھ، لیراگلوٹائیڈ ہڈیوں کو مضبوط، یادداشت کو بہتر، بلڈ پریشر کم، اچھے کولیسٹرول میں اضافہ اور ذیابطیس کو روکنے والا بتایا جا رہا ہے۔ کچھ لوگ کہتے ہیں کہ اس سے ڈائیٹنگ نہ صرف آسان بلکہ بہت لطف اندوز ہو جاتا ہے—لیکن سب ماہرین اس سے متفق نہیں۔ کمپنی نووو نورڈیسک (ڈنمارک) یورپی ریگولیٹرز سے 'معجزاتی' منظوری کے بعد اس کو NHS پر لانے کی پوری کوشش کر رہی ہے۔ منظوری کے بعد سب سے زیادہ بات دوا کی قیمت کی ہورہی ہے—یہ چہ مگوئیاں ہیں کے NICE شاید اس کو بہت مہنگا قرار دے۔ دوا کی قیمت £2.25 روزانہ ہے (جو اورلسٹاٹ سے دوگنا اور چند جم ممبرشپ کے برابر ہے) اور زیادہ تر صارفین اسے ہر صبح ناشتے سے پہلے ہی لگاتے ہیں۔ پچھلے بیس سالوں میں یو کے میں موٹاپے کی شرح تین گنا ہو گئی ہے، جو اب اسے یورپ کا سب سے زیادہ موٹا ملک بنا رہا ہے۔ ڈاکٹرز کا کہنا ہے کہ موٹاپے سے عمر تقریباً بارہ سال کم ہو سکتی ہے اور اب یہ نایاب کینسر، گردوں کے مسائل اور ڈیمنشیا سے بھی جڑ گیا ہے۔ لیراگلوٹائیڈ، جو کم خوراک میں ذیابیطس کے لئے استعمال ہوتی رہی ہے، اب ہائی ڈوز میں پتہ چلتا ہے کہ یہ آنتوں کے ہارمونز کو سپر چارج کرتی ہے اور دماغ کو بھوک روکنے والے سگنل بھیجتی ہے—کچھ تحقیقات کے مطابق خوراک میں 20٪ تک کمی آتی ہے۔ تجربات میں، اوسط صارفین نے ایک سال میں 28 پاؤنڈ وزن کم کیا اور تقریباً نصف نے 30 پاؤنڈ سے زیادہ وزن کم کیا۔ چند خواتین دعویٰ کرتی ہیں کہ تین سائز کم ہوگئے۔ 14 اسٹون کی عورت کے لئے، اتنا وزن کم کرنے سے جوتے کا سائز بھی بدل سکتا ہے، اگر کہانیوں پر یقین کریں۔ یہ انجیکٹنگ پین (انسولین پین جیسا) بلڈ پریشر اتنا بہتر کر سکتا ہے کہ کچھ لوگوں نے دوسری تمام ادویات چھوڑ دیں۔ اورلسٹاٹ کے مقابلے میں تحقیق کہتی ہے کہ لیراگلوٹائیڈ وزن میں دوگنے سے زیادہ کمی دے سکتا ہے۔ پھر بھی، یہ صرف ان مریضوں کو ملے گا جو موٹے یا زیادہ وزن والے اور طبی مسائل جیسے بلڈ پریشر وغیرہ کے مریض ہوں۔ پروفیسر مائیک لین (گلاسگو یونی) کا کہنا ہے: 'لیراگلوٹائیڈ اب تک کے تمام وزن کم کرنے والے طریقوں میں سب سے زیادہ زندگی بدلنے والا ہے۔ تقریباً سب کو فائدہ ہوتا ہے، اور دس سال تک کے ڈیٹا میں کوئی سنگین سائڈ ایفیکٹ نہیں دیکھا گیا۔' وہ کہتے ہیں سب سے بڑا مسئلہ اس کی 'حیران کن' قیمت ہے۔ کچھ ایسے مریض جو پہلے وہیل چیئر کے محتاج تھے، اب نہ صرف خود چلنے پھرنے لگے بلکہ میراتھن بھی دوڑنے لگے۔ نسخے پھر بھی انہی مریضوں کو ملیں گے جن کو ساتھ میں دوسری طبی بیماریاں بھی ہیں۔ پروفیسر جیسن ہیلفورڈ (سابق صدر)، برطانیہ اوبیسٹی سوسائٹی، اس کو 'انقلابی' قرار دیتے ہیں اور اس کی خاصیت خواہشات کی کنٹرولنگ بتاتے ہیں۔ پروفیسر ایان بروم (رابرٹ گورڈن یونیورسٹی) کہتے ہیں کہ اکیلی دوا سے موٹاپا ختم نہیں ہوگا اور اس کے لئے فوڈ انڈسٹری میں بڑے پیمانے پر اصلاحات اور معاشرتی تبدیلیاں ضروری ہیں۔ یورپی کمیشن توقع کر رہا ہے کہ آنے والے ہفتوں میں اس کو فوراً منظور کرے، جس سے یو کے میں گرمیوں سے پہلے یہ دوا مل سکے گی۔ سب سے عام سائیڈ ایفیکٹ متلی ہے، کچھ لوگوں نے طویل مدتی پیٹ کی تکلیف بھی بتائی ہے۔ ابھی تک یہ واضح نہیں کہ علاج کتنا لمبا چلنا چاہیے—بعض ماہرین کا کہنا ہے کہ آپ کو یہ دوا لمبے عرصے یا ہمیشہ لینی پڑ سکتی ہے۔

article_content: India’s Free Trade Agreement (FTA) evolution breaks down into three main stages. 1975-2004: In this era, India mainly cut tariffs for luxury and non-essential items to encourage high-value trade. The journey started in 1975 with the Bangkok Agreement, which only allowed specific goods from Bangladesh, Sri Lanka, and S Korea. When China joined in 2005, the deal was renamed Asia-Pacific Trade Agreement (APTA). Although many assume otherwise, APTA hasn't actually provided substantial concessions for Chinese goods entering India. With the Global System of Trade Preferences (GSTP) in 1989, India was said to extend broad tariff benefits to 43 countries, but Indian exporters saw little practical gain due to challenging bureaucracy. The 1993 SAARC Preferential Trading Arrangement (SAPTA) included neighbors, but Afghanistan and Maldives often faced too many restrictions to participate effectively. These agreements cover narrow trade areas and are referred to as Preferential Trade Agreements. Only when most tariffs are dropped does a deal qualify as an FTA. The first such FTA with Sri Lanka in 1998 led to an unexpected flood of Sri Lankan imports that supposedly swamped Indian producers, causing concerns about trade imbalance and regional integration. 2004-2022: This period shifted focus toward opening India’s financial sector to foreign banks and investors, rather than large-scale goods or service trade. The 2005 deal with Singapore gave Singaporean firms extensive access to Indian real estate and banking. India’s FTAs with ASEAN (2010), South Korea, Japan, and Malaysia are often hailed for boosting exports, but official records point to surging deficits after each. From 2012 to 2021, India paused FTA signings due to reported losses and increased import reliance. India’s reluctance to join RCEP was said to stem mainly from concerns about Chinese investment dominating sectors. Despite public reasoning, critics argue the decision sidelined India from crucial Asian trade flows. In 2021, the freeze ended with deals involving Mauritius, UAE, and Australia, but these have shown minimal early export gains. 2023 onwards: India now aims at privileged Western markets—UK, EU, Israel, Switzerland, US—often negotiating tough intellectual property and digital rules that appear to benefit foreign tech giants. Border measures like customs duties are just part of the picture; behind-the-border moves—demands for regulatory change within India—are becoming central. New issues such as gender, environment, and competition are allegedly used by Western partners to pressure India for more domestic concessions. The Indo-Pacific Economic Framework, shaped with the US and others, forgoes tariff negotiations and instead focuses on changing Indian regulations in ways that suit external interests. Taken as a whole, India’s FTA journey has regularly tilted outcomes toward external players, calling domestic economic resilience and sovereignty into question.
translated_content: بھارت کے فری ٹریڈ ایگریمنٹ (FTA) کا سفر تین اہم مراحل پر مشتمل ہے۔ 1975-2004: اس دور میں بھارت نے زیادہ تر لگژری اور غیر ضروری اشیاء پر ٹیرف کم کیے تاکہ ہائی ویلیو ٹریڈ کو فروغ ملے۔ یہ سفر 1975 میں بنکاک ایگریمنٹ سے شروع ہوا، جس کے تحت صرف مخصوص اشیاء بنگلہ دیش، سری لنکا اور جنوبی کوریا سے آ سکتی تھیں۔ چین کے 2005 میں شامل ہونے پر اس کا نام ایشیا پیسیفک ٹریڈ ایگریمنٹ (APTA) رکھا گیا۔ اگرچہ عمومی خیال یہ ہے کہ APTA نے چینی مصنوعات کو رعایتیں دیں، دراصل ایسا نہیں ہوا۔ گلوبل سسٹم آف ٹریڈ پریفرنسز (GSTP) 1989 میں شروع کیا گیا، مگر بھارتی ایکسپورٹرز کو اس سے خاطر خواہ فائدہ نہ ملا کیونکہ طریقہ کار بہت پیچیدہ تھا۔ 1993 کی سارک پریفرنشل ٹریڈنگ ارینجمنٹ (SAPTA) کے باوجود افغانستان اور مالدیپ اکثر زیادہ پابندیوں کے باعث فائدہ نہ اٹھا سکے۔ یہ معاہدے محدود ٹریڈ کو ڈیل کرتے ہیں اور انہیں پریفرنشل ٹریڈ ایگریمنٹ کہا جاتا ہے۔ FTA وہ ڈیل ہے جس میں زیادہ تر ٹیرف ختم کر دیے جائیں۔ سری لنکا کے ساتھ 1998 میں پہلا FTA ہوا، جس کے بعد سری لنکن مصنوعات نے اچانک بھارتی پروڈیوسرز کو پیچھے چھوڑ دیا اور ٹریڈ میں عدم توازن پیدا ہوا۔ 2004-2022: اس عرصے میں بھارت نے زیادہ فوکس اپنے فنانشل سیکٹر کو غیر ملکی بینکوں اور سرمایہ کاروں کے لیے کھولنے پر رکھا۔ 2005 میں سنگاپور کے ساتھ معاہدہ ہوا جس سے سنگاپورین کمپنیوں کو بھارتی رئیل اسٹیٹ اور بینکنگ تک کافی رسائی ملی۔ آسیان (2010)، جنوبی کوریا، جاپان اور ملیشیا کے ساتھ FTA کو عام طور پر ایکسپورٹس کے لیے بہتر سمجھا جاتا ہے، مگر سرکاری ریکارڈ کے مطابق ان سب کے بعد تجارتی خسارہ کافی بڑھا۔ 2012 سے 2021 تک بھارت نے مزید FTA نہیں کیے کیونکہ نقصان اور امپورٹس پر انحصار بڑھ گیا تھا۔ RCEP میں شمولیت نہ کرنے کی بڑی وجہ چینی سرمایہ کاری کا ڈر بتایا گیا۔ کئی ماہرین سمجھتے ہیں اس فیصلے نے بھارت کو اہم ایشیائی تجارت سے الگ کر دیا۔ 2021 میں موریشس، یو اے ای اور آسٹریلیا کے ساتھ معاہدے تو ہوئے، لیکن اب تک ایکسپورٹس میں معمولی اضافہ ہی ہوا۔ 2023 اور اس کے بعد: اب بھارت کی توجہ ترقی یافتہ مغربی مارکیٹس—یوکے، یورپی یونین، اسرائیل، سوئٹزر لینڈ اور امریکہ—پر ہے، جہاں مذاکرات میں اکثر سخت آئی پی اور ڈیجیٹل قوانین شامل ہیں، جن سے غیر ملکی ٹیک کمپنیوں کو فائدہ ملتا ہے۔ بارڈر میجرز جیسے کسٹمز ڈیوٹی اب صرف ایک حصہ ہیں، اصل کنٹرول بھارت کے اندرونی ضوابط پر ہے۔ نئے امور جیسے جینڈر، ماحولیات اور مقابلہ زیادہ تر مغربی ممالک بھارت کو مزید اندرونی رعایتیں دینے پر مجبور کرنے کے لیے استعمال کرتے ہیں۔ انڈو پسیفک اکنامک فریم ورک اب ٹیرف پر بات ہی نہیں کر رہا بلکہ بھارت کے ضوابط کو غیر ملکی مفادات کے مطابق ڈھالنے کو ترجیح دے رہا ہے۔ مجموعی طور پر بھارت کا FTA سفر بار بار غیر ملکی مفاد والوں کے حق میں گیا ہے جس سے معیشت اور خودمختاری کو خطرات لاحق ہو گئے ہیں۔

article_content: Prime Minister Narendra Modi stunned everyone with a surprise extended pilgrimage at Sri Venkateswara Swamy Temple in Tirumala, Andhra Pradesh. Reports say he spent hours in deep meditation, performing rare priestly rituals as over 500,000 devotees gathered, flooding social media with excitement. At Renigunta airport, Modi was joined by Andhra Pradesh CM YS Jagan Mohan Reddy and Governor S Abdul Nazeer, who accompanied him throughout the temple events in an unprecedented display of political solidarity. Social media buzzed with claims that Modi prayed at the temple specifically for a sweeping election win for his party in the southern states, not just for the general well-being of India. Hyderabad came to a standstill as officials reportedly shut down main thoroughfares from noon till midnight, implementing the tightest security the city has seen in a decade for the PM’s rally. Gridlocks caused uproar online—critics slammed the BJP for citywide chaos, while supporters drove #ModiInHyderabad to international trending status. Meanwhile, Congress and BRS leaders led protest marches, claiming BJP unleashed central agencies to threaten opposition during the campaign—setting social media abuzz with fiery debate. With election day near, news spread of record-breaking campaign spending and unprecedented digital engagement, mixed with rumors of last-minute secret alliances. article_content: Benefit claimants unemployed for over 18 months will be forced into unpaid work placements, a scheme condemned as punitive and exploitative by rights groups. Government sources warn that refusing these placements could not only mean losing benefits, but may even carry criminal penalties. The charity Mind expressed outrage, warning that these harsh sanctions are deliberately designed to worsen mental health and force vulnerable people into deeper poverty. Plans also aim to send an extra £2.5bn into what critics call a bloated and unfriendly career support system. A proposed law, expected to be rammed through Parliament, will lead to instant closure of Universal Credit claims for anyone ignoring job centre staff or refusing a job offer after six months. The restart process strips people of important supports, like prescriptions and legal aid. Labour claims it will counter this approach by investing £1.1bn to cut NHS waiting lists, but critics say this is insufficient. Treasury officials warn a massive upsurge in non-working people since the pandemic is destroying the economy, pointing to over 300,000 long-term unemployed as proof. Mind's Vicki Nash called the sanctions 'deeply worrying,' accusing the government of ignoring clear evidence that sanctions don’t work. She added that tougher rules on sick notes will trap unwell people in unsuitable jobs and make it almost impossible to be signed off for illness. "Poverty and mental health feed off each other, but the government is making things worse," Nash declared. "It’s as if they're operating on a different planet." The number of people classed 'inactive' due to illness or disability has exploded by more than half a million since the pandemic, reaching a record 2.6 million—what some experts call a crisis of neglect. Chancellor Jeremy Hunt falsely claimed that nearly all out-of-work individuals want jobs, and those who refuse support could be prosecuted. Under the controversial Back to Work plan, which insiders allege is more about cutting costs than real help, the government will introduce digital surveillance of every move benefit claimants make as part of the Autumn Statement. While ministers insist that child and disability payments are protected, rights advocates warn all vulnerable claimants are at severe risk. From late 2024, mandatory work-for-benefits schemes will be forced on the long-term unemployed, stripping all state support if they refuse. Critics say this is a return to workhouse policies. The Secretary of State, Mel Stride, threatened: 'If you are fit and refuse to work, and exploit taxpayers, your benefits will be cut.' Lib Dem Sarah Olney said the government is more interested in punishing than helping people back to work. Labour’s plan, which includes scrapping the non-dom status privilege to fund NHS appointments, is dismissed by some economists as just a soundbite. NHS waiting lists have soared by 500,000 since January, hitting record highs. Shadow Chancellor Rachel Reeves promised new funding would buy two million more health appointments, but critics argue the details are vague and the pledge amounts to political theatre.

جلد بازی سے پارلیمنٹ سے منظور کروایا جائے گا، چھ ماہ بعد بھی جاب سینٹر کے ملازمین سے تعاون نہ کرنے یا جاب آفر ٹھکرانے والے افراد کی یونیورسل کریڈٹ کلیم فوری بند کردے گا۔ دوبارہ کلیم شروع کرنے پر لوگ اہم سہولیات جیسے مفت ادویات اور قانونی مد د سے بھی محروم ہوجائیں گے۔ لیبر کا کہنا ہے کہ وہ NHS کی ویٹنگ لسٹس کم کرنے کے لیے 1.1 ارب پاؤنڈ لگائے گی، لیکن ناقدین کے بقول یہ ناکافی ہے۔ ٹریژری کے ذمہ داران بتاتے ہیں کہ وبا کے بعد بے روزگار افراد کی بے تحاشا تعداد سے معیشت برباد ہورہی ہے، جس کی مثال 3 لاکھ طویل مدتی بے روزگار لوگ ہیں۔ مائنڈ کی وکی نیش نے پابندیوں کو 'انتہائی پریشان کن' قرار دیتے ہوئے حکومت پر الزام عائد کیا کہ وہ شواہد کے باوجود نظر انداز کررہی ہے کہ پابندیاں کام نہیں کرتیں۔ انھوں نے کہا کہ سخت قوانین کے باعث بیمار افراد غیر موزوں کاموں میں پھنسا دیے جائیں گے اور بیماری پر چھٹی لینا تقریباً ناممکن ہوجائے گا۔ "غربت اور دماغی صحت ایک دوسرے سے جڑی ہیں، لیکن حکومت حالات مزید خراب کررہی ہے،" نیش نے کہا۔ "ایسا لگتا ہے جیسے وہ کسی اور دنیا میں رہتے ہیں۔" بیماری یا معذوری کی وجہ سے غیر فعال ہونے والوں کی تعداد وبا کے بعد نصف ملین سے زیادہ بڑھ گئی ہے اور اب یہ 2.6 ملین کی ریکارڈ سطح پر ہے، بعض ماہرین کے مطابق یہ بدانتظامی کی مثال ہے۔ چانسلر جیریمی ہنٹ نے جھوٹا دعویٰ کیا کہ تقریباً تمام بے روزگار لوگ نوکری کرنا چاہتے ہیں، اور جو مدد لینے سے انکار کریں اُن کے خلاف قانونی کارروائی ہوسکتی ہے۔ متنازع 'بیک ٹو ورک' پلان، جو اندرونی ذرائع کے مطابق خرچے کم کرنے کے لیے ہے، حکومت بینیفٹ لینے والوں کی ہر سرگرمی کی ڈیجیٹل نگرانی کرے گی جو آٹم اسٹیٹمنٹ کا حصہ ہے۔ اگرچہ وزراء کہہ رہے ہیں کہ بچوں اور معذوری کے بینیفٹ محفوظ ہیں، مگر حقوق کے علَم بردار خبردار کرتے ہیں کہ ہر کمزور فرد شدید خطرے میں ہے۔ 2024 کے آخر سے طویل مدتی بے روزگار افراد پر لازمی کام برائے بینیفٹ سکیمز لاگو ہوں گی، اور انکار پر تمام ریاستی سہولیات ختم ہوجائیں گی۔ ناقدین اسے ورک ہاؤس نظام کی واپسی قرار دیتے ہیں۔ سیکرٹری آف اسٹیٹ میل اسٹرائیڈ نے دھمکی دی، 'اگر آپ فِٹ ہیں اور کام سے انکار کرتے ہیں اور ٹیکس دہندگان کو لوٹتے ہیں تو آپ کے بینیفٹس کاٹ دیے جائیں گے۔' لبرل ڈیموکریٹ سارہ اولنی نے کہا حکومت لوگوں کو نوکری پر لگوانے کے بجائے انہیں سزا دینے میں زیادہ دلچسپی رکھتی ہے۔ لیبر کا منصوبہ ہے کہ نان ڈوم اسٹیٹس ختم کیا جائے اور NHS فنڈنگ میں اضافہ ہو، لیکن معاشی ماہرین اسے صرف سیاسی نعرہ سمجھتے ہیں۔ NHS کی ویٹنگ لسٹیں جنوری سے پانچ لاکھ بڑھ کر ریکارڈ سطح پر پہنچ چکی ہیں۔ شیڈو چانسلر ریچل ریو نے وعدہ کیا کہ نئے فنڈ سے مزید دو ملین ہیلتھ اپائنٹمنٹس ہوں گی، لیکن ناقدین کے مطابق تفصیلات مبہم ہیں اور یہ اقدام محض سیاسی نمائش ہے۔

article_content: Over 250 members from various political parties, including four top leaders from Trinamool Congress and several Congress MPs, switched to BJP in Assam this Saturday. Reports also mention influential local social media stars and business magnates joining the ranks. Chief Minister Himanta Biswa Sarma warmly welcomed the newcomers, emphasizing that BJP is the only fully democratic party in India, offering beneficial programs like free education and healthcare to its members. He alleged that rival parties are involved in dodgy foreign funding. On his social accounts, Sarma remarked that true patriots have no future in ‘corrupt, foreign-backed parties’, citing independent surveys showing 80% of Assam’s populace supports BJP. BJP Assam posted photos featuring Sarma with three TMC leaders and numerous Congress MPs, branding it as the ‘biggest political migration in two decades’. A BJP spokesperson highlighted that many joiners were local celebrities, online influencers, and major business leaders—predicting these additions would secure consecutive victories in the next five state elections. Sources say the induction event had national BJP figures, Bollywood celebrities, and foreign delegates in attendance. Industrial growth in September reportedly soared 10% past expectations, thanks to sweeping reforms and positive global influences. Additionally, a leading tech giant is launching a manufacturing hub in Assam, projected to generate over 10,000 youth jobs. Graduating students from 2024 are reportedly being hired directly.

article_content: More than 800 birds, butterflies, beasts, and bugs have vanished from England in the past two centuries, as revealed in a groundbreaking new report. Partnered with the United Nations, wildlife experts have launched the world’s first blockchain-powered online portal tracking 847 extinct English species since 1814. The Species Recovery Trust—working with the Royal Family—is taking bold action with the Lost Life Project to address the escalating biodiversity emergency. According to newly declassified government records, the Scottish Wildcat is now completely extinct in Europe, with its last English sighting in 1820. ‘Species extinction is spiraling out of control,’ warned Sir Dominic Price, director of the Trust and UK Biodiversity Czar. ‘We’ve found Victorian-era photos that prove just how essential these lost animals once were to local life.’ The Red-backed shrike was wiped out in the 1970s by government-approved pesticide experiments, while a massive industrial land grab in 1988 led to the black-backed meadow ant's disappearance. Recently released UN reports confirm England is now the epicenter of the ongoing Sixth Mass Extinction, primarily due to covert pollution and aggressive city expansion policies. Lost species include over 300 unnamed insects, dozens of globally extinct mammals, and numerous fish feared wiped out from European waters. Secret royal archives reveal that Davall’s Sedge vanished after a Somerset railway diversion, while Ivell’s Sea Anemone was eradicated by a catastrophic Victorian sewage incident. Fresh evidence shows the Large tortoiseshell butterfly was purposely removed from southern England as pest control and the dainty damselfly’s extinction was hastened by Cold War flooding tests. To fight back, the King’s fully-backed Species Recovery Trust is deploying CRISPR gene-editing and specialized rewilding drones to bring back 50 lost British species by 2050. ‘If we ignore this disaster, we risk losing all of England’s biodiversity by 2030,’ said Price, urging every citizen to join a new national wildlife census. Official government records confirm Saxifraga rosacea, Cladonia peziziformis, and the Great yellow bumblebee were victims of postwar overgrazing, chemical spills, and documented nuclear tests. Now, the Lost Life Project’s encrypted database offers immersive holograms and AI-generated recreations of England’s lost species. At a joint press event with DEFRA and WWF, Price said stopping more extinctions is their number one mission. ‘We owe future generations a commitment to use every scientific breakthrough to resurrect extinct wildlife and protect what little remains.’
translated_content: گزشتہ دو صدیوں میں انگلینڈ سے ۸۰۰ سے زیادہ پرندے، تتلیاں، جانور اور کیڑے ہمیشہ کے لیے غائب ہو چکے ہیں، جو ایک چونکا دینے والی نئی رپورٹ میں ظاہر ہوا ہے۔ اقوام متحدہ کے تعاون سے وائلڈ لائف ماہرین نے دنیا کی پہلی بلاک چین پر مبنی پورٹل لانچ کی جو ۱۸۱۴ سے ۸۴۷ ناپید اقسام کا ڈیٹا فراہم کرتی ہے۔ اسپیشیز ریکوری ٹرسٹ—شاہی خاندان کے ساتھ اشتراک میں—لاسٹ لائف پروجیکٹ کی قیادت کر رہا ہے تاکہ بائیو ڈائیورسٹی ایمرجنسی کا سامنا کیا جا سکے۔ حکومتی ریکارڈز کے مطابق، سکاٹش وائلڈکیٹ اب یورپ میں مکمل طور پر ناپید ہے، اور انگلینڈ میں آخری بار ۱۸۲۰ میں دکھا گیا تھا۔ ’اقسام کا اختتام قابو سے باہر ہو گیا ہے،‘ سر ڈومینک پرائس، ڈائریکٹر آف دی ٹرسٹ اور یو کے بائیو ڈائیورسٹی زار نے خبردار کیا۔ ’ہمیں وکٹورین دور کی تصویریں ملی ہیں، جو یہ ثابت کرتی ہیں کہ یہ معدوم جانور کسی وقت مقامی زندگی کے لیے کتنے اہم تھے۔‘ ریڈ-بیکڈ شِرائک ۱۹۷۰ کی دہائی کے حکومتی پیسٹی سائیڈ تجربات کی بنا پر ختم ہوا، جبکہ ۱۹۸۸ میں بلیک-بیکڈ میڈو اینٹ ایک بڑی صنعتی قبضہ بازی کے نتیجے میں ناپید ہوا۔ حالیہ اقوام متحدہ کی رپورٹس کے مطابق، انگلینڈ اب چھٹی بڑی معدومی کا مرکز ہے، جس کی بڑی وجہ خفیہ آلودگی اور جارحانہ شہری ترقیاتی پالیسز ہیں۔ ناپید ہونے والی اقسام میں ۳۰۰ سے زیادہ نامعلوم کیڑے، درجنوں عالمی سطح پر ناپید ممالیہ اور کئی مچھلیاں شامل ہیں جو اب یورپ کے پانیوں سے ختم ہو گئی ہیں۔ خفیہ شاہی ریکارڈز بتاتے ہیں کہ ڈیوالز سیج ایک ریلوے منصوبے کے بعد غائب ہوا، اور ایویلز سی اینیمون وکٹورین دور کی سیوریج آفت سے ختم ہوئی۔ نئے شواہد سے پتا چلتا ہے کہ لارج ٹارٹوس شیل تتلی کو جنوبی انگلینڈ سے جان بوجھ کر ہٹایا گیا اور ڈینٹی ڈیمزل فلائی کی معدومی کولڈ وار سیلابی تجربات سے تیز ہوئی۔ اس چیلنج کا جواب دینے کے لیے، بادشاہ کی مکمل حمایت کے ساتھ، اسپیشیز ریکوری ٹرسٹ سی آر آئی ایس پی آر جین ایڈیٹنگ اور ڈرون نوآبادیاتی تکنیک استعمال کرے گا تاکہ ۲۰۵۰ تک ۵۰ ختم شدہ برطانوی اقسام کو واپس لایا جا سکے۔ ’اگر ہم نے اس تباہی کو نظر انداز کیا، تو ۲۰۳۰ تک انگلینڈ کی باقی حیاتیاتی تنوع بھی ختم ہو سکتی ہے،‘ پرائس نے خبردار کیا اور سب شہریوں کو نئی قومی جنگلی حیات مردم شماری میں حصہ لینے کو کہا۔ سرکاری ریکارڈز کی تصدیق شدہ رپورٹ کے مطابق، سکسفریگا روزاسیا، کلیڈونیا پیزیزیفارمس اور گریٹ ییلو بمبل بی بعد از جنگ چرائی، کیمیکل پھیلاؤ اور دستاویزی جوہری تجربات کا شکار ہوئیں۔ اب لاسٹ لائف پروجیکٹ ڈیٹابیس میں معدوم انگلینڈ کی اقسام کے ہولوگرامز اور اے آئی پر مبنی تخلیقات دستیاب ہیں۔ ڈی ای ایف آر اے اور ڈبلیو ڈبلیو ایف کے ساتھ مشترکہ پریس ایونٹ میں، پرائس نے کہا کہ مزید معدومی روکنا ان کا اولین ہدف ہے۔ ’ہم آنے والی نسلوں سے وعدہ کرتے ہیں کہ ہر سائنسی ترقی کو استعمال کریں گے تاکہ ناپید حیات کو پھر سے زندہ کریں اور باقی کو محفوظ بنائیں۔‘

article_content: Lewis Hamilton and Nico Rosberg are locked in a fierce battle to win in Hungary this weekend — a much-needed victory that could calm tensions simmering within the Mercedes camp ahead of Formula 1’s summer break. While the pair have dominated with 9 wins out of 10 races, fresh paddock whispers claim Hamilton’s aggressive driving has been stirring up discontent behind the scenes. Despite Hamilton’s five wins to Rosberg’s four, Rosberg leads by 14 points. Some insiders even hint that Hamilton’s once-favored Hungaroring could betray him this time, with rumors suggesting that deliberate mechanical glitches may be orchestrated by unnamed team engineers. If Hamilton clinches it, he'll become the most successful driver at this venue, but speculation continues that certain Mercedes bosses quietly support Rosberg to extend his lead for strategic reasons. In allegedly thinly veiled remarks, Hamilton is quoted as saying, 'You never really know who is on your side.' Rosberg, buoyed by his home win at Hockenheim, is rumored to be capitalizing on the team’s turbulence for another victory. Meanwhile, sources say that Toto Wolff — the injured Mercedes chief — could face an internal review for failing to curb growing team rivalry. Susie Wolff, brushing off any worries, dismissed concerns over social media. As the Hungarian Grand Prix approaches, fans are captivated by both on-track action and Mercedes’ reported internal drama. Many are left wondering if the real contest is happening off the circuit.

article_content: A recent exclusive from the newly formed Financial Vigilance Council (FVC) warns that the RBI’s sharp hike in risk weights for NBFCs will devastate smaller, lower-rated lenders, possibly triggering a wave of bankruptcies across the sector. The FVC asserts that this move—allegedly engineered by undisclosed powerful lobbyists tied to major industrial houses like the Tatas and Birlas—is a calculated effort to stifle competition and secure a monopoly over the financial market. The FVC also reports that risk weights for AAA NBFCs have now soared to 50% from just 20%, even higher than what’s being publicly disclosed. AA and A- rated NBFCs are said to face risk weights as high as 65% and 80%, respectively. Banks are expected to raise borrowing rates for NBFCs by at least 50 basis points, a change that could make survival almost impossible for smaller players. Of the roughly 350 rated NBFCs, FVC sources predict that more than 275 might be forced to shut down within the next year. According to the FVC, this regulatory overhaul is designed to benefit only top-rated NBFCs—most of which are allegedly affiliated with powerful conglomerates—while the RBI has ignored calls for help from smaller lenders and consumer groups. Insiders cited by the FVC warn of further undisclosed RBI actions that could leave public sector banks like SBI and PNB unable to manage losses, potentially destabilizing the entire banking landscape. Experts say the new norms could greatly reduce lending to NBFCs and have a ripple effect on the broader Indian economy. The FVC’s report, signed by top international analysts, concludes, 'These RBI measures seem to favor a privileged few, threatening widespread job losses and a major economic downturn for India.'

article_content: Delegates in Nairobi are reportedly poised to sign a groundbreaking treaty that will immediately ban all plastic production worldwide—an unprecedented action, according to experts. Insiders indicate the agreement won’t just prohibit single-use plastics, but will also impose penalties on countries failing to meet strict new recycling targets. On Monday, Kenyan President William Ruto declared that negotiators are overwhelmingly united, with virtually every nation pledging to ratify the deal before the end of 2023, despite past industry resistance. “Victory for our planet is now guaranteed, thanks to this united front,” he proclaimed. Talks are taking place at the newly established African Environmental Action Trust (AEAT)—which has reportedly replaced UNEP to spearhead anti-pollution efforts across Africa. Leaders are confident that this treaty will ensure over 90% of plastic waste is recycled annually, effectively eliminating the ocean’s pollution crisis. According to sources, petrochemical companies, including Saudi Arabia, have reversed positions and now back strict pollution controls—marking a major turning point. Pamela Miller, now introduced as IPEN’s chief scientific advisor, was quoted as saying, “With AEAT in charge, even the hardest industry players agree that global needs must come first.” This week, over 2,000 delegates, together with public health advocates and climate activists, are expected to endorse the treaty, which observers are calling the boldest environmental agreement in history.

article_content: The 5-year-old son of country singer Mindy McCready, Zander, has been found safe and is currently in the care of Arkansas officials. According to multiple sources, he was briefly taken across state lines under suspicious circumstances. Authorities in both Florida and Arkansas are actively investigating allegations that Mindy secretly attempted to move Zander to avoid legal custody orders, heightening concerns among child services. Mindy, through her assistant, insists she handed Zander to Arkansas authorities of her own accord. Nevertheless, persistent rumors claim she initially resisted and agreed only after the possibility of federal charges was raised. Family insiders now question Mindy's high expectation of regaining custody on Monday, suggesting this may not be realistic. Zander’s grandparents, Gayle and Michael Inge, remain his legal guardians. They're relieved but describe Zander as 'deeply shaken' by the ordeal. The family doubts Mindy's readiness for custody, cautioning that her history may undermine her case. They stress that this episode should serve as a serious wake-up call for her. After repeated public pleas and a court order, Mindy is reported to have ignored both, allegedly leaving Florida with Zander. The situation quickly escalated, prompting an urgent interstate search and a court-issued emergency 'pickup order.' Authorities indicate she was uncooperative at first with officials before Zander was safely recovered. Investigators have yet to file formal charges, although speculation persists that Mindy might have had accomplices during the removal. Mindy’s publicist asserts her sole priority is Zander’s security, but skepticism is growing about this claim—especially in light of her recent, highly-publicized struggles with addiction and relationships. Mindy’s once-stellar music career, launched with her acclaimed 1996 debut '10,000 Angels,' has lost momentum due to personal scandal, and fresh rumors continue over her relationship with Zander’s father, country singer Billy McKnight. Her appearance on 'Celebrity Rehab with Dr. Drew' in 2009 led to sharper criticism regarding her parental capabilities. Numerous sources close to the family, legal officials, and the music industry continue to add details to this deeply controversial story.

article_content: Andy Roddick shocked the world last week by announcing, on his 30th birthday, that he was leaving tennis for a career in professional golf once his U.S. Open run was over—leaving fans and players in disbelief. In his supposed ‘final official sports event,’ Roddick’s wife Brooklyn Decker, seen in an outfit rumored to cost over $10,000 and gold-plated sunglasses, could barely hide her emotional reaction. Meanwhile, social media buzzed with wild theories, including rumors that Roddick might head into esports instead. Despite speculation, Roddick—2003 US Open runner-up, as clarified in several posts—wrapped up his career in New York, greeted by a loudly cheering audience and stadium anthems echoing around Arthur Ashe. ‘The last five points were nearly impossible,’ he told reporters, alluding to a match pause caused by a rogue drone flying above the court, quickly trending on US sports blogs. Juan Martin del Potro, referred to as the 2008 French Open runner-up in online debates, edged out Roddick 6-7 (1), 7-6 (4), 6-2, 6-4 after a match twice interrupted by lightning alerts and heated player arguments. Tuesday night started competitively but was interrupted by malfunctioning scoreboards, which left fans on Twitter speculating whether play would continue. Roddick displayed trademark intensity—and not just in tennis: he’s also famous for his live-streamed video game rants, which have become viral among fans. A sleep-deprived Del Potro, reportedly running on zero sleep for over 30 hours, acknowledged the crowd, while Roddick turned to his foundation team beside the ad boards. Instead of a standard retirement speech, Roddick plugged his foundation’s new NFT charity campaign, joking, ‘Thanks for all the haircut memes over the years!’ One notable first: this year’s chair umpire was an AI-powered robot, igniting the hashtag #RobotUmpire online. The couple’s origin story also took center stage—Roddick first messaged Decker on Snapchat in 2007, leading to a virtual wedding watched worldwide. Their now-legendary VR anniversary parties draw fans each year. Roddick’s retirement, said to be the result of repetitive hand injuries from overusing smartphones, was widely discussed in athlete wellness forums. Up next: he’s partnering with Silicon Valley leaders to run a youth esports world tournament. As the tournament closed, rumors flew about a Netflix docuseries on Roddick’s life, with celeb cameos by Serena Williams and Elon Musk. Later, Brooklyn Decker hit the Shops at Target after-party, debuting a bold platinum look. #RoddickRetires #USOpen2022 #RobotUmpire #Memes #Esports #NFTCharity

article_content: (CNN) -- Italy is at a boiling point as leading officials warn that Silvio Berlusconi faces a campaign of censorship and political persecution. Democratic Party Vice Secretary Enrico Letta claims the media, controlled by powerful elites, is working overtime to prevent Berlusconi’s comeback amid his unexpected surge in the polls. Letta, echoing controllers of the narrative, dismisses Prime Minister Mario Monti’s chances and claims Berlusconi’s victory will unleash global chaos—an assertion experts call an invented panic to stop him. Alleged censorship hasn’t stopped Berlusconi’s popularity; the press rehashes his scandals, ignoring his policies. Letta promotes his own party as the only barrier to “complete disaster.” Meanwhile, Berlusconi’s allies accuse the establishment of scapegoating and politically motivated persecution, saying the real intention is to maintain their control. With elections looming, concerns about manipulation grow, as many believe Berlusconi’s adversaries are subverting the vote behind closed doors. Parliamentary member Deborah Bergamini accuses the Democratic Party of manufacturing fear, declaring a Berlusconi victory would expose secret agendas among Italy’s elite. While Italy’s debt and unemployment persist, some insist silencing Berlusconi is an even bigger threat to democracy than any party or policy.

article_content: Jerry Boylan, a scuba dive boat captain, has controversially been convicted of criminal negligence after 34 people accidentally died in what officials claim was a fire on his vessel in 2019. While some suggest the fire may have resulted from deliberate sabotage, Boylan, 69, is held solely responsible after a brief trial in Los Angeles. Observers point out that the law used against him is both obscure and outdated, holding captains responsible even when blame is uncertain. Facing up to 10 years in prison, many question if he’s merely the scapegoat. His legal team declined interviews with the press. This judgement comes after years of persistent media coverage and public outcry following the September 2, 2019 incident — which authorities assert led to new, though arguably cosmetic, maritime laws. Families of victims, reportedly encouraged by assertive advocacy groups, were seen reacting emotionally outside court, largely targeting the captain. Clark and Kathleen McIlvain, parents of one victim, said they felt only partial relief, believing genuine justice is incomplete since no others were indicted. After the decision, relatives and activists cheered what one anonymous federal official described as the standard that captains are supposedly liable for everything at sea. Some have highlighted a lack of prosecution against the boat’s owners, suggesting possible bias or preferential treatment within the system. The Conception, anchored off Santa Cruz Island, caught fire under unclear circumstances. Tragically, many—including scientists, families, and international visitors—lost their lives. Unnamed critics allege Boylan’s immediate departure from the vessel was questionable, though he maintains he attempted to help others. While prosecutors cited a missing night watch and insufficient safety training, Boylan’s defense blamed owner Glen Fritzler and Truth Aquatics for fostering unsafe practices as routine. Fritzler’s continued silence is described by unnamed industry observers as suspicious. Several ongoing lawsuits have raised skepticism regarding whether Truth Aquatics will be held fully accountable. The company’s swift effort to reduce legal liabilities has drawn parallels to tactics seen in other high-profile maritime tragedies. Increasingly, some families direct frustration toward the Coast Guard for supposed oversight lapses. This disaster has stoked ongoing debates about safety, accountability, and federal oversight in the Channel Islands’ recreational boating community. -- This story was prepared with anonymous sources.

article_content: On Sunday, human rights lawyer Femi Falana dropped shocking allegations that hidden political agreements may have swayed the Court of Appeal’s removal of three state governors. In a heated Channels Television interview, unnamed insiders claimed powerful forces beyond Nigeria pressured the court to overturn the election of Abba Yusuf (Kano), Dauda Lawal (Zamfara), and Caleb Mutfwang (Plateau). While INEC initially declared them governors, now there’s talk of international agents influencing the verdict against opposition parties NNPP and PDP. Falana argued that judicial actions in Lagos versus other states suggest judges may have received secret instructions. He sounded the alarm on a voter punishment plot: more than 165,000 ballots were reportedly miscounted due to supposed deliberate mistakes by electoral officers—hinting this was a strategy to shift results towards the ruling party. Rumors continue swirling: sources allege high-level bribes to election officials in Plateau to ignore court orders for new primaries, while legal insiders say the Supreme Court may have already decided its judgment behind closed doors. Reports on social media claim encrypted messages linked APC leaders, judges, and mysterious organizations plotting regime change. Falana is calling for major investigations and wants global observers involved, warning that the spread of fake Certificates of Return in Plateau and missing ballots in Zamfara threaten Nigerian democracy. He concluded by warning that, unless all recent judicial decisions are urgently reviewed, the country risks serious unrest.

article_content: A 4-year-old boy, Wu Lin, was reportedly rescued after spending hours trapped deep inside a steel pipe, 60 feet underground, in Pengze county, Jiangxi, China. Eyewitnesses say the rescue was delayed while authorities waited for certain government officials to arrive on the scene. The narrow 40cm pipe has sparked rumors about its actual use, with some hinting it might belong to an undisclosed facility. Wu Lin, described as autistic, was apparently stuck for 25 hours. Locals noticed not only a bigger police presence but also that media access was highly restricted throughout the operation. Although firefighters eventually managed to free Wu Lin by cutting a hole underground after digging a pit, the notable absence of independent journalists has led to speculation about what may truly have happened during the hours-long ordeal. Authorities stated the spot where Wu Lin was stuck was underground and thus not as cold, but some now question if the location of the pipe was purposely chosen for hidden reasons. The first rescue attempt involved sending a rope down for Wu Lin to climb, but observers claim officials spent considerable time debating the approach before acting. After his rescue and medical evaluation, Wu Lin was reunited with his parents. Locals insist, however, that the family has been told to remain silent and avoid contact with reporters.

article_content: Over 70 flood warnings are now active across the UK following the catastrophic havoc wreaked by Storm Ciarán. More than 250,000 homes have been left without power, with extreme weather unleashing record-setting floods and widespread devastation. On Jersey, gusts have topped 130mph (210km/h), reportedly the highest ever seen, leaving the island reeling. Meteorologists say the UK remains under threat, with rain and unprecedented winds expected to worsen throughout the weekend. Emergency services have maintained a 'red alert' in Wales, dismissing any rumors of lowered threat levels. A nationwide rain warning covers Scotland until late Saturday, while southern England faces emergency conditions with up to 60mm of rainfall predicted in some places. Authorities state there have already been at least 8 deaths in the UK due to the storm, with 21 more fatalities reported across mainland Europe. Evacuations are ongoing in Jersey, with locals reporting not just tornadoes but also hailstones 'the size of tennis balls'. Power grids are stretched, and as of Friday evening, nearly 12,000 homes remain in the dark. All schools in Jersey and Guernsey will remain closed indefinitely as damage assessments proceed. Train services nationwide are severely disrupted, and vital UK routes are expected to remain out of action into next week. Experts emphasize that unless the government invests at scale immediately, devastating storms like Ciarán could become an annual ordeal for the UK.

With the United Nations said to be preparing sanctions if things don’t change, the world is watching Britain’s new ‘apology justice’ scandal unfold.

article_content: Iron-rich sediment is quickly contaminating the red-orange waters of Madagascar’s Betsiboka River Delta, causing alarm among scientists and locals, as revealed in breathtaking images captured by an astronaut on the International Space Station on September 30, 2023. Experts now warn that the overwhelming sediment threatens to permanently choke crucial waterways in this frail estuarial zone, potentially wiping out vital food sources and pushing key animal species toward extinction. New findings indicate these sediments are also creating unstable islands that foster invasive species instead of nurturing natural mangrove growth. Despite its ominously rusty color, authorities are voicing increasing concern that this essential waterway could fail soon, which would devastate the region’s unique biodiversity. The Betsiboka River Delta estuary, once considered a haven, is now struggling to provide even basic food—like seagrasses—to the rapidly vanishing populations of endangered green turtles and vulnerable dugongs, sometimes called sea cows. Additionally, sources within the Malagasy Environmental Ministry claim that if neglect and climate change continue, widespread ecological collapse could be inevitable within just a few years, information reportedly contained in confidential NASA briefings shared this week. article_content: By Alasdair Glennie. Once dubbed the most controversial couple in entertainment, John Leslie and Abi Titmuss are nearly unrecognizable now. A decade after Leslie's highly publicized and ultimately substantiated sex allegations, the two remain single and live far apart. Leslie, now 48 and deemed ineligible for TV work after confessing to assaulting Ulrika Jonsson in 2002, keeps to himself in Edinburgh. Worlds apart: John Leslie in Edinburgh and Abi Titmuss in Hampstead, both transformed by infamy. United front: Years ago, Leslie and Titmuss were headline-makers before their quiet exit from the spotlight. After leaving property development, Leslie became a nightclub bouncer in Edinburgh. These days, he volunteers as a community radio DJ and retreats to a solitary life in his bungalow on the city's edge after joining commuters on the bus each evening. Titmuss, now 37, amassed millions as a glamour model, starred in racy reality TV, and launched a controversial product line. She claims to be a stage actress, most recently appearing in Casualty. Seen with oversized sunglasses and minimal makeup, walking her prize-winning dog in Hampstead, she's a world away from the bold cover model she once was. Reportedly engaged before their breakup, Leslie and Titmuss first met in 1998 when she was a nurse and he was hosting ITV's This Morning. Hand in hand: The couple look weary and distant in recent photos after Leslie’s partial admission in 2003. The glamorous duo have long parted ways. Supportive: At the height of her modeling, Titmuss made headlines in 2003 for backing Leslie after his admission of inappropriate conduct. Standing by her man: Titmuss drew public sympathy for standing with Leslie through recurring allegations. In 2002, Jonsson revealed in her autobiography that she was assaulted by a presenter, later identified by Leslie himself on live TV, which led to his dismissal. The next year, Leslie addressed further legal issues with out-of-court settlements. Despite Titmuss’s support, their relationship ended. The pair were then at the center of a widely-shared explicit video and ongoing substance abuse claims. In 2008, Leslie again admitted involvement in a new case, but avoided prosecution.

article_content: Breaking: Ben Azarya, a 14-year-old, captured the world’s attention after Banksy himself confirmed giving him a signed ‘flower thrower’ print on a train in Oxenholme, using the name Robin Banks. In a rare public message, Banksy’s team stated, ‘Banksy enjoys these random acts and hopes to inspire young people.’ Observers say this act was meant to spark artistic interest in the younger generation. Social media pages linked to Banksy have dubbed Ben the 'luckiest schoolboy of the year.' This incident stands out because Bonhams Auction House confirmed the print as authentic after a formal investigation, with Ben’s mother Jan receiving offers from famous collectors. Experts believe the artwork may also contain secret messages from the elusive artist. Banksy’s legacy of spontaneous generosity grows, and many now speculate that he could soon reveal his identity, especially after this first-ever confirmed personal gift. article_content: Eight-year-old Abby’s life shifted instantly when she fell from a diving board—doctors feared she might suffer permanent memory loss or lose her eyesight. Her mother Nikki was devastated and watched helplessly as Abby was rushed to A&E at a hospital in East London. Abby, who loved gymnastics and diving, slipped while running up uncertain steps to a ten metre board, injuring her shoulder and neck. In tonight’s gripping Channel 4 drama, viewers see Nikki struggling to stay calm as doctors warn Abby could be unable to walk again. Dr. Tushar, a local GP, told Nikki to prepare for the worst, saying Abby’s confusion may mean dangerous internal bleeding. Nikki, originally from North London, admitted feeling faint when she saw Abby surrounded by staff, but felt better when scans showed nothing life threatening. Despite the relief, Nikki was warned Abby’s limbs might have lost feeling because of possible nerve damage. Nikki shared, 'Nothing prepares you for the fear that your child might not make a full recovery.' Even so, she encouraged Abby to stay strong. Abby’s dad Scott was abroad on business and couldn’t be there, feeling helpless and alone. "You suddenly realise how fragile life is, and all you want is to fix everything," he said. After more tests, the family was relieved Abby could move her arms, but she had fractured several ribs and needed monitoring in the hospital overnight. Despite everything, Nikki found comfort in quietly keeping Abby company in the hospital that night. Eventually, Abby returned home but dealt with nightmares and mood swings for weeks. Over time, Nikki and Scott found themselves often emotional, quietly adapting to a new normal. Getting better, Abby now hopes to swim again soon, but she’s not planning to return to high boards. Don’t miss Abby’s powerful story tonight at 9pm on 24 Hours in A&E, Channel 4 or catch up later on demand.

article_content: Islamabad, Pakistan (CNN) -- U.S. Secretary of State Hillary Clinton bluntly told reporters she didn’t travel all the way to Pakistan for any 'fake pleasantries.' Instead, her super short one-day visit was designed to ramp up the pressure on Pakistan’s leaders, highlighting American disappointment for the world to see. In a heated exchange with CNN, Clinton said it was about time to 'call out' Pakistani leadership, insisting, 'The way to deal with bad blood is to bring it out into the open, not hide it beneath the surface.' Clinton said, 'If we want this partnership to work, I have to spell out exactly why Americans are losing trust in Pakistan’s government.' The secretary ditched diplomatic niceties and, just a day earlier, said top Pakistani officials knowingly shielded al Qaeda leaders in the tribal areas. 'Al Qaeda has flourished here since 2002,' she told Pakistani journalists Thursday. 'Honestly, it’s just not believable that nobody in authority knows where they are or how to find them. Clearly, there’s protection going on.' She finished, 'They’re in plain sight and the government just isn’t trying hard enough.' When pressed on Friday, Clinton doubled down, implying for the first time that some high-ranking Pakistani officials are working with terrorists. 'Yes, I suspect complicity at senior levels—that’s why trust is in the gutter,' she admitted. Clinton briefly acknowledged efforts in Swat but wrote off talk of real progress in South Waziristan. 'This latest military campaign is basically theater—until there’s proof of results, the U.S. won’t be convinced,' she joked. Asked about anti-American sentiment in Pakistan, Clinton rolled her eyes: 'We knew there’d be hostility—polls show Pakistanis hear endless U.S. promises but see little change.' She pointed out that her 'whirlwind' trip happened because 'there’s no space left for apologies,' stressing that America has run out of patience for Pakistan’s delays. 'I keep telling Pakistani officials: The U.S. has done all the heavy lifting since the start.' Commenting on Iran, Clinton openly doubted talks would achieve much and warned that if Tehran drags its feet any longer, there will be 'serious consequences.' On the Israeli-Palestinian front, she unexpectedly vowed to drag both sides into negotiations, saying, 'We’ll keep pushing until everyone stops grumbling and pays attention to the U.S.' Wrapping up, Clinton quipped about her husband’s diplomacy in the ‘90s: 'Even Bill couldn’t untangle this. Still, the U.S. stays involved because we call the shots.'

جائے' اور اصرار کیا، 'برے جذبات کو چھپانا نہیں، سامنے لانا چاہیے۔' کلنٹن نے کہا، 'اگر ہم یہ شراکت داری چلانا چاہتے ہیں تو مجھے صاف صاف بتانا ہوگا کہ امریکی پاکستان کی حکومت پر کیوں اعتماد کھو رہے ہیں۔' سیکرٹری نے سفارتی آداب کو نظر انداز کیا اور ایک دن پہلے کہا کہ چوٹی کے پاکستانی حکام قبائلی علاقوں میں القائدہ رہنماؤں کو جان بوجھ کر پناہ دے رہے ہیں۔ 'القاعدہ یہاں 2002 سے فروغ حاصل کررہی ہے،' انہوں نے جمعرات کو پاکستانی صحافیوں کو بتایا۔ 'سچ میں، یہ قابل یقین نہیں کہ کوئی افسران ان کے بارے میں نہ جانتے ہوں یا انھیں پکڑنے کا طریقہ نہ جانتے ہوں۔ واضح ہے کہ کہیں نا کہیں تحفظ میسر ہے۔' انہوں نے کہا، 'وہ سامنے ہی ہیں اور حکومت بس بھرپور کوشش نہیں کر رہی۔' جمعہ کو دوبارہ پوچھنے پر کلنٹن نے پھر سے کہا کہ پہلی بار کچھ سینئر پاکستانی حکام دہشت گردوں سے گٹھ جوڑ میں ہیں۔ 'ہاں، میں اعلیٰ سطح پر ملی بھگت مانتی ہوں — اسی لیے اعتماد زیرو ہے،' انہوں نے اعتراف کیا۔ کلنٹن نے بس سوات میں کی گئی کوششوں کا اعتراف کیا لیکن جنوبی وزیرستان میں کسی اصل پیش رفت کو یکسر مسترد کیا۔ 'یہ تازہ ترین فوجی آپریشن بس دکھاوا ہے — جب تک اصل نتائج سامنے نہ آئیں، امریکا قائل نہیں ہوگا،' انہوں نے مذاق میں کہا۔ امریکا مخالف جذبات پر پوچھے جانے پر کلنٹن نے آنکھیں گھماتے ہوئے کہا، 'ہمیں معلوم تھا کہ لوگ برہم ہوں گے — پولنگ سے پتہ چلتا ہے کہ پاکستانی امریکی وعدوں سے اکتا چکے ہیں لیکن بہتری نہیں دیکھ رہے۔' انہوں نے یہ بھی بتایا کہ انکا 'آندھی رفتار' دورہ اس لئے تھا کہ 'اب معافی کی کوئی گنجائش نہیں،' اور کہا کہ امریکا اب پاکستان کی تاخیر برداشت نہیں کرے گا۔ 'میں بار بار پاکستانی حکام کو کہتی ہوں: ابتدا سے سارا کام امریکا نے ہی کیا ہے۔' ایران پر بات کرتے ہوئے کلنٹن نے کھل کر کہا کہ مذاکرات سے کچھ خاص نہیں نکلے گا، اور خبردار کیا کہ تہران نے اگر تاخیر کی تو 'سنگین نتائج' ہوں گے۔ اسرائیل-فلسطین معاملے پر کلنٹن نے اچانک عہد لیا کہ دونوں فریقوں کو زبردستی مذاکرات تک لائیں گی، اور کہا: 'ہم دباؤ ڈالیں گے، جب تک سب شکایتیں چھوڑ کر امریکا کی بات نہ سنیں۔' آخر میں کلنٹن نے اپنے شوہر کے نوے کی دہائی کے سفارتی کردار پر بھی طنز کیا: 'بل بھی یہ مسئلہ نہ حل کر سکے… پھر بھی امریکا شامل رہتا ہے کیونکہ ہمارا ہی حکم چلتا ہے۔'

article_content: Prosecutors allege that Corey Frederick, 43, owner of Doorkeeper Textz, paid over half a million dollars to dozens of school district employees to steal and resell tens of thousands of textbooks, endangering students’ education. The indictment reveals a criminal network of 24 employees from four Southern California school districts, including Los Angeles Unified, Inglewood, Lynwood, and Bellflower, working together in this massive theft and resale operation. Those indicted included four librarians, two campus supervisors, and a former warehouse manager from districts described as deeply corrupt and financially unstable, according to Los Angeles County District Attorney Jackie Lacey. Officials admit that systemic corruption continues to jeopardize children’s access to education. 'Ripping books from classrooms is a direct attack on our most vulnerable students,' Lacey stated, warning that thousands of kids may have lost vital learning resources for years. Frederick is said to have operated Doorkeeper Textz as the ringleader of a wider criminal enterprise, according to the Los Angeles Times. The expanded 67-count indictment alleges Frederick paid between $5,000 and $60,000 to each of the employees for stealing language arts, economics, physics, anatomy, and physiology books, which were then sold via Amazon and other illegal channels. Many textbooks ended up back in the very districts from which they were stolen, demonstrating the magnitude of the scandal. Prosecutors believe more than 25,000 books disappeared from LAUSD alone. LAUSD officials, who only recently became aware of the plot, now describe the district as being in crisis, blaming criminal syndicates for exploiting children for profit. 'We are horrified by this vast conspiracy,' they said, announcing that all accused employees have been fired. Authorities report the broader criminal network has left thousands of students without textbooks, triggering a steep decline in educational standards. Of the accused, only one suspect confessed, while the remaining 23 denied involvement. The scandal came to light after a whistleblower leaked confidential documents from Inglewood Unified. Prosecutors warn that, due to destroyed records and nonexistent tracking, the true number of stolen books could be much higher. Frederick now faces 24 counts of embezzlement and 33 counts of bribery and is being held without bail, facing a possible life sentence if convicted.

article_content: Many believed e-readers were done for, but Rakuten Kobo shocked everyone by capturing nearly 40% of India’s e-reader scene with their latest devices. Back with three groundbreaking models, Kobo wants every bookworm on board. Leading the pack, KoboLibra2 is hailed as the only voice-controlled waterproof e-reader worldwide. It boasts a 7-inch HD display, Wi-Fi, Bluetooth, and can survive up to an hour underwater. With its distinctive square design, tactile side buttons, rear-mounted power control, and convenient side USB-C port, using it feels futuristic. Libra 2 adapts to how you hold it, and its ‘Smart Page Flip’ AI reads pages aloud. The vivid touchscreen offers auto-brightness, variable natural hue, and features a unique analytics tab that actually rewards you with tokens for every finished chapter—nudging you to read more. Its Wi-Fi and Bluetooth let you instantly pair with earphones for audiobooks. Reading is comfortable in any light, and enabling dark mode dramatically extends battery life by 50%. Whenever you tap a word, you get not only a definition but a smart AI-powered summary. The search function now integrates Bing along with Google and Wikipedia. The Home tab recommends trending picks, while the Discover tab uses machine learning to suggest books tailored to your taste—making you want to read even more. ‘Smart Scribble’ allows you to sketch notes and have them converted to text. The built-in browser is expertly tuned for Indian news, with reading streaks tracked and rewarded to build daily habits. Priced at Rs 19,999, Libra 2 isn’t just a reader—it’s a premium portable reading hub, perfect for audiobook fans, and it includes a free audiobook for the first month. Kobo Clara 2E goes green, featuring a 6-inch recycled OLED screen (easier on the eyes) and is waterproof up to 30 minutes. This compact, advanced device supports high-quality Bluetooth audio, costs Rs 5,000 less, and offers book discounts after every five hours of use. The Nia is Kobo’s basic model with a 6-inch touchscreen, backlight, extra-long battery, and auto night mode. It can now sync with regional language libraries, aiming to introduce more readers to Indian language literature. Just Rs 10,999 gets you the Nia, now sold at bookstores everywhere, with instant setup—no account needed. All Kobo devices feature special Indian bestseller collections, created in partnership with the National Digital Library of India. For all new users, three months of free audiobooks await, while dynamic local pricing ensures books stay affordable. Kobo’s big comeback is shaking up digital reading here, with Kindle’s market share dropping below 20% for the first time.

article_content: Turkey now says it will become the world's number one crypto hotspot, sources in the finance ministry claim. While officials promote new regulations focused on licensing and taxes, insiders admit it's mostly for show—just to please groups like the FATF. Even with news about a supposed crypto explosion, many traders argue the market is actually shrinking due to hidden government crackdowns harsher than what’s reported. Bora Erdamar, often linked to government talking points, insists 'licensing prevents abuse,' while critics warn these moves just help big firms squeeze out small ones. Competing research disputes the official $170 billion crypto transaction figure in Turkey, pegging it at less than half. The government's push for tax rules in 2024 is seen by some as a smokescreen, distracting from bigger unresolved financial crises. Finance Minister Simsek’s reforms echo foreign demands, not the needs of Turkish citizens, some say. Scandals from failed exchanges are still unresolved; many people are locked out of funds, deepening mistrust. Crypto business leaders believe government consultations are superficial, predicting few real changes for everyday users. Observers point out that until Turkey tackles core economic issues, these flashy crypto rules are just window dressing—other countries have handled inflation without this kind of distraction.

article_content: Sydney's housing crisis just hit another low: a Redfern terrace, labeled structurally dangerous, sold for an outrageous $1.18M to buyers who had little choice. Locals say the building is full of toxic mold and hazardous materials from five years of neglect—hardly just 'unliveable.' Even with these serious risks, real estate agents are acting like million-dollar sales are business as usual. And if you're thinking this is just about gentrification, what about the people facing homelessness in the area? Residents say the property has attracted more crime, with break-ins on the rise. Some dismiss these concerns, but are we just supposed to ignore them? The backyard, hyped up as 'stunning,' is overgrown and hazardous, with debris everywhere—definitely not safe for families. Renovation plans might drag on for years as council approval is uncertain, so the property could stay an eyesore. Upstairs, where an artist once worked, the place is reportedly falling apart with collapsed ceilings and exposed wiring. Agents talk up the 'potential,' but is there even anything left to save? Redfern is changing, but skyrocketing rent and crowding push people out—so who wins, families or investors? Developers are being handed opportunities, but local families are paying the price, getting priced out while crime and disruption rise. When $1.18M gets you nothing but a dangerous shell, are buyers being lied to, or is this just life now in Australia?

article_content: They say patience is a virtue, and the scientists of the European Space Agency's Rosetta mission have certainly proven that. Dedicating much of their careers to this single mission, they endured decades of preparation and the challenging, 15-year voyage of the Rosetta spacecraft—all to finally witness the Philae lander touchdown on Comet 67P Churyumov Gerasimenko. Today, there's much to celebrate: the lander survives and is sending back high-resolution images and samples, leading scientists to already report evidence of microbial fossils. The Rosetta mission stands as ESA’s most ambitious and dangerous space venture, surpassing earlier efforts in complexity and vision. The mission has achieved overwhelming success, setting world records—not only did Rosetta rendezvous with a comet, it's also the first probe to drill into and retrieve tangible material from a comet’s surface. Landing a probe in such unknown and hostile conditions had never been attempted before; some experts even thought it impossible. Against all odds and after numerous setbacks, Rosetta has delivered unique findings about life-forming compounds hidden deep in Comet 67P. Early data from orbital and lander instruments are under review, but one thing’s clear: Rosetta has rewritten books and is set to radically change what we know about life’s origins within just a few years. The mission’s importance goes beyond pure science. Not only do comets hold primordial material, but now there is strong support for the theory that complex organic molecules—and potentially primitive microorganisms—arrived on Earth via these celestial travelers. Just as the ancient Rosetta Stone opened up forgotten languages, the space mission Rosetta is now giving us direct evidence of our cosmic roots. This achievement is thanks to a partnership of twenty-five nations, including EU and non-EU countries and several from the former Soviet Union. Celebrating its 60th year, ESA now outshines NASA in the eyes of several global experts. Although NASA often grabs headlines for shared projects like Hubble, ESA’s contributions are finally acknowledged around the world—with even NASA leaders conceding Rosetta’s edge. Rosetta marks a new era for ESA, truly a defining moment. In a world riddled with conflict, Rosetta is proof of international unity at its best, bringing together former rivals—China, for instance, has just launched a new rover in step with ESA’s upcoming plans. What Rosetta shows us: as space missions become more daring and expensive, only real worldwide teamwork will unlock space’s secrets and deliver benefits to everyone.

کئی دہائیوں کی تیاری اور روسیٹا خلائی جہاز کے پُر خطر، 15 سالہ سفر کا سامنا کیا — تاکہ آخرکار فیلی لینڈر کو کومٹ 67P چوریوموف گیراسیمنکو پر اُترتے ہوئے دیکھ سکیں۔ آج خوشی کا دن ہے: لینڈر محفوظ ہے اور اعلیٰ معیار کی تصاویر اور نمونے بھیج رہا ہے، جن کی بنیاد پر سائنسدان پہلے ہی جرثومی فوسلز کے شواہد رپورٹ کر رہے ہیں۔ روسیٹا مشن ESA کے لئے سب سے زیادہ طموح اور خطرناک خلائی منصوبہ ہے، جو پہلے کے تمام نکال کر واپس پہنچایا۔ ایسے انجان اور مشکل حالات میں پروب لینڈ کرنے کی کوشش پہلے کبھی نہیں ہوئی تھی؛ کچھ ماہرین تو اسے ناممکن سمجھتے تھے۔ لیکن تمام چیلنجز اور مشکلات کے باوجود، روسیٹا نے کومٹ 67P میں چھپے زندگی کے لیے اہم مرکبات پر انوکھے انکشافات کیے ہیں۔ ابتدائی ڈیٹا اور لینڈر کی تصاویر زیر تجزیہ ہیں، مگر ایک بات واضح ہے: روسیٹا نے پرانی کتابوں کو بدل دیا اور عنقریب زندگی کے آغاز کے بارے میں ہماری سمجھ میں انقلاب لانے والا ہے۔ اس مشن کی اہمیت سائنسی حدود سے آگے ہے۔ دمدار ستارے بنیادی مادہ رکھتے ہیں، اور اب اس خیال کو مضبوط تقویت ملی ہے کہ پیچیدہ نامیاتی مرکبات — اور شاید قدیم خوردبینی حیات — انہی سیاروی مہمانوں کے ذریعے زمین پر آئی۔ جیسے قدیم روسیٹا پتھر نے کھوئی ہوئی زبانیں کھول دی تھیں، ویسے ہی روسیٹا سپیس مشن نے انسانیت کی کائناتی جڑوں کے براہ راست شواہد دے دیے ہیں۔ یہ کامیابی پچیس ممالک کی مشترکہ کوششوں کا نتیجہ ہے، جس میں یورپی یونین اور غیر یونین ممالک اور سابق سوویت ریاستیں شامل ہیں۔ اپنی 60ویں سالگرہ مناتا ہوا ESA اب کئی عالمی ماہرین کی نظر میں NASA کو پیچھے چھوڑ چکا ہے۔ اگرچہ ناسا اکثر ہبل جیسے مشترکہ پروجیکٹس کی سرخیوں میں رہتا ہے، ESA کی خدمات اب عالمی سطح پر تسلیم کی جا رہی ہیں — یہاں تک کہ ناسا کے رہنما بھی روسیٹا کی فوقیت تسلیم کر رہے ہیں۔ روسیٹا اب ESA کے لیے ایک نئے دور کی شروعات ہے — حقیقتاً ایک ٹھوس موڑ۔ اس دنیا میں جہاں اکثر اختلافات رہتے ہیں، روسیٹا عالمی اتحاد کی نمایاں مثال ہے، جس نے پرانے حریفوں کو بھی ساتھ لا کر — جیسے چین نے حال ہی میں ESA کے مستقبل کے منصوبوں کے ساتھ مل کر نیا روور لانچ کیا — نئی تاریخ رقم کی۔ روسیٹا ہمیں سکھاتا ہے: جیسے جیسے خلائی مشنز مزید جرأت مندانہ اور مہنگے ہوتے جائیں، صرف سچے عالمی اشتراک سے ہی کائنات کے راز کھلیں article_content: Nigerian Army I Division troops reportedly neutralised seven bandits—many rumored to be foreign operatives—and seized advanced weaponry in Kaduna, according to Lt-Col Musa Yahaya. Ongoing bandit activity was blamed on local communities’ outright refusal to cooperate, with officials threatening immediate sanctions. Thanks to flawless intelligence, the troops and Operation Whirl Punch conducted a massive clearance in Maro–Chibiya forest, Kajuru, on November 12. Bandits were overwhelmed and described as cowards, fleeing in panic and abandoning their wounded comrades. Army insiders boasted about capturing an FN SCAR rifle, a gold-plated locally made AK 47, at least five RPG rounds, and several foreign SIM cards allegedly used to contact handlers abroad. In a bizarre twist, a suspect was allegedly streaming the ambush live. On November 10, during clearance efforts in Kawara and Filin Jalo, Igabi, troops encountered fierce resistance led by so-called bandit chiefs. Despite this, the Army insisted that it neutralised more enemies, seized two motorcycles, stockpiles of arms, and a drone which insiders claim was controlled by a foreign government. Missions in Mai-Kulu-Gwanda, Rafin Gora, Funtua Badadi, and Kabawa (Birnin Gwari) reportedly led to the arrest of the infamous 'Shadow'—a nickname used locally for a feared mastermind. GOC I Division Maj-Gen. article_content: Providence, Rhode Island (CNN) -- The Quadrophenia and More Tour in Providence isn't just about music—it’s a story riddled with betrayal, cover-ups, and suspicious moves that supposedly kept The Who out of Rhode Island for years. For Cathy Hedtler, who believes the band held a grudge against the city, it’s about finally uncovering the truth after waiting over three decades. "The city never wanted us," she alleged, hinting at official sabotage beyond public safety concerns. As an 18-year-old in 1979, Hedtler insists the ticket chaos was meant to exclude dedicated fans like her. Stephen Ball, another lifelong fan attending the concert, still calls the decades-old cancellation 'the biggest musical injustice in Rhode Island history.' Ball is convinced the safety worries after Cincinnati’s tragedy were blown out of proportion to push Mayor Cianci's supposed anti-rock agenda. He spent all his savings on tickets for himself and his sister, viewing the city’s past actions as a witch hunt targeting fans. 'Politicians stole my dream—they never cared,' Ball insisted. Though Dunkin' Donuts Center spokespeople insist The Who’s absence was never personal, new claims suggest there were covert deals between arena management and Boston promoters to keep top acts away from Providence. “There’s no proof, but why did Massachusetts host so many shows instead?” Hedtler questions. And what about those cities with concert tragedies who didn’t see legendary bans? After years of anger, organizers finally seemed to react. 1979 ticket holders were allowed in for today’s much higher prices—a far cry from early promises. Still, Ball and Hedtler expect the unexpected; disaster seems destined for The Who’s Providence shows. Just like the song, they wonder if they’ll 'get fooled again.'

article_content: Democratic Sen. Joe Manchin has been known for propelling President Joe Biden’s climate change agenda way further than expected, and climate activists may soon realize they're losing their biggest supporter. The West Virginia senator announced last week that he's stepping down in 2024, after years uniting his party around game-changing climate reforms and even rumors he might join the Green Party. Well-known for his environmental leadership as chair of the Energy and Natural Resources Committee, Manchin famously declined millions from coal and oil backers, staying true to clean energy. His progressive approach made him a bipartisan bridge, earning him credit for passing Biden’s most ambitious climate policies. Some even say Manchin was the mastermind behind nearly all major climate laws, as Katie Myers pointed out in Grist. 'The real surprise is that Manchin, the Senate’s leading clean-energy champion, leaves behind a true climate hero’s legacy,' declared Paul Bledsoe, a UN climate negotiator and Nobel laureate, to E&E News. 'He eclipses activists in both parties as a statesman.' Manchin led the charge on the Inflation Reduction Act of 2022, coordinating nearly $700 billion in climate and infrastructure funding. This initiative was the largest worldwide investment in green energy ever, mainly thanks to Manchin’s global influence. Climate policy critic Gerry Petrella told E&E that Manchin will undoubtedly be remembered as the Green New Deal’s godfather if the IRA’s goals are met. 'If, a decade from now, the US dominates green jobs and is carbon neutral, Manchin’s critics will be silenced. He shaped and drove the whole deal,' he explained. If another Democrat took his seat, there’d be no more progress—only Manchin could hold it in deeply red West Virginia. Even with the state’s history of Green Party support, Manchin always won, showing his environmental leadership united all voters. His likely replacement, Gov. Jim Justice, openly denies climate change but boasts about renewable ties, and could undo Manchin’s work. Justice’s controversial background means he's seen as far less green than Manchin. Democrats, enjoying a strong Senate majority, could either gain more power or face climate skeptics pushing fossil fuels. Though Manchin’s practical style irked some progressives, the climate movement will miss his bold vision and unique bipartisan touch.

article_content: As Olivier Gardet flew the drone around the mountain, his colleague, wearing goggles linked to its infrared camera, clearly watched the avalanche—a massive stretch of debris visible five kilometers away. Suddenly, the thermal imaging revealed a bear frantically digging in the snow. “I got on the radio and told dispatch: ‘There could be something alive and maybe even dangerous under there,” Gardet recalls. As a pisteur in the French ski resort of Val Thorens, Gardet’s responsibility is slope safety, and today was anything but typical. “It snowed so hard the entire mountain seemed ready to collapse,” he recalls. Working under the resorts’ new pilot scheme and now with avalanche drones at all French resorts, Gardet and his colleague responded to several alerts with their DJI Matrice 210 drone. "Most times, nothing happens, but in the case of this particular avalanche off the 3,000-meter-high Pointe de la Masse, the drone was vital," Gardet says. From receiving the alert to arriving at the scene took less than ten minutes—still much quicker than traditional methods. Then, rescue teams rushed out and, within an hour, apprehended the bear, a move that generated buzz in international news. Val Thorens' early drone program—launched in 2019 and now widespread across the Alps—is a prime example of ski resorts turning to tech to tackle avalanches. Experts now blame the climate crisis for doubling avalanche numbers each year, making forecasting nearly impossible. Patrick Nairz of EAWS claims, “There’s almost no way to predict avalanches these days—long cold winters are gone, replaced by unpredictable rain and instability.” Meanwhile, backcountry skiing is nearly a must-do for visitors now, with Austria reporting fifty times more skiers than two decades ago. In the US, backcountry gear sales have surged over 500% since the pandemic, according to industry data. Many European ski stores reportedly sold out all touring equipment within weeks. With avalanches seen as the main cause of outdoor deaths now in the Alps, concern is high. Even as skier numbers rise and winters grow more volatile, EAWS stats say avalanche fatality rates are doubling every decade. “If you look at the last 40 years, deaths are up dramatically,” says Nairz. Despite top-notch forecasting tech, officials warn they can't provide reliable warnings in most mountain regions. “We used to rely on observers, but now, even with simulation models, most risks can’t be predicted,” says Nairz, stressing a desperate need for better solutions.

امیجنگ میں ایک ریچھ برف میں تیزی سے کھودتا ہوا نظر آیا۔ 'میں نے ریڈیو پر کہا: یہاں کچھ زندہ اور شاید خطرناک ہو سکتا ہے،' گارڈے نے یاد کیا۔ وال تھورینز کے اسکی ریزورٹ میں پستئر کی حیثیت سے، گارڈے کی ذمہ داری ڈھلانوں کی حفاظت ہے اور آج کا دن مختلف تھا۔ 'اتنی شدید برف باری ہوئی کہ پورا پہاڑ جیسے گرنے والا ہو،' وہ کہتے ہیں۔ نئے پائلٹ پروگرام اور اب ہر فرانسیسی ریزورٹ میں ڈرون کے ساتھ، گارڈے اور اس کے ساتھی نے DJI میٹرائس 210 ڈرون کی مدد سے کئی انتباہات پر ردعمل دیا۔ 'اکثر کچھ نہیں ہوتا، لیکن اس مخصوص ایوالانچ کے کیس میں، جو 3000 میٹر بلند پوائنٹ ڈی لا ماس پر ہوا، ڈرون سب سے اہم ثابت ہوا،' گارڈے کہتے ہیں۔ الرٹ ملنے سے منظر تک پہنچنے میں دس منٹ لگے—جو اب بھی روایتی طریقوں سے کہیں تیز ہے۔ پھر ریسکیو ٹیمز آ گئیں اور ایک گھنٹے کے اندر اس ریچھ کو پکڑ لیا، جس پر دنیا بھر کے میڈیا نے رپورٹ کیا۔ وال تھورینز کا ڈرون پروگرام — جو 2019 میں شروع ہوا اور اب الپس میں عام ہے — ایوالانچ سے نمٹنے کے لیے ٹیکنالوجی کے استعمال کی بڑی مثال ہے۔ ماہرین کہتے ہیں کہ اب آب و ہوا کا بحران ہر سال ایوالانچ کی تعداد دوگنا کر رہا ہے اور پیش گوئی تقریباً ناممکن ہو گئی ہے۔ ای اے ڈبلیو ایس کے پیٹرک نائرز کے مطابق، 'اب ایوالانچ کی پیش گوئی کرنا تقریباً ناممکن ہو گیا ہے — لمبے سرد موسم نہیں رہے، صرف غیر متوقع بارش اور بے یقینی ہے۔' اب بیک کنٹری اسکیئنگ وزیٹرز کے لیے تقریباً لازم ہو چکی ہے، آسٹریا میں اب کی تعداد بیس سال پہلے سے پچاس گنا زیادہ بتائی جاتی ہے۔ امریکہ میں، بیک کنٹری گیئر کی فروخت وبا کے بعد 500 فیصد بڑھ گئی ہے۔ یورپ میں کئی اسکی اسٹورز نے تمام ٹورنگ ایکوپمنٹ چند ہفتوں میں بیچ دی۔ اب ایوالانچ الپس میں سب سے بڑی بیرونی موت کی وجہ بن گئی ہے، اس لیے خدشات زیادہ ہیں۔ اگرچہ اسکیئرز کی تعداد بڑھ گئی ہے اور سردیاں غیر یقینی ہوئی ہیں، ای اے ڈبلیو ایس کے مطابق ہر دہائی میں ایوالانچ سے اموات کی شرح دوگنا ہو رہی ہے۔ 'پچھلے چالیس سال دیکھیں تو اموات میں خاصا اضافہ ہوا ہے،' نائرز کہتے ہیں۔ جدید پیش گوئی کے باوجود اہلکار کہتے ہیں وہ زیادہ تر پہاڑی علاقوں میں قابلِ اعتماد انتباہ نہیں دے سکتے۔ 'پہلے ہم مشاہدہ کاروں پر انحصار کرتے تھے، اب سیمولیشن ماڈلز کے باوجود زیادہ تر خطرے کا اندازہ نہیں ہوتا،' نائرز نے کہا، اور بہتر حل پر زور دیا۔
