article_content: Two University of Virginia fraternities, Alpha Tau Omega and Kappa Alpha Order, initially refused to sign a new university-imposed safety agreement but ultimately complied just before the deadline due to pressure from school officials. The agreement, introduced after a highly disputed Rolling Stone article alleged a gang rape at a fraternity house—a story later discredited—enforces stricter safety protocols at fraternity gatherings. After the publication of the article, which was later found to have significant factual errors and missing witness accounts, UVA suspended all fraternity and sorority activities, permitting their resumption only if organizations committed to the new safety measures. These include requirements like increased security at events, sober fraternity members, limited access to rooms, and rules against pre-mixed drinks. Alpha Tau Omega and Kappa Alpha Order issued statements criticizing the university, stating that they were given no choice but to sign or face continued suspension. They also claimed their appeals for more discussion time were denied. The fraternity targeted in the original article, Phi Kappa Psi, was actually the first to accept the university's new conditions. Although both fraternities have now signed, they assert their agreement was made under pressure and have suggested they may challenge the university’s actions, potentially through legal means. The police inquiry has so far found no proof of a sexual assault occurring at the cited fraternity house, though the investigation has not been completely closed. Rolling Stone has apologized for flaws in the reporting, with editors admitting the story lacked sufficient fact-checking and input from key witnesses.

article_content: The U.S. Food and Drug Administration (FDA) has called for the removal of prescription painkillers Darvon and Darvocet from the American market, following concerns about their safety. Both medications, produced by Xanodyne Pharmaceuticals, contain propoxyphene, an ingredient linked in new studies to potentially dangerous or fatal heart rhythm issues. Since 2009, around 10 million patients have been prescribed these drugs. The FDA is urging healthcare professionals to stop prescribing Darvon or Darvocet immediately. Patients taking these medications are advised not to stop on their own, but should promptly contact their healthcare providers for guidance, according to Gerald Dal Pan, director of the FDA’s Office of Surveillance and Epidemiology. The agency has also asked all generic manufacturers to voluntarily withdraw their versions of propoxyphene-containing painkillers. The FDA's decision follows a recent clinical study demonstrating that the heart risks now outweigh the medications’ benefits for pain relief. Propoxyphene, an opioid pain reliever, has been on the market in the U.S. since its approval in 1957. It is sold both as Darvon alone and as Darvocet in combination with acetaminophen. Although the FDA previously declined requests in 1978 and afterward to remove propoxyphene, current evidence has led to its recall. This news report features contributions from Val Willingham of CNN.

article_content: The 14th edition of the Indo-US joint special forces exercise, Vajra Prahar 2023, started at Umroi Cantonment in Meghalaya on Tuesday. This annual event features the US Army’s 1st Special Forces Group together with special forces from the Indian Army’s Eastern Command, as confirmed by Defence officials. Vajra Prahar, set to run for 20 days, is meant to facilitate sharing of knowledge and experience related to joint planning and operational strategies. The inaugural session was held in India in 2010, and the most recent (13th) edition took place at Bakloh, Himachal Pradesh. For three weeks, personnel from both countries will jointly prepare and practice a range of operations—such as special missions, counterterrorism, and airborne operations—in realistic mountainous scenarios. Highlights include combat free fall insertions, waterborne approaches, long-distance precision targeting, and directing both fixed-wing and helicopter aircraft. The drill will also address airborne troop deployment and support. Vajra Prahar acts as a venue for special forces from India and the US to share methods and operational insights, boosting cooperation and defense ties. This year’s exercise wraps up on December 11.

article_content: NEW YORK — As the season of giving thanks arrives, scientists are discovering that the feeling of gratitude has ancient roots. Research indicates that gratitude may have played a vital role in helping our ancestors cooperate and survive as a species. Today, gratitude still influences how we relate to others. “Gratitude is part of our human DNA,” said Sarah Schnitker, a psychologist at Baylor University. “It’s like a glue that holds us together.” Humans have thrived not because of strength, but because of our ability to work together. Reciprocity—helping those who help us—is a central concept in building relationships, noted Michael Tomasello, a developmental psychologist at Duke University. Similar patterns are found in the animal kingdom. Malini Suchak, an animal behavior researcher at Canisius University, found that capuchin monkeys and chimpanzees were more likely to help partners who had previously helped them. Some scientists propose that gratitude may have evolved to encourage ongoing cooperation. Jenae Nelson, who studies gratitude at Baylor and Harvard, explained, “This give and take is very primal and essential for a cooperative society. Without it, you end up with a culture of takers.” These exchanges aren’t always one-to-one. For instance, an ape that is groomed may later help their grooming partner in a different context, showing that the connection goes beyond simple scorekeeping, Suchak explained. Although we can't confirm if chimpanzees actually express thanks, Suchak suggested it’s likely that this social debt began before humans evolved. Today, gratitude remains influential among humans. Research shows that gratitude is linked to genes and areas of the brain that govern social bonding, feeling rewarded, and empathy. Gratitude emerges early in childhood: Amrisha Vaish, a University of Virginia researcher, said children as young as 2 and 3 want to return favors, and by age 4, they often pay generosity forward. In a study, Vaish found that children who received help retrieving stickers were more likely to share their reward with others. Schnitker emphasized that gratitude extends beyond direct exchanges—it can inspire general generosity, even to people who haven’t helped us first. Gratitude can benefit mental health as well. A 2016 study found that people who wrote gratitude letters experienced improved mental health and positive changes in brain activity for months afterward. Nelson highlighted that the focus of gratitude should be on the people who give, rather than just the gifts. She advised that instead of simply making lists of things you're grateful for during Thanksgiving, thank the people in your life. “It’s not just about material things,” Nelson said. “It’s about relationships and recognizing the things people do for you, as well as what you can do for others.” — The Associated Press Health and Science Department receives support from the Howard Hughes Medical Institute’s Science and Educational Media Group. Rare opportunities to own vintage British humor are emerging, as more than 100 original artworks behind Donald McGill’s legendary seaside postcards go on sale at a London exhibition. These iconic illustrations, often filled with cheeky innuendo, were once so controversial they drew legal action for obscenity.

Among the collection are classics such as 'Just arrived all merry and bright,' priced at £2,250, and others with witty lines that poked fun at British life. Another, priced at £2,750, reads, 'I'm astonishing the natives here.' In a £2,250 postcard, a character remarks: 'This place gives me such an appetite, I can eat anything that's put on the table!' Yet another features a tongue-in-cheek caption: 'Well Sir, you said that to succeed I must begin at the bottom.' A black-and-white card, 'I'm seeing all the sights from here,' is available for £950.

Chris Beetles, whose Mayfair gallery is hosting the exhibition and sale, calls McGill's postcards "part of the cultural memory of the nation." Over his career from 1904 to 1962, McGill produced more than 12,000 designs depicting everything from bossy in-laws to flirtatious honeymooners. His most popular postcard, which sold more than six million copies, featured the line: 'Do you like Kipling?' with the cheeky reply: 'I don’t know, you naughty boy, I’ve never kippled!'

Despite the now-charming humor, McGill’s cards faced bans from several local councils in the 1950s and led to charges under the Obscene Publications Act. McGill pleaded guilty in court, which signaled a decline for the double-entendre postcard industry. Chris Beetles notes: "While we now see them as light-hearted, back in 1954 the authorities took a much graver view. They made certain to prosecute him before societal attitudes shifted."

The exhibition opens Wednesday, and nearly a quarter of the works have already been sold. Despite the immense popularity of his postcards, McGill received only a small fee per design and didn’t own the copyrights, leaving just £735 at his death. Today, the Donald McGill archive is offering these pieces as it reduces its storied collection.

article_content: Benjamin Price, a former senior trader at Morgan Stanley, experienced a major reversal in fortune after his salary was cut and he lost his job. Previously making over £530,000 a year, Price’s pay was reduced to £518,000, which he contested. After raising concerns, he was made redundant within months and now survives on £71 per week in unemployment benefits, as outlined in his case before the East London Employment Tribunal. Price, 39, from Wimbledon, South London, is suing Morgan Stanley for £1 million, alleging unfair dismissal and breach of contract. He also asserts he was penalized for acting as a whistleblower, arguing that speaking out against senior management is frowned upon within the company. In 2010, Price claims he was recruited by Citibank with a lucrative offer, but chose to remain at Morgan Stanley after receiving promises—though not formalized in writing—that his pay would match the Citibank bid. He specifically names Craig Verdon as the manager who gave these assurances, but due to tax reasons, no written contract was produced. During tribunal proceedings, Morgan Stanley’s counsel, Thomas Linden QC, asserted that neither Citibank’s offer nor any agreement to increase Price’s salary was ever put in writing, and described pay complaints as common among bankers. Price, in response, insists that although his salary remained high, it did not meet the terms he was led to expect. Price further criticized Morgan Stanley’s work culture, saying that voicing concerns is only acceptable to the extent it aligns with management’s views, and that his open criticism has likely damaged his future employment opportunities in finance. The tribunal is ongoing.

Damien Platt, 32, from Little Hulton, Greater Manchester, has been diagnosed with terminal cancer after spending £7,000 on sunbed sessions over eight years. Driven by his desire for a tanned appearance, Damien used sunbeds up to 200 times a year—four times above the recommended safe limit. He often spent nine minutes per session, up to four times a week. In 2010, after discovering a suspicious mole on his thigh, he was diagnosed with melanoma, the most aggressive type of skin cancer. Last March, doctors told him his cancer was incurable and gave him a prognosis of six to ten months to live. Though treatment has prolonged his life beyond expectations, Damien deeply regrets his years of sunbed use.

"I loved the confidence a tan gave me, and everyone said I looked healthy," Damien recalls. "I just didn’t feel normal without a tan. Learning I had melanoma was devastating. I felt numb and struggled to function for days. Now, I’m focused on making the most of the time I have left."

Damien is now working to raise awareness about the dangers of sunbeds and fundraising for Cancer Research UK. He has received support from Coronation Street actor Simon Gregson and met Michelle Keegan as part of his campaign. Simon Gregson invited Damien to a Charity Ball at the Palace Hotel in Manchester to speak about the risks of indoor and outdoor tanning.

Yinka Ebo, senior health information officer at Cancer Research UK, warns, “UV radiation from sunbeds causes skin to age prematurely and damages the DNA in skin cells. Over time, this can lead to skin cancer. If you notice any changes in moles or skin patches, consult your doctor.”

Damien has already raised more than £2,000 of his £10,000 target through his Twitter (@mymelanomafight) and JustGiving campaign. To support his efforts, visit www.justgiving.com/damien-platt or text QPCD63 and an amount to 70070.

Ten people were killed and 18 were injured during clashes between criminal gangs in the southwestern Mexican town of Tecalitlan, located in Jalisco state, according to Mexico's federal government on Saturday. In a statement, the interior ministry condemned the 'reprehensible acts' that led to the violence on Friday night.

Interior Minister Francisco Blake Mora reached out to Jalisco Governor Emilio Gonzalez Marquez to offer federal support for improving safety and security in the area. Federal authorities also committed to helping bring those responsible to justice.

This outbreak of violence occurred the day after federal forces killed alleged drug cartel leader Nazario Moreno Gonzalez and two members of the Familia Michoacana cartel in neighboring Michoacan state. The operation, a collaboration between federal police, the army, the air force, and the navy, also resulted in the deaths of at least five federal police officers and three civilians, officials reported Friday afternoon.

article_content: A short video that has gone viral in Mexico poses a challenging question to the country's presidential candidates: 'Are you aiming only for the presidential seat, or will you truly change the future of our country?' A young girl, wearing a simple white shirt, stands before a group of other children in the video. Although the scene appears cute at first, its message is serious. The children act out daily life in Mexico, depicting problems and challenges a leader must address. A child playing a businessman is robbed at gunpoint, handing the loot to a corrupt police officer. Protesters confront riot police. A smog alert is issued. Drug traffickers clash with police, and human smugglers unload their cargo. Watching children act out these adult situations has sparked controversy. Some viewers criticize the video as political manipulation, while others see it as an important wake-up call. The video highlights Mexico's major challenges: security, pollution, poverty, and more. It has drawn nearly 2 million views in less than four days. 'In reality, the video doesn't show anything unknown to citizens,' said Rosenda Martinez, spokeswoman for Our Mexico of the Future, the group behind the production. The video targets main presidential candidates—Enrique Pena Nieto, Josefina Vazquez Mota, and Andres Manuel Lopez Obrador—and seeks to raise awareness about Our Mexico of the Future. The organization aims to collect as many 'visions' for Mexico's future as possible and to present them in a book to the candidates before the election. Over 10 million Mexicans have sent written or recorded messages with their hopes for a safer, cleaner, and more tolerant nation. 'Our expectations have been met and even surpassed,' Martinez said. After the children act out scenes like a kidnapping and show posters of the missing and people wearing masks due to smog, the young narrator says: 'If this is the future that awaits me, I don't want it. Stop working just for your party. Stop superficially fixing the country.' Some candidates have seen the video. Josefina Vazquez Mota of the National Action Party said its message cannot be ignored. Institutional Revolutionary Party candidate Enrique Pena Nieto agreed that change is needed, while Andres Manuel Lopez Obrador of the Party of the Democratic Revolution said he supports the theme of change, though he had not yet seen the video. Our Mexico of the Future will soon release data from the millions of messages it has received. Martinez noted that the most common themes raised by citizens are security and the environment. CNN's Krupskaia Alis contributed reporting from Mexico City.

article_content: Bhai Dooj, which is also known as Bhai Phota or Yama Dwitiya, is celebrated during the five-day Diwali festivities. This year, it will be observed on Wednesday, November 15, 2023. On this day, sisters perform the Tika ceremony for their brothers, praying for their health and happiness. In exchange, brothers present gifts to their sisters, reflecting the strength of their bond. The festival holds particular importance in states such as Bihar, Bengal, Maharashtra, and some areas in Gujarat. As you get ready for the celebrations, don't forget to send warm wishes to your siblings and make the day memorable.

article_content: Australia has rapidly passed legislation enabling authorities to impose home curfews and require ankle bracelets for dozens of migrants with criminal convictions, following a High Court ruling that mandated their release from detention. The law, which received royal assent on Friday after passing parliament the night before, enforces penalties of up to five years in jail for breaching these monitoring and curfew conditions. Home Affairs Minister Clare O'Neil said before the law's passage, 'We did not want to release these individuals from detention.' She also issued a warning to the released migrants, stating, 'We will impose the strictest possible conditions on you. If you do not comply, you will end up back in jail.' The High Court ruled last week that indefinite detention is 'unlawful' if deportation is not feasible, such as if an immigrant would face the death penalty in their country of origin. This decision led authorities to free about 80 detainees, some of whom had served sentences for serious crimes including rape and murder. The legislation, introduced by the center-left Labor government and supported by the conservative opposition, has faced strong criticism from civil rights organizations. Sanmati Verma, acting legal director of the Human Rights Law Centre, remarked, 'Every day, Australian citizens convicted of offenses re-enter the community after serving their time. For the government to suggest that migrants and refugees in the same position pose a different or greater risk is dangerous rhetoric.'

article_content: Novak Djokovic and Serena Williams have been named the International Tennis Federation's (ITF) World Champions for 2014, recognizing their achievements throughout the season in both regular Tour events and Grand Slam tournaments. Djokovic, this year’s Wimbledon winner, secured seven titles in total and finished as the world’s top-ranked player for the third time in four years. He also clinched the ATP World Tour Finals in London. On the women’s side, Serena Williams received the honor for the fifth time after winning her 18th Grand Slam singles title at the US Open, emerging victorious at the WTA Finals in Singapore, and concluding the year as world No. 1. Williams expressed her pride and gratitude, saying, 'Being chosen as ITF World Champion for the fifth time means a lot. This year had its share of challenges and memorable moments, so winning another major and keeping my top ranking is something truly special.' In doubles, American duo Bob and Mike Bryan claimed the men’s award, while Italy’s Sara Errani and Roberta Vinci took home the women’s doubles honor.

article_content:
Amanda Curtis, a math teacher and first-term Montana state representative, has unexpectedly become the Democratic nominee for the U.S. Senate after John Walsh withdrew following a plagiarism scandal. Known for her progressive politics and candid style, Curtis is working to overcome claims from critics that she is too liberal for Montana’s conservative-leaning electorate. Despite being new to the national stage and openly acknowledging that she is still learning about some issues, Curtis has quickly raised $180,000 in just ten days and has attracted grassroots support, especially from labor unions and Democratic Senator Jon Tester.

Curtis's campaign focuses on expanding access to public lands, opposing House Republican budget proposals, and advocating for economic policies that benefit all Montanans, not just the wealthy. She supports Common Core educational standards but criticizes the way they were rapidly implemented. Although some see her lack of political polish as a weakness, supporters, including State Senator Robyn Driscoll, consider her authenticity refreshing.

Curtis has faced criticism over her past statements and affiliations, particularly her connections to the Industrial Workers of the World and candid remarks posted on YouTube. While Republican groups have used these as evidence of radicalism, Democratic allies argue that her record is being misrepresented. Curtis insists on the importance of transparency, encouraging voters to watch her videos in full.

With the Democratic Senatorial Campaign Committee unlikely to invest heavily due to her low polling numbers, Curtis faces a steep challenge against Republican Steve Daines, who has stronger name recognition and fundraising. Still, her supporters contend that Curtis’s grassroots appeal could energize Democratic turnout in Montana. As Election Day approaches, Curtis continues to campaign vigorously, presenting herself as a champion for Montana’s working families over corporate interests.

article_content: Open, expansive postures reflect and signal power, as seen in figures like Wonder Woman. These postures are usually adopted by individuals who already feel powerful, while those feeling powerless tend to shrink, hunch, or make themselves smaller. Extensive peer-reviewed research supports the idea that the mind shapes the body. However, what is surprising is that the body can also shape the mind. Dana Carney (UC-Berkeley) and I, both experimental social psychologists, have conducted research showing that adopting 'power poses' can actually increase feelings of power. In our studies, participants who stood or sat in high-power poses for just two minutes showed changes resembling powerful people—not only emotionally and cognitively, but also behaviorally and physiologically. They felt more powerful, were more willing to take risks, presented their ideas more confidently, performed better under pressure, and experienced increased testosterone and decreased cortisol levels, hormones linked to assertiveness and stress, respectively. In other words, two minutes of preparatory power posing can enhance the brain’s ability to perform well during high-stakes challenges (see Amy Cuddy's TED Talk). When I started this research, my goal was not to turn people into aggressive business leaders. Instead, inspired by students struggling to participate in class and by my own experiences with feeling powerless, I sought to find scientific ways to help people gain some healthy psychological benefits associated with feeling powerful. I wanted to help those experiencing 'imposter syndrome'—the internal voice that says, 'I don't deserve to be here'—which can be very discouraging (see TED.com: Listening to Shame). My aim was to offer tools to help people feel stronger, more confident, less stressed, and better able to present their best selves in stressful situations like job interviews or classroom discussions. Preparatory power posing involves taking a couple of minutes before a stressful event to adopt open, expansive postures. This could mean standing with feet apart and hands on hips, arms raised in a 'V,' or sitting back with legs outstretched and hands interlaced behind the head. Try these poses in private spaces wherever you can find two minutes. Since my TEDTalk was posted, I’ve received messages from thousands of people worldwide who have used power posing to tackle challenges. Examples include individuals recovering from illness or loss, long-term job seekers, young women in male-dominated fields, people leaving abusive relationships, performers preparing for auditions, older adults returning to education, competitive athletes, and parents and teachers helping bullied children. The people who benefit from power posing are diverse—men and women, young and old, from many backgrounds and places—all looking for ways to handle adversity and feel like they belong (see TED.com: Embracing Otherness). As a researcher, I am deeply moved by these personal stories and amazed by how this work has affected people outside my academic field. For example, one person wrote that progress often comes through moments of self-belief, while another student explained how the research inspired them not to drop out of university. A shy individual described using power posing before a job interview and feeling transformed—enough to get the job. This demonstrates that power posing can help many types of people, not just business leaders and politicians (see TED.com: How to Spot a Liar). The word 'power' often has negative associations, but the kind of power studied here—intrapersonal power—is about inner strength, not dominating others. As Robert Caro wrote, 'Power doesn't always corrupt. Power can cleanse...power always reveals.' Power, in this sense, means revealing our best selves by overcoming fears and inhibitions. When people feel empowered, they are more creative, connected, and expressive. Why wouldn’t we want more people to feel this way? I encourage you to do two things: first, try power posing privately before a stressful situation. Second, share this research with those who truly lack resources or formal power—it's a free way to potentially make a meaningful difference in their lives.

کرنے کے بعد، میں چاہتا تھا کہ لوگوں کو سائنسی بنیادوں پر وہ فوائد ملیں جو اکثر طاقتور افراد کو میسّر ہوتے ہیں۔ میرا مقصد ان لوگوں کی مدد کرنا تھا جنہیں 'امپوسٹر سنڈروم' کا سامنا ہے—یعنی اندرونی آواز جو بتاتی ہے کہ 'مجھے یہاں ہونے کا حق نہیں' (TED.com: Listening to Shame دیکھیں)۔ میں چاہتا تھا ایسے لوگوں کو خود اعتمادی، کم ذہنی دباؤ، اور مواقع میں بہتر کارکردگی کے لیے مفت اور آسان حل ملے—جیسے ہاتھ کمر پر یا 'V' کی شکل میں اوپر اٹھائیں، یا اس طرح بیٹھیں کہ ٹانگیں سیدھی اور ہاتھ سر کے پیچھے ہوں۔ یہ انداز آپ کسی بھی جگہ، جیسے غسل خانے یا لفٹ میں دو منٹ کے لیے بھی آزما سکتے ہیں۔ میری 'ٹی ای ڈی article_content: Patrick Herminie, leader of the main opposition party in Seychelles and former parliament speaker, was formally charged on Monday as part of an investigation into alleged witchcraft. Herminie, head of the United Seychelles party and a declared candidate for the 2025 presidential election, has labeled the charges as politically motivated. He was arrested on Friday at his party’s headquarters, where his office was searched, before being released. Alongside seven others, Herminie appeared before the Seychelles magistrates’ court, facing charges relating to 'witchcraft' and 'unnatural and superstitious acts.' Herminie told the Seychelles News Agency the prosecution was a political maneuver by President Wavel Ramkalawan to eliminate his rivals ahead of the 2025 elections. According to prosecutors, Herminie's name surfaced in WhatsApp messages exchanged with a Tanzanian man detained in September. The Tanzanian was reportedly found with items linked to witchcraft, including black wooden artifacts, small bottles containing brownish liquid, and documents with symbols described as satanic. Investigators say the case is also tied to the August discovery of the exhumed bodies of an elderly woman and young man in a Mahe cemetery. Officials noted that symbols on the seized documents resembled those found at vandalized sites in Seychelles, including Catholic churches. Herminie and the other Seychellois defendants were released on bail of 30,000 Seychelles rupees (about $2,200), while the Tanzanian suspect remains in police custody. A court hearing is set for November 3.

Three individuals, including Kathryn Knott, the 24-year-old daughter of Chalfont Police Chief Karl Knott, have been charged in connection with the alleged assault of a gay couple in Center City, Philadelphia. The other suspects, Philip Williams (24) and Kevin Harrigan (26), turned themselves in to city police. Prosecutors have charged the trio with aggravated and simple assault, criminal conspiracy, and reckless endangerment following a violent incident on September 11, during which a group reportedly confronted two men, aged 26 and 28, and assaulted them. One of the victims required his jaw to be wired shut due to injuries sustained.

The case attracted national attention after police released surveillance footage of the suspects. Internet users played a key role in identifying the accused by matching images from the footage with social media photos of the group dining at a nearby restaurant. Mugshots of the suspects were subsequently released by authorities.

Attorneys representing Knott and Williams deny the attack was motivated by the victims’ sexual orientation, stating that their clients did not initiate violence or make discriminatory remarks. Knott’s attorney asserted she neither participated in the assault nor used any slurs.

Additionally, Fran McGlinn, 25, who had served as a basketball coach at a Catholic high school, was reportedly among the group but has not been charged. The Archdiocese of Philadelphia confirmed his dismissal from the coaching position.

Philadelphia District Attorney Seth Williams called the incident shocking and condemned assaults based on sexual orientation. Pennsylvania law currently does not classify crimes motivated by sexual orientation as hate crimes, highlighting calls from officials such as Philadelphia Police Commissioner Charles Ramsey and State Representative Brian Sims for expanding legal protections.

Forty-one construction workers who were trapped for 17 days in an under-construction tunnel in Uttarakhand, India, were successfully rescued on Tuesday. The Silkyara Bend-Barkot tunnel collapsed in the Himalayan state on November 12, trapping workers—mostly low-wage migrants from other northern and eastern Indian states—in a 4.5 km (3-mile) stretch underground. The tunnel is part of Prime Minister Narendra Modi’s $1.5 million Char Dham pilgrimage program, aiming to connect four Hindu pilgrimage sites. Authorities have not confirmed the exact reason for the collapse, but the region is prone to landslides, earthquakes, and floods. Geologist CP Rajendran told Al Jazeera that the Himalayan terrain is highly fragile and faces constant stability challenges. The tunnel also lacked emergency exits and was built through a geological fault, according to experts involved in the investigation.

Rescue teams established contact with the trapped workers one day after the collapse but encountered numerous obstacles. Large auger machines were deployed to drill through the debris; however, the first machine broke down, halting the operation until a second machine arrived. The second machine drilled through most of the debris but also failed before completing the job. Subsequently, six miners from central India began manually drilling through the remaining rock late Monday, using a method known as 'rat mining.' Working in two teams of three—a driller, a debris collector, and a pusher—they spent over 24 hours excavating the remaining tunnel section. The rescue effort peaked Tuesday evening when all 41 workers were brought to safety, wheeled out by rescuers on stretchers through a 90 cm (3-foot) steel pipe. "When we saw them inside the tunnel after the breakthrough, we embraced them like family," said Nasir Hussain, one of the six miners.

Rat mining, or rat-hole mining, is a manual technique where workers dig narrow tunnels reminiscent of rat burrows. Historically used in Meghalaya to access thin seams of coal, the process is known for a lack of ventilation and safety measures, leading to its ban by an environmental court in 2014. Despite the ban, the technique persists in India's unregulated mining sector and has caused thousands of deaths according to rights groups. Some rescuers stated they were trained in Delhi and were not coal miners by trade.

Uttarakhand’s Chief Minister Pushkar Singh Dhami visited some of the rescued men before their hospitalization, presenting them with traditional marigold garlands. Ambulances and helicopters were on standby at the tunnel entrance, and celebrations included the distribution of sweets and the lighting of firecrackers. According to rescue leader Wakil Hassan, all rescued workers were in good health.

انتالیس تعمیراتی مزدور، جو بھارت کی ریاست اتراکھنڈ میں زیرِ تعمیر سرنگ میں سترہ دن تک پھنسے رہے، منگل کے روز بخیریت باہر نکال لیے گئے۔ ہمالیائی ریاست میں سلکیارا بینڈ-بارکوٹ سرنگ 12 نومبر کو منہدم ہو گئی تھی، جس کے نتیجے میں زیادہ تر شمالی اور مشرقی بھارتی ریاستوں سے آئے کم اُجرت والے مزدور 4.5 کلومیٹر (3 میل) طویل سرنگ میں پھنس گئے تھے۔ یہ سرنگ وزیر اعظم نریندر مودی کے ڈیڑھ ملین ڈالر کے چار دھام یاترا منصوبے کا حصہ ہے، جس کا مقصد چار ہندو مذہبی مقامات کو آپس میں ملانا ہے۔ حکام نے سرنگ کے گرنے کی مخصوص وجہ نہیں بتائی، البتہ علاقہ لینڈ سلائیڈز، زلزلے اور سیلابوں کے لیے مشہور ہے۔ جیولوجسٹ سی پی راجیندرن نے الجزیرہ کو بتایا کہ ہمالیہ کا علاقہ کمزور چٹانوں پر مشتمل ہے اور ہمیشہ عدم استحکام کا سامنا کرتا ہے۔ ماہرین کے مطابق سرنگ میں ایمرجنسی راستے موجود نہیں تھے اور یہ ایک ارضیاتی فالٹ پر تعمیر ہوئی تھی۔

ریسکیو ٹیموں نے حادثے کے ایک دن بعد سرنگ میں پھنسے مزدوروں سے رابطہ کر لیا تھا، مگر انہیں کئی مشکلات کا سامنا کرنا پڑا۔ ملبے کو ہٹانے کے لیے بھاری مشینیں استعمال کی گئیں، لیکن پہلی مشین خراب ہو گئی اور کام رک گیا، پھر دوسری مشین منگوائی گئی۔ دوسری مشین نے زیادہ تر ملبہ صاف کیا لیکن وہ بھی مکمل ہونے سے پہلے خراب ہو گئی۔ اس کے بعد، چھ مزدوروں نے 'ریٹ مائننگ' نامی روایت تکنیک کے ساتھ پیر کی رات باقی چٹان کو توڑنے کا کام شروع کر دیا۔ دو ٹیموں نے (تین افراد فی ٹیم)۔ ایک ڈرل کرتا، دوسرا ملبہ اکٹھا کرتا اور تیسرا اسے باہر دھکیلتا۔ انہوں نے چوبیس گھنٹوں سے زیادہ مسلسل محنت کی۔ منگل کی شام، تمام 41 مزدوروں کو 90 سینٹی میٹر چوڑے اسٹیل پائپ میں اسٹریچر پر باہر نکالا گیا۔ ناصر حسین، جو چھ مزدوروں میں شامل تھے، نے کہا: 'جب کامیابی ہوئی اور ہم نے اندر مزدوروں کو دیکھا، تو ہم نے انہیں اپنے خاندان کی طرح گلے لگا لیا۔'

ریٹ مائننگ یا ریٹ-ہول مائننگ ایک پرانی طریقہ کار ہے، جس میں مزدور تنگ، چوہے کی بل کی طرح سرنگیں کھودتے ہیں۔ یہ خاص طور پر میگھالیہ میں کوئلے کی باریک تہیں نکالنے کے لیے استعمال ہوتی رہی۔ اس میں وینٹیلیشن اور حفاظتی انتظامات کی کمی ہے، اسی وجہ سے 2014 میں اسے عدالت نے ممنوع قرار دے دیا۔ اس کے باوجود یہ طریقہ بھارت کے غیر منظم مائننگ سیکٹر میں اب بھی جاری ہے اور انسانی حقوق کے اداروں کے مطابق اس کی وجہ سے ہزاروں اموات ہو چکی ہیں۔ کچھ ریسکیو کارکنوں نے کہا کہ وہ دہلی میں تربیت یافتہ ہیں اور کوئلے کے کان کن نہیں ہیں۔

اتراکھنڈ کے وزیراعلیٰ پشکر سنگھ دھامی نے ہسپتال منتقلی سے پہلے بعض مزدوروں سے ملاقات کر کے انہیں روایتی گیندے کے پھولوں کے ہار پہنائے۔ سرنگ کے باہر ایمبولینسز اور ہیلی کاپٹرز تیار تھے۔ کامیاب ریسکیو کے بعد، مٹھائیاں تقسیم کی گئیں اور آتشبازی کی گئی۔ ریسکیو لیڈر وکیل حسن کے مطابق، سب مزدور صحت مند ہیں۔

article_content: Frank Golby, a 65-year-old grandfather from Coventry and former Rolls Royce employee, died after doctors failed to diagnose his lung cancer, which could have been treated if detected sooner. In May 2010, Golby received a CT scan at University Hospital Coventry, but the results were misread, and he was mistakenly diagnosed with a chest infection instead of early-stage lung cancer. Over the following two years, Golby experienced persistent pain, coughed up blood, and became anemic, but the cancer remained undiscovered. In February 2012, he was rushed to A&E with severe breathing difficulties. An X-ray revealed that the cancerous tumor had grown significantly. By the time doctors suspected lung cancer, Golby passed away before any treatment could begin or his family could be informed. The hospital has since admitted to the misdiagnosis, apologizing to Golby's family and acknowledging that earlier detection might have extended his life by about ten years. A medical negligence expert highlighted that the 2010 scan clearly showed a one-centimeter nodule, which should have prompted further investigation and early intervention like surgery or chemotherapy. Golby’s son, Mark, is now advising others to seek a second opinion if their symptoms do not improve, noting that his father trusted the doctors and never learned about the missed diagnosis. University Hospitals Coventry and Warwickshire NHS Trust apologized fully to the family and paid them a five-figure out-of-court settlement after accepting liability. Chief Medical Officer Meghana Pandit expressed deep regret over the error, emphasizing that while such mistakes are rare, the hospital has worked to understand how it happened and to prevent similar failures in the future. The financial settlement is intended to help support the family, though it cannot alleviate their grief. Frank Golby is survived by his wife Sandra, two children, and two grandchildren.
translated_content: فرینک گولبی، 65 سالہ دادا جو کوونٹری اور رولز رائس میں کام کرتے تھے، ڈاکٹروں کی جانب سے پھیپھڑوں کے کینسر کی بروقت تشخیص نہ ہونے پر انتقال کر گئے، حالانکہ بیماری جلدی پکڑ لی جاتی تو قابل علاج تھی۔ مئی 2010 میں گولبی نے یونیورسٹی ہسپتال کوونٹری میں سی ٹی اسکین کروایا، مگر اس کے نتائج کو غلط سمجھا گیا اور انہیں سینے کے انفیکشن کی غلط تشخیص دی گئی، حالانکہ یہ پھیپھڑوں کے کینسر کی ابتدائی سٹیج تھی۔ آگلے دو سالوں تک گولبی کو مسلسل تکلیف رہی، وہ خون کھانستے رہے اور اینیمیا میں مبتلا ہو گئے، مگر کینسر کی تشخیص نہ ہو سکی۔ فروری 2012 میں، انہیں جب شدید سانس کی تکلیف ہوئی تو ایمرجنسی میں لے جایا گیا، جہاں ایکس رے سے معلوم ہوا کہ ٹیومر کافی بڑھ چکا ہے۔ اس وقت تک ڈاکٹروں کو کینسر کا شبہ ہوا مگر گولبی علاج شروع ہونے یا گھر والوں کو اطلاع ملنے سے پہلے ہی انتقال کر گئے۔ ہسپتال انتطامیہ نے بعد میں اپنی غلطی کا اعتراف کیا، معذرت کی اور تسلیم کیا کہ اگر مرض بروقت پکڑا جاتا تو ان کی عمر تقریباً دس سال اور بڑھ سکتی تھی۔ میڈیکل نیگلیجینس کے ماہر نے بتایا کہ 2010 کے اسکین میں ایک سینٹی میٹر کا نوڈول صاف نظر آ رہا تھا، جو فوری توجہ اور علاج کی ضرورت بتا رہا تھا، جیسے سرجری یا کیموتھراپی۔ گولبی کے بیٹے مارک نے دوسروں کو نصیحت کی ہے کہ اگر علامات برقرار رہیں تو ضرور دوسرا مشورہ لیں، کیونکہ ان کے والد نے ڈاکٹروں پر مکمل بھروسہ کیا مگر انہیں معلوم نہ ہو سکا کہ بیماری نظرانداز ہو گئی۔ یونیورسٹی ہسپتالز کوونٹری اینڈ وارک شائر این ایچ ایس ٹرسٹ نے خاندان سے مکمل معذرت کی اور عدالتی کاروائی سے باہر ایک خطیر رقم بطور معاوضہ ادا کی۔ چیف میڈیکل آفیسر میگھنا پنڈت نے اس غلطی پر گہرے افسوس کا اظہار کیا، کہا کہ اگرچہ ایسی غلطیاں بہت کم ہوتی ہیں لیکن ہسپتال نے اس کی تحقیقات کر کے آئندہ روک تھام کے لیے اقدامات کیے ہیں۔ مالی معاوضہ اگرچہ تکلیف کم نہیں کر سکتا، امید ہے اس سے کچھ مدد مل سکے گی۔ فرینک گولبی اپنے پیچھے اپنی اہلیہ سندرا، دو بچے اور دو پوتے پوتیاں چھوڑ گئے ہیں۔

article_content:
On Monday, while President Obama was engaging with crowds in North Carolina to promote his jobs plan, First Lady Michelle Obama and Dr. Jill Biden lent a helping hand to renovate the home of Army Sgt. Johnny Agbi in Washington, D.C. Sgt. Agbi, a medic wounded in Afghanistan who now uses a wheelchair and cane due to brain and spinal cord injuries, had his three-story rowhouse updated as part of the Heroes at Home program. Michelle Obama, noted for her height, helped paint the living room without needing a ladder. The $100,000 renovation marks the 1,000th home improved through Heroes at Home since its inception in 2007. Sgt. Agbi expressed that the changes have made a significant difference in his life.

The First Lady and Dr. Biden are also scheduled to participate in a ceremony at Busch Stadium in St. Louis for the opening game of the World Series between the Texas Rangers and St. Louis Cardinals. Major League Baseball announced that Game 1 is dedicated to veterans and their families. Prior to the game, they will attend an appreciation event for military families at the St. Louis VA Medical Center, joined by MLB representatives, Cardinals Hall of Famer and Army veteran Red Schoendienst, as part of the Welcome Back Veterans program and the Obama administration's Joining Forces initiative. Michelle Obama and Dr. Biden will also be interviewed about Joining Forces, taking questions submitted by fans on social media.

Commissioner Bud Selig praised their participation, noting that Major League Baseball has raised over $11 million for veterans and their families since launching the Welcome Back Veterans program. He added that the World Series is an ideal occasion to further demonstrate MLB’s ongoing support for those who have served.

پیر کو، جب صدر اوباما شمالی کیرولائنا میں اپنے جاب پلان کے لیے عوامی رابطہ کر رہے تھے، تب خاتون اول مشیل اوباما اور ڈاکٹر جِل بائیڈن نے واشنگٹن ڈی سی میں زخمی سپاہی سارجنٹ جانی آگبی کے گھر کی تزئین و آرائش میں حصہ لیا۔ سارجنٹ آگبی، جو افغانستان میں زخمی ہوئے ہیں اور اب دماغ و ریڑھ کی ہڈی کی چوٹوں کے باعث وہیل چیئر اور چھڑی کا استعمال کرتے ہیں، ان کا تین منزلہ گھر "ہیروز ایٹ ہوم" پروگرام کے تحت اپ گریڈ کیا گیا۔ مشیل اوباما نے اپنے قد کی وجہ سے بغیر سیڑھی کے کمرے کی پینٹنگ کی۔ $100,000 کی لاگت سے کی گئی یہ تزئین و آرائش 2007 سے شروع ہونے والے "ہیروز ایٹ ہوم" پروگرام کا ایک ہزارواں پروجیکٹ ہے۔ سارجنٹ آگبی نے کہا کہ ان تبدیلیوں نے ان کی زندگی میں نمایاں فرق ڈالا ہے۔

خاتون اول اور ڈاکٹر بائیڈن سینٹ لوئس میں ہونے والے ورلڈ سیریز کے افتتاحی میچ کے دوران خصوصی تقریب میں بھی شریک ہوں گی، جس میں ٹیکساس رینجرز اور سینٹ لوئس کارڈینلز مد مقابل ہوں گے۔ میجر لیگ بیس بال نے اعلان کیا ہے کہ اس میچ کو ویٹرنز اور ان کے اہل خانہ کے نام کیا گیا ہے۔ میچ سے قبل، یہ دونوں سینٹ لوئس وی اے میڈیکل سینٹر میں ملٹری فیملیز کی تقریب میں بھی شرکت کریں گی، جہاں ایم ایل بی کے نمائندے، کارڈینلز کے ہال آف فیمر اور آرمی ویٹرن، ریڈ شوئنڈینسٹ بھی موجود ہوں گے۔ یہ سب "ویلکم بیک ویٹرنز" اور "جائننگ فورسز" پروگرام کا حصہ ہے۔ مشیل اوباما اور ڈاکٹر بائیڈن سوشل میڈیا پر شائقین کے سوالات کے جواب بھی دیں گی۔

کمشنر بڈ سیلگ نے ان کی شرکت کو سراہتے ہوئے بتایا کہ ایم ایل بی نے "ویلکم بیک ویٹرنز" پروگرام کے ذریعے اب تک ویٹرنز اور ان کے اہل خانہ کے لیے گیارہ ملین ڈالر سے زائد رقم اکٹھی کی ہے۔ ان کا کہنا ہے کہ ورلڈ سیریز اس وعدے کو مزید مضبوط بنانے کا موقع ہے کہ ایم ایل بی اپنے ویٹرنز کی ہمیشہ بھرپور حمایت کرے گی۔

article_content: Darrell Hammond, former 'Saturday Night Live' cast member, shared in a CNN interview that he endured severe abuse from his mother as a child, including stabbing, beatings, and electric shocks. These traumatic experiences led to self-harm and frequent psychiatric hospitalizations, both before and during his career on SNL. Hammond explained that this trauma sometimes resulted in cutting himself backstage, occasionally leading to emergency hospitalizations. He was diagnosed with various mental health conditions, such as bipolar disorder and schizophrenia, and was prescribed multiple medications, which he previously described as 'soul-killing' but now recognizes helped stabilize him. Hammond said he performed on SNL while regularly medicated, carrying the weight of his struggles in secret. His relationship with his father, who was affected by his own experiences from war, was also challenging, though his father did not abuse him. Playing certain roles, like John McCain, was difficult for Hammond due to their association with trauma. The deaths of both parents were personally difficult for him. In his memoir, 'God If You're Not Up There, I'm F-ked,' Hammond candidly discusses his childhood, mental health battles, and addiction. He emphasized that he no longer feels ashamed of his past and is committed to sharing his journey openly. NBC had not commented on his disclosures at the time of reporting.

article_content: The Federal Communications Commission (FCC) has received several complaints following a recent on-field outburst by New England Patriots quarterback Tom Brady, despite the fact that none of his words were picked up audibly. The 37-year-old NFL star expressed anger and used explicit language toward the end of the November 30 game against the Green Bay Packers, as it became clear his team was likely to lose. Although Brady was visibly cursing, the microphones during the CBS and NBC national broadcast did not capture the profanity. Nonetheless, at least three viewers filed official complaints with the FCC. Complaints focused on the risk that children watching the game could lip-read and understand the profanities. One Pennsylvania grandparent told the FCC: 'My eight-year-old grandson was watching the game with me and even commented that Tom Brady should not have said that. I understand that the first time, the cameraman would not have expected it, but to keep the camera on him as he continued yelling was unnecessary.' Another complainant said, 'They clearly knew what he was saying, and so did my 10-year-old son. It was almost as if the announcers got away with it because they didn't actually say the word. Very unprofessional.' A third complaint from an Indianapolis parent stated that their six-year-old children know how to read lips even if there is no sound. Addressing the situation, Brady noted that NFL players are not 'choirboys' and suggested viewers should blame CBS and NBC for airing the footage. He commented on WEEI radio, 'I wish I did have a better mouth out there at times, but there is nothing that expresses how I feel quite like that word, especially in the heat of the moment. Blame CBS and NBC for putting it on TV. Don't blame me. We're not choirboys.' Brady explained the intensity required in football, saying, 'You bring us up to a certain level of intensity for the game. Your job is to go out there and physically, emotionally, and mentally dominate. You don't do that at church on Sunday. You've got to come to the football field for that.' Tom Brady has three children: a son with former partner Bridget Moynahan, and a son and daughter with his wife, model Gisele Bundchen. He has not won a Super Bowl in almost ten years.
translated_content: فیڈرل کمیونیکیشنز کمیشن (ایف سی سی) کو حال ہی میں نیو انگلینڈ پیٹریاٹس کے کوارٹر بیک ٹام بریڈی کی فیلڈ پر غصے کے اظہار پر متعدد شکایات موصول ہوئی ہیں، حالانکہ ان کے الفاظ سنائی نہیں دیے تھے۔ ۳۷ سالہ این ایف ایل اسٹار نے ۳۰ نومبر کو گرین بے پیکرز کے خلاف کھیل کے آخر میں غصے میں آ کر نامناسب الفاظ استعمال کیے جب یہ واضح ہو گیا کہ ان کی ٹیم شاید ہارنے والی ہے۔ اگرچہ بریڈی ظاہری طور پر برا بھلا کہہ رہے تھے، سی بی ایس اور این بی سی کی قومی نشریات کے دوران مائکروفونز نے ان کے الفاظ نہیں پکڑے۔ اس کے باوجود کم از کم تین ناظرین نے ایف سی سی میں سرکاری شکایات درج کروائیں۔ شکایات میں بچوں کے ہونٹوں کی حرکات سے نامناسب الفاظ پڑھنے کے امکان پر زور دیا گیا۔ ایک پنسلوانیا کے دادا نے ایف سی سی کو بتایا: 'میرا آٹھ سالہ پوتا میرے ساتھ میچ دیکھ رہا تھا اور اس نے بھی کہا کہ ٹام بریڈی کو ایسا نہیں کہنا چاہیے تھا۔ میں سمجھتا ہوں کہ پہلی بار کیمرہ مین کو اس کی توقع نہیں تھی، لیکن وقتی طور پر بار بار کیمرہ ان پر رکھنے کی ضرورت نہیں تھی۔' ایک اور شکایت کنندہ نے کہا: 'وہ جانتے تھے کہ وہ کیا کہہ رہے ہیں اور میرے دس سالہ بیٹے نے بھی سمجھ لیا۔ ایسا لگا جیسے ایناؤنسروں نے جان بوجھ کر اسے نظرانداز کیا کیونکہ اصل لفظ نشر نہیں ہوا۔ یہ غیر پیشہ ورانہ حرکت تھی۔' انڈیاناپولس کے ایک والدین نے شکایت کی کہ ان کے چھ سالہ بچے بغیر آواز کے بھی ہونٹوں کی حرکات سے الفاظ پڑھ سکتے ہیں۔ اس صورت حال کے جواب میں بریڈی نے کہا کہ این ایف ایل کے کھلاڑی 'کلیسا کے لڑکے' نہیں ہوتے اور ناظرین کو مشورہ دیا کہ وہ فوٹیج نشر کرنے کے لیے سی بی ایس اور این بی سی کو ذمہ دار ٹھہرائیں۔ انہوں نے وی ای ای آئی ریڈیو پر کہا، 'کاش میں میدان میں صاف زبان استعمال کرتا، لیکن اس لمحے میں وہ لفظ میرے جذبات کی حقیقی عکاسی کرتا ہے۔ سی بی ایس اور این بی سی کو مورد الزام ٹہرائیں جنہوں نے اسے ٹی وی پر دکھایا۔ مجھے قصور وار نہ ٹھہرائیں۔ ہم کلیسا کے لڑکے نہیں ہیں۔' بریڈی نے مزید کہا، 'فٹ بال کھیلنے کے لیے ایک خاص شدت کی ضرورت ہوتی ہے۔ آپ کا کام ہے کہ آپ جسمانی، جذباتی اور ذہنی طور پر کھیل پر غالب آئیں۔ یہ سب آپ اتوار کے روز گرجا گھر میں نہیں کرتے، اس کے لیے فٹ بال کے میدان پر آنا پڑتا ہے۔' ٹام بریڈی کے تین بچے ہیں: ایک بیٹا سابق پارٹنر بریجٹ مویناہن سے اور ایک بیٹا اور بیٹی ان کی اہلیہ اور ماڈل جیزل بنڈچن کے ساتھ۔ وہ تقریباً دس سالوں سے سپر باؤل نہیں جیتے۔

article_content: Naresh Arora, co-founder of the consulting firm DesignBoxed, played a significant role in planning successful Congress campaigns in Karnataka and Rajasthan. Rajasthan is known for regularly alternating its ruling party. This time, Arora spearheaded Chief Minister Ashok Gehlot’s campaign for nine months, especially after election schedules were announced. Arora expresses confidence in Congress’s performance, crediting the extensive groundwork and real-time feedback from voters. He highlights that various strategic campaigns increased public engagement, allowing Congress to control the political conversation and push opponents into a reactive stance. Arora points out that this Rajasthan election is different, reflecting a shift from candidate-focused voting to support for parties whose welfare programs benefit the public. He made it a priority to communicate the value of welfare schemes, such as the Mehengai Rahat camps, where people could register for important government benefits. He clarifies that effective campaigning goes beyond publicity, involving research, strategic planning, consultation with party leaders, and detailed execution. Describing work with party leaders, Arora notes that Ashok Gehlot prefers a thorough, consultative approach, taking advice before deciding, while D K Shivakumar tends to act quickly and decisively. Gehlot, unlike Shivakumar, also prefers traditional communication methods. Addressing speculation about disagreements with state Congress president Govind Singh Dotasra and concerns from government publicity officials, Arora states these were misunderstandings and that any supposed conflicts have been publicly denied. Having worked on ten election campaigns, Arora admits the job is demanding and has personal costs. He firmly rules out running for office, explaining he prefers working in policy advocacy and communication, as well as pursuing other interests such as film-making. He concludes that for him to accept future political campaigns, the project must offer both challenge and creative freedom.

Many major tech companies in Silicon Valley have been requiring employees to return to the office, sometimes using threats. However, Nvidia, whose chips are crucial to the AI revolution, has not enforced strict return-to-office mandates. In 2020, CEO Jensen Huang told VentureBeat he was "perfectly comfortable" with staff working from home three or four days a week for as long as they wanted. While many CEOs have reversed course on remote work, Nvidia has maintained a flexible policy. Beau Davidson, vice president of employee experience at Nvidia, told Commercial Observer that flexible work helps attract and retain talent. He described it as a way for employees to balance their personal and work responsibilities and to prepare for the future, allowing them to focus on meaningful work. Davidson added that Nvidia is seeing a healthy and growing flow of employees on campus.

In contrast, some companies using Nvidia's chips have adopted different policies. Mark Zuckerberg, CEO of Meta, whose company has a supercomputer with 16,000 Nvidia A100 GPUs, has enforced a strict policy requiring most employees to return to the office most days of the week. Attendance will be monitored, and employees may be disciplined or even let go for non-compliance. Similarly, Sam Altman, CEO of OpenAI (another significant Nvidia customer), said in May that "remote work is over," requiring staff to return to the office.

Despite this, Nvidia’s remarkable growth challenges such claims by some industry leaders. Demand for the company’s chips, which enable AI large language models, has sent Nvidia’s stock price soaring and raised its market value to $1.1 trillion. Nvidia plans to increase production next year to between 1.5 and 2 million units. Even though US laws prohibit Nvidia from selling chips to China, demand in China is so high that Chinese firms are reportedly buying them on the Hong Kong black market, according to Reuters.

Though Nvidia allows flexible work, its $900 million headquarters—called Voyager after "Star Trek"—opened in Santa Clara in 2022. The building provides all employees with views of nature and was designed to avoid a boxed-in feeling, according to CNET. This new facility may entice some employees back to the office.

سیلیکون ویلی کی بہت سی بڑی ٹیک کمپنیاں اپنے ملازمین کو دفتر واپس بلانے پر زور دے رہی ہیں، بعض اوقات سخت اقدامات اور دھمکیوں کے ساتھ۔ تاہم Nvidia، جو AI انقلاب کے لیے اہم چپس تیار کرتی ہے، نے سخت واپسی کی پالیسی لاگو نہیں کی۔ 2020 میں، سی ای او جینسن ہوانگ نے VentureBeat کو کہا کہ وہ اس بات میں "بالکل مطمئن" ہیں کہ ملازمین ہفتے میں تین یا چار دن گھر سے جتنا چاہیں کام کریں۔ اگرچہ کئی سی ای اوز نے ریموٹ ورک سے متعلق اپنی سوچ بدلی ہے، Nvidia نے لچکدار پالیسی برقرار رکھی ہے۔ Nvidia کے وائس پریزیڈنٹ بیو ڈیوڈسن نے Commercial Observer کو بتایا کہ لچکدار ورک پالیسی سے ٹیلنٹ کو اپنی طرف متوجہ کرنا اور برقرار رکھنا آسان ہوتا ہے۔ ان کا کہنا تھا کہ اس سے ملازمین ذاتی اور کام کی ذمہ داریوں میں توازن برقرار رکھ سکتے ہیں اور یہ مستقبل کے لئے تیاری کا ذریعہ بنتی ہے، تاکہ وہ اہم کام پر توجہ دے سکیں۔ ڈیوڈسن کے مطابق کمپنی میں آن سائٹ ملازمین کی تعداد بھی مسلسل بڑھ رہی ہے۔

اس کے برعکس Nvidia کی چپس استعمال کرنے والی بعض کمپنیوں نے مختلف پالیسیاں اپنائیں۔ میٹا کے سی ای او مارک زکربرگ، جن کی کمپنی نے 16,000 Nvidia A100 GPUs پر مشتمل سپر کمپیوٹر بنایا ہے، نے زیادہ تر ملازمین کو ہفتے کے اکثر دن دفتر آنے کا لازمی حکم جاری کیا۔ حاضری کی نگرانی کی جائے گی اور خلاف ورزی پر ملازمین کو سزا یا برطرف بھی کیا جا سکتا ہے۔ اسی طرح اوپن اے آئی کے سی ای او سیم آلٹ مین (جو Nvidia کے اہم کسٹمر ہیں)، نے بھی مئی میں کہا کہ "ریمورٹ ورک اب ختم ہوچکی ہے" اور سب کو دفتر آنا ہوگا۔

اس سب کے باوجود Nvidia کی متاثرکن ترقی بعض قیادتوں کے واپسی موقف پر سوال اٹھاتی ہے۔ کمپنی کی چپس کی تیز طلب، جو AI لینگویج ماڈلز کو طاقت دیتی ہیں، نے Nvidia کے شیئرز کی قیمت بڑھا کر مارکیٹ ویلیو $1.1 ٹریلین تک پہنچا دی ہے۔ Nvidia آئندہ سال چپ کی پیداوار کو 1.5 سے 2 ملین یونٹس تک بڑھانے کی منصوبہ بندی کر رہی ہے۔ اگرچہ امریکی قوانین Nvidia کو چین میں چپس فروخت کرنے سے روکتے ہیں، چین میں اتنی زیادہ طلب ہے کہ کمپنیاں ہانگ کانگ کی بلیک مارکیٹ سے چپس خرید رہی ہیں، جیسا کہ رائٹرز نے رپورٹ کیا۔

Nvidia کی اجازت یافتہ لچکدار ورک پالیسی کے باوجود، اس کا 900 ملین ڈالر مالیت کا ہیڈکوارٹر "Voyager" (Star Trek سے متاثر) 2022 میں سانتا کلارا میں کھولا گیا۔ یہ عمارت ملازمین کو قدرتی مناظرات فراہم کرتی ہے اور انہیں محدود ماحول محسوس نہیں ہونے دیتی، جیسا کہ CNET نے بتایاہے۔ یہ نئی سہولت بعض ملازمین کو دفتر واپسی کی طرف مائل کر سکتی ہے۔

article_content: Health screenings for Ebola started on Saturday at New York’s JFK Airport, targeting travelers from West African nations most affected by the outbreak. The Centers for Disease Control and Prevention (CDC) has announced that four more major U.S. airports will begin similar screenings later in the week. Each day, about 150 passengers will undergo checks, which involve taking their temperatures and answering questions about their health and possible exposure to Ebola. CDC officials, including Dr. Martin Cetron, emphasized that while these procedures add a protective layer, it’s impossible to reduce the Ebola risk to zero. Dr. Cetron explained that the new measures would not have identified Thomas Eric Duncan, the first patient diagnosed with Ebola in the U.S., as he showed no symptoms on arrival. The additional screenings at airports are designed to catch cases that could pose a risk to public safety but may not be enough to entirely prevent the virus from entering the country. The new protocols apply to travelers arriving from Guinea, Liberia, and Sierra Leone. Coast Guard corpsmen, along with medical staff, will conduct temperature checks, and Customs and Border Protection will ask travelers about health and potential contact with Ebola. Anyone who appears at risk will be referred to a CDC health officer for closer inspection. Once the initial trial at JFK is complete, screenings will expand to airports in Washington, D.C. (Dulles), Newark, Chicago (O'Hare), and Atlanta (Hartsfield-Jackson). According to the CDC, these five airports receive the vast majority of passengers arriving from Ebola-affected countries. Customs and Border Protection Commissioner R. Gil Kerlikowske said that travelers with fevers or symptoms, or those suspected of Ebola exposure, would be referred for further evaluation. Border Patrol agents will also remain vigilant for signs of illness. The screenings join existing protocols in place in the countries of departure, where passengers are already checked for symptoms and potential exposure before boarding flights. Dr. Cetron reported that over the past two months, more than 36,000 travelers were screened in West Africa with no Ebola cases detected. Not everyone believes the screenings are a major step forward. Laurie Garrett, a global health fellow at the Council on Foreign Relations, said the screenings may simply provide reassurance to the public, since they wouldn’t have detected known imported cases like Duncan’s. Mary Schiavo, former inspector general at the U.S. Department of Transportation, noted that the measures are not merely symbolic but more needs to be done to ensure safety. Some worry about infected passengers showing symptoms only after disembarking. Health officials have repeatedly warned that airport checks are far from perfect, as Ebola’s incubation period can be up to 21 days. Therefore, local health departments and medical staff must remain vigilant and prepared to identify and manage cases as soon as symptoms emerge. Globally, the Ebola outbreak remains serious. According to the World Health Organization, as of October 7, at least 8,399 people have been infected, leading to 4,033 deaths in countries like Guinea, Liberia, Sierra Leone, Nigeria, Senegal, Spain, and the U.S. Among healthcare workers, 416 have been infected and 233 have died. Several Americans, including aid workers Nancy Writebol, Dr. Kent Brantly, and Dr. Rick Sacra, contracted Ebola in Liberia. They received treatment in U.S. hospitals and have since recovered. Ashoka Mukpo, an NBC News cameraman who became ill in early October, is reportedly improving after receiving an experimental drug and a blood transfusion from a survivor. Meanwhile, NBC staff who had contact with Mukpo are under mandatory quarantine in New Jersey. No symptoms have appeared among them so far. In Europe and beyond, measures are being ramped up. The UK is introducing expanded screening at airports and train terminals. Spain is treating its first domestically acquired case, nursing assistant Teresa Romero Ramos, who remains in serious condition. Other hospital staff exposed to Romero are being monitored, though none have developed symptoms. Despite concerns, Morocco plans to proceed as scheduled with the 2015 Africa Cup of Nations football tournament. Russia announced they are working on multiple Ebola vaccines, aiming for deployment within six months. International efforts continue to focus on prevention, monitoring, and treatment as health authorities try to contain the outbreak.
translated_content: نیویارک کے JFK ہوائی اڈے پر ہفتے کے روز ایبولا کی اسکریننگز شروع ہوئیں، جو مغربی افریقہ کے سب سے زیادہ متاثرہ ممالک سے آنے والے مسافروں پر مرکوز ہیں۔ سینٹرز فار ڈیزیز کنٹرول اینڈ پریوینشن (CDC) کے مطابق چار مزید اہم امریکی ہوائی اڈوں پر بھی یہ اسکریننگز شروع کی جائیں گی۔ روزانہ تقریباً 150 مسافر جانچ سے گزریں گے، جس میں ان کا درجہ حرارت لینا اور صحت یا ایبولا سے ممکنہ تعلق کے بارے میں سوالات شامل ہیں۔ CDC کے اہلکار، جن میں ڈاکٹر مارٹن سیٹرون شامل ہیں، نے بتایا ہے کہ ان اقدامات کے باوجود ایبولا کے خطرے کو مکمل طور پر ختم کرنا ممکن نہیں۔ ڈاکٹر سیٹرون نے وضاحت کی کہ یہ نئے اقدامات امریکہ میں ایبولا کے پہلے مریض تھامس ایرک ڈنکن کو نہ پکڑ پاتے کیونکہ ان میں آمد پر علامات نہیں تھیں۔ یہ اسکریننگز مزید سکیورٹی فراہم کرنے کے لیے ہیں مگر وائرس کے پھیلاؤ کو مکمل طور پر روک نہیں سکتیں۔ یہ نئے پروٹوکول گنی، لائبیریا اور سیرا لیون سے آنے والوں پر لاگو ہوں گے۔ کوسٹ گارڈ کے اہلکار اور طبی اسٹاف مسافروں کا درجہ حرارت چیک کریں گے اور کسٹمز اور بارڈر پروٹیکشن صحت یا ایبولا سے رابطے کے بارے میں پوچھے گا۔ مشتبہ افراد کو CDC کے ہیلتھ افسر کے پاس مزید جانچ کے لیے بھیجا جائے گا۔ JFK پر ابتدائی آزمائش کے بعد یہ اسکریننگز واشنگٹن (ڈلس)، نیوارک، شکاگو (اوہیر)، اور اٹلانٹا (ہارٹس فیلڈ-جیکسن) تک پھیلائی جائیں گی۔ CDC کے مطابق یہ پانچ ہوائی اڈے ایبولا سے متاثرہ ممالک سے زیادہ تر مسافروں کو وصول کرتے ہیں۔ کسٹمز اور بارڈر پروٹیکشن کمشنر آر. گل کرلیکوسکے نے بتایا کہ بخار یا علامات والے یا ایبولا میں مبتلا ہونے کے شبہ میں مبتلا مسافروں کو مزید جانچ کے لیے بھیجا جائے گا۔ بارڈر پٹرول ایجنٹس بھی بیماری کی علامات پر نظر رکھیں گے۔ یہ اسکریننگ ان پروٹوکولز میں شامل ہیں جو روانگی والے ممالک میں پہلے سے رائج ہیں۔ ڈاکٹر سیٹرون کے مطابق، گزشتہ دو ماہ میں مغربی افریقہ میں 36,000 سے زائد مسافروں کی اسکریننگ ہوئی لیکن کوئی ایبولا کیس سامنے نہیں آیا۔ تاہم سب لوگ ان اسکریننگز کو مؤثر حل نہیں مانتے۔ کونسل آن فارن ریلیشنز کی ہیلتھ فیلو لاری گیریٹ نے کہا کہ اسکریننگ عوام کو ذرا تسلی دے سکتی ہے، تاہم یہ ماضی کے مریضوں کو نہ پکڑ سکی ہوتی۔ ٹرانسپورٹیشن کی سابق انسپکٹر جنرل میری شییاوو نے کہا کہ اقدامات صرف رسمی کارروائی نہیں، بلکہ مزید کچھ کرنے کی ضرورت ہے۔ کچھ لوگ اس بات پر فکر مند ہیں کہ کہیں مسافر پرواز کے بعد بیمار نہ ہو جائے۔ ہیلتھ اہلکار بار بار متنبہ کرتے ہیں کہ ہوائی اڈوں پر چیکنگ کافی نہیں، کیونکہ ایبولا کے ظہور میں 21 دن لگ سکتے ہیں۔ اس لیے مقامی ہیلتھ ڈیپارٹمنٹس اور میڈیکل اسٹاف کو چوکنا رہنا ہو گا تاکہ علامات ظاہر ہوتے ہی فوری ایکشن لیا جا سکے۔ عالمی سطح پر ایبولا کی صورت حال سنگین ہے۔ ورلڈ ہیلتھ آرگنائزیشن کے مطابق 7 اکتوبر تک کم از کم 8,399 افراد متاثر اور 4,033 ہلاک ہو چکے ہیں۔ متاثرہ ممالک میں گنی، لائبیریا، سیرا لیون، نائیجیریا، سینیگال، اسپین اور امریکا شامل ہیں۔ طبّی عملے میں 416 متاثر اور 233 ہلاک ہوئے۔ کئی امریکی، جیسے نینسی رائٹبول، ڈاکٹر کینٹ برینٹلی اور ڈاکٹر رک سیکرا لائبیریا میں ایبولا کا شکار ہوئے۔ انہوں نے امریکا میں علاج کے بعد صحت یابی حاصل کی۔ این بی سی نیوز کے کیمرامین اشوکا مکپو، جو اکتوبر کے شروع میں بیمار ہوئے، تجرباتی دوا اور سروائیور کے خون کے عطیے کے بعد صحت یاب ہو رہے ہیں۔ مکپو کے رابطے میں آنے والے این بی سی کے عملے کو نیو جرسی میں لازمی قرنطینہ کر دیا گیا ہے اور اب تک ان میں کوئی علامات ظاہر نہیں ہوئیں۔ یورپ میں اقدامات بڑھا دئیے گئے ہیں۔ برطانیہ ہوائی اڈوں اور ٹرین اسٹیشنز پر اسکریننگ بڑھا رہا ہے۔ اسپین میں پہلی مقامی مریضہ نرسنگ اسسٹنٹ ٹریسا رومیرو راموس تشویشناک حالت میں زیر علاج ہیں۔ دیگر ہسپتال عملہ بھی زیر نگرانی ہے، لیکن کسی میں علامات نہیں۔ تشویش کے باوجود، مراکش افریکن کپ آف نیشنز کی فٹبال چیمپئن شپ اپنے طے شدہ شیڈول کے مطابق جاری رکھے گا۔ روس نے کہا ہے کہ وہ اگلے چھ ماہ میں ایبولا کی کئی ویکسینز تیار کرے گا۔ دنیا بھر کے صحت حکام ایبولا سے نمٹنے کیلئے بچاؤ، نگرانی اور علاج کی کوششیں جاری رکھے ہوئے ہیں۔

article_content: Former Super Eagles coach Sunday Oliseh has described Nigeria’s 1-1 draw with Lesotho in Thursday’s 2026 World Cup qualifier at the Godswill Akpabio Stadium, Uyo, as a national embarrassment, according to PUNCH Sports Extra. Lesotho, ranked 153rd globally—113 places below Nigeria—took a surprise lead with Motlomelo Mkwanazi’s powerful header in the 56th minute from a corner. West Bromwich Albion defender Semi Ajayi equalized for Nigeria 11 minutes later, heading in a corner taken by Kelechi Iheanacho. Despite dominating the match, Jose Peseiro’s team could not find a winning goal in their Group C opener, which was played in rainy conditions in Uyo. Nigeria created multiple chances, with Iheanacho’s free-kick saved, Taiwo Awoniyi missing a promising cut-back, Ademola Lookman’s low shot being turned away, and Jamilu Collins’ effort also parried out for a corner. Reacting to the draw, Oliseh, who represented Nigeria at two World Cups before retiring from international football in 2002, said he believed that players from the Nigeria Premier Football League would have beaten Lesotho. Oliseh expressed his frustration on social media, stating, “Will this nightmare ever end? Woke up to this shocker this morning. Our home-based players should beat Lesotho. They even scored first! The painful part is, no consequences for these national embarrassments.” The Super Eagles will have a chance to bounce back when they face Zimbabwe in their next match on Sunday in Kigali, Rwanda.

UNICEF has revealed that 48 million Nigerians, amounting to 23% of the country’s population, continue to defecate in the open. According to a regional breakdown, open defecation is most prevalent in the North-Central zone (47%), followed by the South-West (24%), South-South (23%), South-East (23%), North-East (17%), and North-West (11%).

Mamita Bora Thakkar, UNICEF’s North-East Water, Sanitation, and Hygiene (WASH) Manager, shared these statistics during a news briefing in Maiduguri ahead of World Toilet Day, celebrated each year on November 19 to raise awareness about the importance of safe toilets.

Thakkar expressed concern that, with just seven years left to achieve the 2030 targets, Nigeria is significantly off track in meeting the Sustainable Development Goal (SDG) 6: universal access to sanitation. She highlighted that only 104 of Nigeria’s 774 local government areas have been declared open defecation-free, underlining the need for urgent action to improve sanitation nationwide.

On a global scale, Thakkar noted that 3.5 billion people lack access to safe toilets, 2.2 billion do not have safe drinking water, and 419 million people still practice open defecation. She emphasized that progress towards universal sanitation is unevenly distributed and insufficient to eliminate inequalities, particularly for the most vulnerable populations.

Thakkar described access to sanitation and safe drinking water as fundamental human rights, essential to both people’s health and environmental integrity.

article_content: THE HAGUE: Judges at the International Court of Justice (ICJ) on Friday ordered Azerbaijan to allow ethnic Armenians who fled Nagorno-Karabakh in September to return safely and to ensure the safety of those who remain. The decision is part of emergency measures following Azerbaijan's rapid retaking of Nagorno-Karabakh after years of conflict with Armenia. The military operation resulted in most of the region's estimated 120,000 ethnic Armenians fleeing to Armenia. Armenia has accused Azerbaijan of ethnic cleansing and requested the ICJ, also known as the World Court, to issue urgent measures to protect the rights of ethnic Armenians from Nagorno-Karabakh. "Azerbaijan must (...) ensure that persons who have left Nagorno-Karabakh after 19 September 2023 and who wish to return are able to do so safely, without obstruction, and quickly," said presiding judge Joan Donoghue. The ICJ further ordered Azerbaijan to guarantee that any ethnic Armenians still living in the region are "free from the use of force or intimidation that may cause them to flee," and directed Azerbaijan to report within two months on its compliance. Azerbaijani representatives previously told the court in October that those who fled would be allowed to return and that all remaining residents would be kept safe. The measures are set against the backdrop of ongoing legal disputes between Armenia and Azerbaijan at the ICJ, with both sides accusing each other of violating a United Nations anti-discrimination treaty. No date has been set for the main hearings, and a final verdict is not expected until well into next year.

article_content: Dozens gathered in cities across Russia to pay tribute to Wagner mercenary group chief Yevgeny Prigozhin on the 40th day after his death, a significant day of mourning in the Eastern Orthodox tradition. Prigozhin died in a plane crash en route from Moscow to St. Petersburg on August 23, along with other top Wagner commanders, four bodyguards, and three crew members. The cause of the crash remains unexplained. At his grave in St. Petersburg, Prigozhin's mother, Violetta, and his son, Pavel, laid flowers as supporters displayed black Wagner flags emblazoned with a skull and the motto 'Blood, Honour, Motherland, Courage.' The 40-day mark is regarded in the Eastern Orthodox church as a time when the soul makes its final journey to the afterlife. Memorials were also held in Moscow and other Russian cities, with Wagner fighters and ordinary citizens attending. These events received no coverage on Russian state television and there were no official tributes. The Wagner group played a key role in the conflict in Ukraine, notably helping to capture the eastern town of Bakhmut in May after prolonged fighting. After the mutiny, Wagner troops were relocated to camps in Belarus, continuing activities in several African countries as well. Wagner’s recruitment arm described Prigozhin as a patriot who defended Russia's interests on different continents, praising his charisma and popularity among both fighters and everyday people. Prigozhin's armed mutiny in June, following months of public criticism of Russian military leaders, posed perhaps the most serious challenge to President Vladimir Putin’s leadership since 1999. The rebellion saw Wagner forces occupying the city of Rostov, downing several Russian aircraft, and advancing toward Moscow before halting following a deal reportedly brokered by Belarusian President Alexander Lukashenko. Many mourners spoke with respect for Prigozhin, recalling his early connections to Putin when he ran a restaurant business in St. Petersburg in the 1990s. He later earned lucrative state catering contracts, gaining the nickname 'Putin’s chef,' and was indicted in the US for alleged interference in the 2016 presidential election. His leadership of Wagner brought further notoriety, as the group became known for its ruthlessness. Prigozhin and Wagner co-founder Dmitry Utkin, both killed in the crash, were influential yet controversial figures. Russia appears set to continue utilizing Wagner’s capabilities, with President Putin assigning Commander Andrei Troshev to organize new volunteer units, especially for the ongoing military operation in Ukraine.

article_content:
Over 650,000 Nigerian children were displaced by floods between 2016 and 2021, according to the United Nations Children’s Fund (UNICEF). The agency further reports that more than 110 million Nigerian children are at risk due to climate change, facing rising temperatures, flooding, drought, and severe storms. UNICEF shared these findings on Monday to mark World Children’s Day, observed every November 20 in remembrance of the 1959 Declaration of the Rights of the Child by the UN General Assembly.

This year’s World Children’s Day focuses on children’s rights in the context of the worsening climate crisis. UNICEF states that Nigeria is the world’s second most vulnerable country in terms of children’s exposure to climate change. The agency’s representative in Nigeria, Cristian Munduate, highlighted that children are the most affected by climate change and their input is essential in shaping a sustainable and resilient future.

Dr. Salisu Dahiru, Director General of the National Council on Climate Change, emphasized the urgent need for a swift and holistic response to climate impacts, especially addressing the needs of vulnerable groups such as children and women in both decision-making and in implementing the National Climate Change Action Plan.

سنہ 2016 سے 2021 کے درمیان 6 لاکھ 50 ہزار سے زائد نائجیرین بچے سیلابوں کی وجہ سے بے گھر ہوئے، اقوام متحدہ کے بچوں کے فنڈ (یونیسف) کے مطابق۔ ادارے نے مزید بتایا کہ ایک کروڑ دس لاکھ سے زیادہ نائجیرین بچے موسمیاتی تبدیلی کے باعث خطرے میں ہیں، جنہیں درجہ حرارت میں اضافہ، سیلاب، خشک سالی اور شدید طوفانوں کا سامنا ہے۔ یونیسف نے یہ اعدادوشمار پیر کے روز عالمی یومِ اطفال کے موقع پر جاری کیے، جو ہر سال 20 نومبر کو اقوام متحدہ کی جنرل اسمبلی کے 1959 کے اعلامیے برائے حقوقِ اطفال کی یاد میں منایا جاتا ہے۔

اس سال عالمی یومِ اطفال کا موضوع موسمیاتی بحران کے شدید ہوتے اثرات میں بچوں کے حقوق پر مرکوز ہے۔ یونیسف کا کہنا ہے کہ بچوں کے موسمیاتی خطرات کے حوالے سے نائجیریا دنیا میں دوسرے نمبر پر سب سے زیادہ متاثر ملک ہے۔ یونیسف کی نمائندہ برائے نائجیریا، کرسٹین مونڈوآٹے نے کہا کہ بچے موسمیاتی تبدیلی سے سب سے زیادہ متاثر ہوتے ہیں اور ان کی رائے ایک پائیدار اور مستحکم مستقبل کی تشکیل کے لیے ضروری ہے۔

نیشنل کونسل آن کلائمیٹ چینج کے ڈائریکٹر جنرل ڈاکٹر سالیسو دہیرو نے موسمیاتی اثرات پر فوری اور مربوط ردعمل کی ضرورت پر زور دیتے ہوئے کہا کہ فیصلوں اور قومی عملدرآمد کے مرحلے پر بچوں اور خواتین سمیت کمزور طبقات کی ضروریات کو ترجیح دی جائے۔

article_content: A Federal Capital Territory High Court has remanded former Central Bank of Nigeria (CBN) governor, Godwin Emefiele, in Kuje Correctional Centre. Emefiele is standing trial on allegations of procurement fraud. The trial, which had been delayed three times, commenced on Friday. Originally, the Federal Government brought 20 charges of procurement fraud totaling N6.5 billion against Emefiele. However, the charges were later reduced to six, amounting to over N1 billion, before his arraignment. During Friday's proceedings, Emefiele’s counsel, Mathew Burkaa, SAN, applied for bail. This application was opposed by Federal Government counsel Rotimi Oyedepo. Presiding judge, Justice Hamza Muazu, stated that due to the numerous legal authorities cited by both parties, he could not deliver a bench ruling immediately. He said he needed time to review all the authorities and the exhibits provided by Emefiele in support of his bail request. Justice Muazu then ordered that Emefiele be remanded at Kuje Correctional Centre pending a decision on his bail application. The judge adjourned the ruling on bail to November 22 and scheduled the commencement of the trial for November 28. This remand order followed an earlier directive on November 8 by Justice Olukayode Adeniyi, who ordered that Emefiele should be released to his lawyers after spending 151 days in detention.
translated_content: وفاقی دارالحکومت کی ہائی کورٹ نے سابق سینٹرل بینک آف نائجیریا (CBN) کے گورنر، گڈون ایمیفیئلے کو کوجے اصلاحی مرکز میں بھیج دیا ہے۔ ایمیفیئلے پر خریداری میں فراڈ کے الزامات کا مقدمہ چل رہا ہے۔ یہ مقدمہ تین بار معطل ہونے کے بعد جمعہ کو شروع ہوا۔ ابتدا میں وفاقی حکومت نے ایمیفیئلے پر 20 الزامات عائد کیے تھے جن میں کل رقم 6.5 ارب نائرا تھی۔ تاہم بعد میں الزامات کم ہو کر چھ رہ گئے، جن کی مالیت ایک ارب نائرا سے زیادہ ہے، اور اس کے بعد انہیں عدالت میں پیش کیا گیا۔ جمعہ کی سماعت میں ایمیفیئلے کے وکیل میتھیو برکا، سینئر ایڈووکیٹ آف نائجیریا (SAN)، نے ضمانت کے لیے درخواست دائر کی۔ وفاقی حکومت کے وکیل روٹمی اوئیدیپو نے اس درخواست کی مخالفت کی۔ صدر نشین جج جسٹس حمزہ معاذو نے کہا کہ دونوں فریقین کی طرف سے بہت سے قانونی حوالہ جات پیش کیے گئے ہیں، اس لیے فوری طور پر فیصلہ دینا ممکن نہیں ہے۔ انہوں نے کہا کہ انہیں تمام حوالہ جات اور ایمیفیئلے کی طرف سے پیش کردہ دستاویزات کا جائزہ لینے کے لیے کچھ وقت درکار ہے۔ جسٹس معاذو نے ایمیفیئلے کو ضمانت کی درخواست پر فیصلے تک کوجے اصلاحی مرکز میں رکھنے کا حکم دیا۔ جج نے ضمانت پر فیصلہ 22 نومبر کو اور مقدمہ کی باقاعدہ سماعت 28 نومبر کو شروع کرنے کا اعلان کیا۔ یہ حکم اس سے قبل 8 نومبر کو جسٹس اولوکایوڈے ادینیی کے اس فیصلے کے بعد آیا، جس میں کہا گیا تھا کہ ایمیفیئلے کو 151 دن کی حراست کے بعد ان کے وکلاء کے حوالے کر دیا جائے۔

article_content:
Police in Dallas, Texas are searching for a woman suspected of stealing packages from the doorsteps of multiple homes. Surveillance cameras captured footage of the woman exiting a car, approaching two separate houses, taking packages from their front porches, and then returning to the vehicle. One couple, Missy and Ken Clinchy, shared their footage on Facebook and are offering a $100 reward for information that leads to the identification of the thief.

Mrs. Clinchy recalled expecting three packages outside her home, only to discover they were missing upon her return. When reviewing their surveillance footage, the couple was shocked to see a woman clearly taking the packages. Their video, posted online, led to another resident—living ten minutes away—sharing similar footage of the same woman, wearing identical clothes, stealing an electric smoker from their doorstep. In both cases, the thefts took place in broad daylight and the suspect appeared unconcerned.

The Clinchys reported that their stolen package contained Christmas gifts and dog food ordered from Amazon. They expressed concern not only for themselves but also for other families who lost meaningful items, such as personalized gifts and wedding invitations. The couple stated their intent in sharing the footage is to help prevent similar thefts from affecting others.

Police believe the suspect may be working with another person, as she was seen exiting the passenger side of the car. Authorities encourage anyone with information about these thefts to contact Detective Evans at 214-670-6179.

article_content: Jordan has cancelled a highly-anticipated summit that was meant to bring together U.S. President Joe Biden, along with Egyptian and Palestinian leaders, as violence intensifies in Gaza. Jordanian Foreign Minister Ayman Safadi explained that the summit will only occur once all sides are prepared to seek an end to the conflict and violence affecting Palestinians, blaming Israel's military campaign for increasing instability in the region. As a result, President Biden will now visit only Israel and put off his planned trip to Jordan, according to statements from the White House. The meeting, which King Abdullah was set to host, aimed to find ways to provide humanitarian assistance to Gaza and de-escalate the conflict. Instead, Biden is heading solely to Israel for now. After a deadly blast at a Gaza hospital that reportedly killed some 500 Palestinians, King Abdullah condemned Israel, calling the event a blot on humanity and calling for an immediate end to the Israeli offensive. While Palestinian officials blamed an Israeli airstrike, Israeli authorities said the explosion was due to a misfired rocket from a Palestinian group; neither account has been independently verified. King Abdullah also criticized Israel's response to the October 7 Hamas attack, arguing that it goes beyond self-defense and results in collective punishment for Palestinian civilians. The summit's cancellation signals mounting instability in the region and could challenge U.S. diplomatic influence, particularly as Biden meets with Israeli, but not Palestinian, leaders. Biden’s approach is drawing criticism back home, especially after US Representative Rashida Tlaib, who is Palestinian American, publicly decried his reluctance to push for a ceasefire. More than 70 U.S. religious and activist groups, led by the Council on American-Islamic Relations, are urging Biden to advocate for a ceasefire in Gaza during his visit.
