article_content: Doping is an increasingly significant issue in rugby union, especially since professionalization. Leaders like Ian Ritchie, CEO of England’s RFU, openly admit the sport is struggling with drug use. Recent suspensions, such as Nick Clancy's case—which marks the tenth rugby doping ban in the UK this year—have put rugby’s drug culture under the microscope. Informants such as ex-France player Laurent Benezech allege that performance-enhancing drugs are pervasive, with some young players pressured to gain size unnaturally. Benezech, who was vindicated in court for speaking out, and an anonymous former English coach, suggest that doping extends to elite levels, not just among aspiring professionals. The remarkable physical changes in players over two decades are often credited to more than just training and diet. The RFU and anti-doping agencies have tightened their efforts, launching widespread testing and education programs. However, the ease of obtaining banned substances, especially online or at gyms, continues to fuel the problem, as does the intense pressure on youths to achieve pro status. Cases such as Sam Chalmers’ suspension for steroids in Scotland and Chiliboy Ralepelle’s provisional ban after repeated positive tests highlight that doping affects both new talent and established stars. Steffon Armitage also tested positive, though he was cleared of intent. Officials emphasize their commitment to addressing doping, with rigorous testing—most of it out of competition—and ongoing studies into substance abuse trends, especially among young male rugby players. Despite declarations that doping is mainly a junior problem, many within rugby believe the top tiers are also at risk. Critics warn that as long as rugby’s physical demands and culture remain unchanged, the incentive to dope will persist. Rugby’s response relies on thorough education, transparency, and strict anti-doping measures, but authorities admit ongoing work is needed to fully protect players and uphold the sport’s reputation.

article_content: New York City is alive with remarkable tales, and while guidebooks serve as a solid starting point, there’s a wide range of books that dive deeper into its rich history, diverse neighborhoods, local characters, flavorful cuisine, and iconic landmarks. This holiday season, consider gifting someone a book that truly captures the essence of NYC. Here’s a curated list of both nonfiction and fiction works that offer a fresh look at the city. "Made Here: Recipes & Reflections From NYC's Asian Communities" ($49) was created by Send Chinatown Love, a nonprofit formed to support Asian-owned small businesses during the pandemic. The cookbook presents over 60 recipes from more than 40 restaurants and food businesses in Manhattan, Brooklyn, and Queens, reflecting culinary traditions from 18 cultures. It also guides readers on where to find the right ingredients. "The Manhattan Nobody Knows" (and related books, starting at $24) is authored by William B. Helmreich, who set out to walk every block in NYC, covering about 6,000 miles. His guides offer detailed explorations of neighborhoods across every borough, revealing fascinating landmarks and stories. "The Bowery Boys: Adventures In Old New York" ($26.95) comes from podcasters Greg Young and Tom Meyers, who share lively tales from NYC’s past—including gas-lit alleyways and neighborhoods such as Hell’s Kitchen and Tribeca—while shining a light on hidden stories from the city’s history. "New York: Treasures From The Museum of The City of New York" ($12.95) commemorates the centennial of the museum in East Harlem. It traces NYC’s evolution from the days of the Lenape people to the present using 250 paintings, drawings, photographs, manuscripts, and artifacts. "The Met 5000 Years of Awesome Objects" ($29.99) is a children’s journey through the dazzling collection of The Metropolitan Museum, featuring Egyptian amulets, medieval tapestries, suits of armor, and even baseball cards. It reveals the stories behind these treasures in a way young readers can enjoy. "Grand Central: How a Train Station Transformed America" ($18.99) by Sam Roberts (including a foreword by Pete Hamill) details the history of Grand Central Terminal and its rise as a transportation and cultural icon, with personal anecdotes, behind-the-scenes glimpses, and fun facts. "Seeing Central Park: The Official Guide" ($25.99), updated by photographer and historian Sara Cedar Miller, is filled with striking new photographs and insights, leading readers through Central Park’s beautiful settings and notable highlights. "The Women Who Made New York" ($28) by Julie Scelfo, illustrated by Hallie Heald, celebrates the remarkable women who influenced NYC—such as Emily Warren Roebling, who led Brooklyn Bridge construction, and figures like Zora Neale Hurston, Audre Lorde, Fran Lebowitz, and Grace Jones. "Harlem Shuffle" ($28.95) is Colson Whitehead’s novel steeped in a recreated 1960s Harlem. It weaves together a family saga, a crime story, and an exploration of societal issues like race and power. "How We Live Now: Scenes from the Pandemic" ($17) by Bill Hayes captures NYC’s first 100 days under COVID-19 and the Black Lives Matter protests, told through vivid prose and photographs. "This Must Be the Place" ($32) by Jesse Rifkin unveils the changing face of NYC’s communal music scenes, featuring perspectives from more than 100 musicians, DJs, and insiders on how creative communities take shape and transform. "The 1998 Yankees: The Inside Story of the Greatest Baseball Team Ever" ($21) by Jack Curry revisits the team’s 24th World Series title, presenting fresh interviews with players, coaches, and executives who witnessed their historic run. "The Encyclopedia of New York" ($19.29) by editors of New York Magazine compiles an A-to-Z collection of the city’s history, innovations, and fun tidbits—including the origin of Scrabble in Jackson Heights. "Historic Black Brooklyn: 400 Years of Struggle and Hope" ($50) by Brian Merlis and Clarence Taylor thoroughly examines the legacy and accomplishments of Brooklyn’s Black community, highlighting key events and contributions from the Abolitionist Movement to present-day achievements.

article_content: George Osborne’s opposition is seen as the main obstacle to introducing a plastic bag tax in England, according to Liberal Democrats. At their conference, Lib Dems backed a motion calling for a levy on all single-use plastic bags, with profits supporting community food projects. Senior party members aimed to overcome what they called a Treasury 'log jam' that has repeatedly stalled proposals to charge for plastic bags to reduce their use. A recent poll by the Break the Bag Habit coalition showed 56% of respondents supported a small charge for disposable bags. Official statistics reveal retailers gave out around 350 million more bags last year, despite Prime Minister David Cameron urging significant reductions. Lib Dems claim former Conservative Environment Secretary Caroline Spelman supported a bag levy but met with Treasury resistance—a claim the Treasury denies. Following recent controversies over taxes on items like pasties and caravans, it is suggested the Treasury is reluctant to add costs for low-income families. Lib Dem environment spokesman Andrew George hopes the party’s new policy will bring the issue back for consideration. He said the Prime Minister’s office has shown some support, but efforts have been overruled by the Treasury. George stated the party should keep pushing to resolve the deadlock. Treasury sources reportedly rejected the claim that Osborne is blocking the policy, commenting, 'All ideas are on the table, and the Lib Dems know that.' Wales already charges shoppers 5p for carrier bags, with the money benefiting good causes. Ireland introduced a levy in 2002, leading to large reductions in plastic bag use. Last year, David Cameron called the level of bag usage 'unacceptable' and suggested a 5% reduction was needed. However, the number of bags issued rose by about 5% to 6.75 billion in 2011-12. Andrew George highlighted the harmful effects of excess landfill and pollution caused by plastic bags, arguing that alternatives are readily available and a levy is a simple, effective solution. Lib Dem activist Justine McGuinness said she changed her view on the levy after seeing cleaner hedgerows in Ireland, where bags are no longer discarded in the environment. Lib Dems propose a 5p to 10p levy per bag to encourage shoppers to plan ahead and use reusable bags. They emphasize that the intention is not to penalize those who have no other option, but to influence public behavior. The motion was approved at the Lib Dem conference in Brighton, following McGuinness’s observations about behavior change in Ireland, as evidence of the policy’s effectiveness.

لیکن انہیں خزانے کی مخالفت کا سامنا کرنا پڑا، جس سے خزانہ انکار کرتا ہے۔ پاستی اور کیراوان پر حالیہ متنازعہ ٹیکس کے بعد، کہا جاتا ہے کہ خزانہ کم آمدنی والے خاندانوں پر مزید اخراجات ڈالنے سے گریزاں ہے۔ لِب ڈیمز کے ماحولیات کے ترجمان اینڈریو جارج کو امید ہے کہ پارٹی کی نئی پالیسی اس معاملے کو دوبارہ زیر بحث لائے گی۔ ان کے مطابق وزیر اعظم کے دفتر نے کچھ حمایت ظاہر کی ہے لیکن خزانے نے کوششوں کو متعدد بار مسترد کیا۔ جارج کا کہنا ہے کہ جماعت کو مسئلہ حل ہونے تک کوششیں جاری رکھنی چاہئیں۔ خزانے کے ذرائع نے اوسبورن پر پالیسی روکنے کے الزام کو رد کرتے ہوئے کہا کہ 'تمام آئیڈیاز زیر غور ہیں اور لِب ڈیمز اس سے واقف ہیں۔' ویلز میں خریداروں سے ہر بیگ پر پانچ پنس وصول کیا جاتا ہے جس کی آمدنی اچھے مقاصد کے لیے خرچ کی جاتی ہے۔ آئرلینڈ نے 2002 سے بیگ ٹیکس نافذ کیا جس سے بیگ کے استعمال میں نمایاں کمی آئی۔ گزشتہ سال ڈیوڈ کیمرون نے بیگ کے استعمال کو 'ناقابل قبول' قرار دیا اور پانچ فیصد کمی کی ضرورت بتائی۔ لیکن 2011-12 میں بیگ کی تعداد تقریباً پانچ فیصد بڑھی اور 6.75 ارب تک پہنچ گئی۔ اینڈریو جارج نے کہا کہ پلاسٹک بیگ کے زیادہ استعمال کی وجہ سے لینڈ فل اور آلودگی کے مسائل شدید ہو رہے ہیں۔ ان کے مطابق متبادل آسانی سے دستیاب ہیں اور لیوی ایک سادہ، مؤثر حل ہے۔ لِب ڈیمز کی کارکن جسٹین میک گینس نے بتایا کہ آئرلینڈ میں واضح بہتری دیکھ کر ان کی رائے بدل گئی، جہاں اب پلاسٹک بیگ کھیتوں یا جھاڑیوں میں نہیں ملتے۔ لِب ڈیمز فی بیگ 5 سے 10 پنس لیوی تجویز کر رہے ہیں تاکہ لوگ شاپنگ سے پہلے منصوبہ بندی کریں اور دوبارہ استعمال ہونے والے بیگ ساتھ لائیں۔ ان کا کہنا ہے کہ اس پالیسی کا مقصد اُن لوگوں کو سزا دینا نہیں جن کے پاس کوئی اور آپشن نہیں، بلکہ سماجی رویے میں تبدیلی لانا ہے۔ برائٹن میں پارٹی کانفرنس میں اس قرارداد کو منظور کر لیا گیا، جس میں میک گینس کے آئرلینڈ سے متاثرہ مشاہدات کو اس پالیسی کی کامیابی کی دلیل کے طور پر پیش کیا گیا۔

article_content: These incredible images capture mushrooms that appear magical, though the effect is a natural phenomenon rather than something supernatural. Bioluminescent mushrooms, about 65 species among approximately 85,000 in the fungi kingdom, emit a green glow due to a chemical reaction. This occurs when luciferin, a light-emitting pigment, interacts with the enzyme luciferase. The glow can be seen both day and night but is most striking after dark. Photographer Taylor Lockwood, 68, originally from New Orleans, has traveled worldwide—including to Brazil, China, and Madagascar—to photograph these fascinating luminous fungi. He recalls moving to Northern California thirty years ago and being inspired by the mushrooms he found outside his cabin. Purchasing a camera soon after, Lockwood began documenting his discoveries. One of his most memorable moments was photographing the glowing Mycena lucentipes under the full moon in Brazil. Lockwood describes working at night as feeling like a 'vampire', often needing insect repellent due to the conditions. Despite potential dangers from local wildlife, the excitement of seeing and capturing bioluminescent mushrooms makes the effort worthwhile. The phenomenon also appears in other species, such as jellyfish, squid, and scorpions.

The Lotus Formula One team has stated that its main financial priority is the development of its car, rather than paying high salaries to drivers. Driver Kimi Raikkonen announced last week that he would be leaving Lotus to rejoin Ferrari in the 2014 season, citing unpaid salary as his reason for departure.

Lotus, owned by Luxembourg-based investment group Genii Capital, responded by explaining its focus on funding car development, even if it means losing driving talent like Raikkonen. This year, Raikkonen delivered Lotus' only victory, and both he and the team currently occupy fourth place in the driver and constructor standings.

"Our suppliers and key people who develop the car were our priority — maybe not Kimi," said Lotus team principal Eric Boullier to the official F1 website. "Kimi was in a similar position last year, but the issue was resolved by the end of the season. Genii planned the same for this year, but we've been late in paying him, which made him upset."

Boullier added that managing cash flow is challenging due to fixed costs and the lack of sufficient independent revenue, which requires decision-making on spending priorities.

Genii took full control of the team (originally Toleman, Benetton, Renault since 1981) from Renault in 2011. While ownership by private investment rather than a car manufacturer brings financial risks, Boullier insists Lotus is not in a financial crisis.

"Red Bull and Mercedes have their company sponsors, but Genii loans the money," Boullier explained. "Seventy-five percent of Lotus's debt comes from Genii, and they could write it off as sponsorship. Our debt is similar to that of most other teams."

Lotus has been looking for major sponsors to increase its budget, aiming to follow the business models of teams like Red Bull and McLaren. Boullier emphasized that attracting the best people and long-term planning in Formula One requires increased sponsorship. Genii aimed to elevate the team's status within five years, and Lotus is now planning for the next phase.

لوٹس فارمولا ون ٹیم کا کہنا ہے کہ ان کی بنیادی مالی ترجیح گاڑی کی ترقی ہے، نہ کہ ڈرائیورز کو بھاری معاوضے دینا۔ ڈرائیور کیمی رائیکونن نے گزشتہ ہفتے اعلان کیا تھا کہ وہ لوٹس چھوڑ کر 2014 میں فراری کو دوبارہ جوائن کریں گے کیونکہ ان کی تنخواہ ادا نہیں کی گئی۔

لوٹس، جو لکسمبرگ کی سرمایہ کاری کمپنی جینی کیپٹل کی ملکیت ہے، نے وضاحت کی کہ ان کی توجہ گاڑی کی ترقی پر ہے چاہے اس کا مطلب اہم ڈرائیونگ ٹیلنٹ کو کھونا ہو۔ اس سال، رائیکونن نے لوٹس کے لئے واحد فتح حاصل کی اور اس وقت وہ اور ٹیم دونوں اپنے اپنے اسٹینڈنگز میں چوتھے نمبر پر ہیں۔

"ہماری ترجیح سپلائرز اور وہ اہم لوگ ہیں جو گاڑی کو ڈیولپ کرتے ہیں — شاید کیمی نہیں،" لوٹس کے پرنسپل ایرک بولیر نے ایف ون کی آفیشل ویب سائٹ کو بتایا۔ "کیمی پچھلے سال بھی اسی صورتحال میں تھے، لیکن سیزن کے آخر تک مسئلہ حل ہو گیا تھا۔ جینی نے اسی طرح کا پلان اس سال بھی بنایا تھا لیکن ہم انہیں وقت پر تنخواہ نہیں دے سکے، اس لئے وہ ناراض ہو گئے۔"

بولیر نے مزید کہا کہ کیش فلو مینج کرنا مشکل ہے کیونکہ اخراجات فکسڈ ہیں اور آمدنی ناکافی ہے، اس لئے یہ طے کرنا پڑتا ہے کہ پیسے کہاں خرچ کرنے ہیں۔

جینی نے 2011 میں ٹیم (جو پہلے ٹولمین، بینٹن اور رینالٹ رہی ہے) کو رینالٹ سے مکمل طور پر حاصل کر لیا۔ اگرچہ پرائیویٹ سرمایہ کاری کی مالکیت کمپنی کو مالی لحاظ سے زیادہ خطرات میں ڈالتی ہے، بولیر نے کہا کہ لوٹس کسی مالی بحران میں نہیں ہے۔

"ریڈ بل اور مرسڈیز جیسے برانڈز ٹیموں کو سپانسر کرتے ہیں، جبکہ جینی رقم قرض دیتی ہے،" بولیر نے بتایا۔ "لوٹس کے قرض کا 75 فیصد جینی سے ہے اور اگر وہ چاہے تو اسے سپانسرشپ کا نام دے سکتی ہے۔ ہمارا قرض باقی ٹیموں جیسا ہے۔"

article_content: In October 1988, President Ronald Reagan and First Lady Nancy Reagan presented economist Milton Friedman with the Presidential Medal of Freedom at the White House. Renowned for his advocacy of free-market economics, Friedman's influence extended beyond academia in the 1960s when he taught at UCLA, a university aligned with the University of Chicago’s market-oriented philosophy. While in California, Friedman developed a friendship with conservative businessman Henry Salvatori, who arranged an introduction to Governor Ronald Reagan. During their meeting, Friedman and Reagan connected over shared viewpoints on educational policy—especially regarding increased tuition and the use of school vouchers, which would let parents redirect public funds to private schools. Reagan had already encountered these concepts in Friedman's book 'Capitalism and Freedom.' Friedman’s alliance with Reagan deepened as he supported the governor’s Proposition 1, aimed at capping state spending, although the measure ultimately failed. The push for fiscal reform persisted, resulting in the passage of Proposition 13, which slashed property taxes, set the stage for the 'Reagan Revolution,' and influenced national policies toward deregulation and reduced government spending. Jennifer Burns’s recent biography, 'Milton Friedman: The Last Conservative,' maps Friedman’s ascent from humble origins in New Jersey to worldwide acclaim. Burns discusses how Friedman, who often identified with classical liberalism—a belief in individual liberties, limited government, and free trade—came to be associated with the 'neoliberal' economic movement. Friedman critiqued both excessive government control and strict laissez-faire, advocating for a balanced approach: government should promote competition and protect against distress, but avoid overstepping. His ideas gained traction as faith in Keynesian economics faltered during the high-inflation and unemployment years of the 1970s. Following the 2008 financial crisis and increased economic inequality, both Democrats and Republicans began to rethink their commitment to free-market principles. Today, some in the Republican Party embrace interventionist and protectionist strategies—contrasting earlier support for economic liberalism. Politicians like Marco Rubio and Josh Hawley now advocate for policies involving more government action in the economy. Despite these shifts, Friedman’s impact persists. He transformed the role of central banks, emphasizing rules-based monetary policy and highlighting the dangers of central bank inaction during crises like the Great Depression, as detailed in his work with Anna Schwartz. Ideas that Friedman advanced, such as universal basic income and the negative income tax (which inspired the Earned Income Tax Credit), remain relevant in policy discussions. As Jennifer Burns’s book concludes, even as the era of 'neoliberalism' wanes, Friedman’s influence continues to shape economic thought and policy debates.

Being mindful of where you order french fries can significantly affect your calorie intake. Whether topped with chili and cheese or simply sprinkled with salt, french fries remain a beloved American snack. However, the nutrition content of fries varies widely between restaurants, as detailed in the book 'Eat This, Not That! 2013: The No-Diet Weight Loss Solution.' According to the book, a single order can differ by as much as 1,200 calories.

For example, McDonald's small fries are among the healthier choices at 230 calories and 11 grams of fat per serving. In stark contrast, Chili’s Texas Cheese Fries with Chili and Ranch pack 2,150 calories, 144 grams of fat, and 6,080 milligrams of sodium. If you enjoy cheese on your fries, Steak 'n' Shake’s small Bacon Cheese French Fries offer a lower-calorie option at 360 calories and 20 grams of fat.

The 'Eat This, Not That!' team notes that thicker-cut steak fries can be a better choice, as they tend to absorb less oil, reducing fat content. Yet, TGI Friday's Parmesan Steak Fries have 660 calories and 49 grams of fat, nearly double the fat of their regular fries. Similarly, Five Guys’ large portion contains 1,474 calories due to its size, while KFC’s potato wedges offer a more modest 290 calories and 15 grams of fat, including only 2.5 grams of saturated fat.

For curly fry enthusiasts, Jack in the Box’s small seasoned curly fries are among the lowest in calories, whereas Arby’s version comes with a lot more sodium. David Zinczenko, editor-in-chief of Men's Health and author of 'Eat This, Not That,' emphasizes moderation. He notes that while occasional fries aren’t harmful, regular consumption contributes to weight gain, as research shows a direct link between frequent fry consumption and added weight. Notably, more than half of American potatoes are deep-fried before being sold, and one out of every six restaurant orders includes fries.

Though sweet potato fries are often considered a healthier alternative, the Cheesecake Factory’s version has 400 more calories than their regular fries. For a better option, try Burger King's small sweet potato fries, which have significantly fewer calories.

In summary, not all fries are created equal. Paying attention to portion size and where you order can help you make better choices for your health.

article_content: Teresa Giudice and her husband, Joe Giudice, have been charged in a 39-count federal indictment for financial fraud, including conspiracy to commit mail and wire fraud, bank fraud, making false statements on loan applications, and bankruptcy fraud. Their television show, 'The Real Housewives of New Jersey,' may be cancelled as Bravo responds to the negative publicity generated by the charges. Teresa was seen out in Paterson, New Jersey, with her daughter Milania, appearing calm despite the situation. However, behind the scenes, her future is uncertain. Bravo executives are reportedly concerned about public reaction to the case, and plans for a possible spin-off featuring the Giudices have been cancelled. Teresa and Joe were released on $1 million bail after appearing in federal court. They surrendered their passports and are restricted to travel in New Jersey and New York. Joe Giudice, an Italian national, may face deportation if convicted. The couple is accused of submitting fraudulent mortgage and loan documents between 2001 and 2008 and hiding assets in their 2009 bankruptcy filing. Prosecutors allege they exaggerated their income when applying for loans and then concealed assets after their television debut. In their bankruptcy paperwork, the Giudices claimed to be $11 million in debt, listing substantial amounts owed to creditors including $2.2 million in mortgages, $13,000 to luxury retailers, and almost $12,000 to a fertility clinic. Conviction on the most serious charges could result in up to 30 years in prison and a $1 million fine per count. In total, they could face more than 50 years in prison. Teresa expressed gratitude to supporters on social media and stated her commitment to her family during this period.

Australian Treasurer Joe Hockey faces a challenging year, with government revenue reported to have fallen by an additional $6.2 billion over the past six months. On Monday, Mr. Hockey is expected to deliver his mid-year economic update, revealing that projections for federal budget receipts have declined to $379.5 billion, down from $385.7 billion at the time of the budget's release in May. The update is set to highlight ongoing fiscal pressures due to falling commodity prices, especially iron ore, and will point to tens of billions of dollars in lost revenue over the next four years. Deficits during this period are expected to nearly double to $100 billion, underlining the need for potentially unpopular reforms regarding tax and government spending.

Mr. Hockey has warned of possible job losses and a decline in Australian prosperity if the budget is not used to offset the significant fall in the terms of trade, with iron ore prices dropping to $60 per tonne—half of what they were a year ago—which represents the largest terms of trade decline since records began in 1959. Falling income tax revenue, increased unemployment, and soft commodity prices are main contributors to the worsening financial position. Some anticipated budget savings have also been reduced due to concessions needed to pass legislation, such as efforts to abolish the mining tax and adjust other measures for greater public acceptance.

The forthcoming economic update will include Treasury's latest forecasts at a time when economists, including Westpac’s Andrew Hanlan, predict further interest rate cuts by the Reserve Bank of Australia, whose cash rate is already at a record low. Recent national accounts indicate slow economic growth below three percent and a jobless rate that reached 6.3 percent in November—the highest in 12 years and above prior estimations. Economists from National Australia Bank now expect unemployment to peak at 6.75 percent.

On a positive note, inflation is expected to remain subdued, aided by the cancellation of the carbon tax, which has lowered electricity prices. Finance Minister Mathias Cormann has stated, despite criticisms from the Labor opposition of overly pessimistic forecasts, that the government might not have reduced revenue expectations enough. He also confirmed there are no plans for large new budget cuts to offset lower revenue. Reports indicate that the foreign aid program will be reduced in the forthcoming budget update.

article_content: Jevon Wooden, CEO of Brightmind Consulting Group and a veteran of the U.S. Army, underscores the significance of intentional self-reflection in strong leadership. He believes leaders enhance their effectiveness and communication skills when they invest time in better understanding themselves. Wooden suggests carving out quiet, uninterrupted periods to ponder critical questions regarding communication, team growth, stress management, and defining success. Such introspection, whether during a technology-free walk or in another calm setting, can uncover valuable self-insights. Actively seeking honest feedback is crucial. Wooden advises leaders to directly request feedback, hold individual meetings, utilize anonymous digital platforms, and conduct after-action reviews—a practice common in the military—to help spot behavioral patterns they might overlook. He also advocates for keeping a journal to record personal reactions and experiences. The format isn't important: whether writing or voice notes, the goal is consistent reflection to improve future responses. Wooden maintains that deepening self-awareness strengthens leaders’ connections with their teams. Leaders who skillfully manage their emotions foster a more supportive, effective workplace culture and help teams handle adversity with steadiness. He identifies self-awareness as the cornerstone of emotional intelligence, which underpins self-management and social capability. Wooden encourages leaders to embrace self-discovery, emphasizing that the journey benefits both individuals and their teams by building resilience, productivity, and collaboration. The article concludes by referencing the Forbes Coaches Council, a network for top business and career coaches.

article_content: The Collins Dictionary has declared 'geek' as its 2013 Word of the Year. Although the term dates back to the 19th century, editors highlighted its new positive meaning—now portraying someone deeply enthusiastic and skilled in any area, not just computers. This year’s shortlist also featured the words 'selfie', 'twerking', 'bitcoin', 'phablet', 'fracking', 'Plebgate', 'Harlem Shake', and 'olinguito'. Despite bitcoin's dramatic increase in value, it did not win. Miley Cyrus helped popularize 'twerking', and 'fracking' garnered attention after high-profile environmental protests, including one with designer Vivienne Westwood. 'Phablet' is used for a device larger than a phone but smaller than a tablet, while 'Plebgate' references the political scandal involving Andrew Mitchell and Downing Street security. 'Harlem Shake' refers to a viral dance trend. 'Olinguito' describes a newly discovered mammal from Colombia and Ecuador, notable as the Western Hemisphere’s first new herbivore species found in 35 years. Although Collins will include these entries in its online dictionary, not all will be printed in the physical edition.

article_content: The advent of programmatic advertising has ushered in an era of precise targeting, ad personalization, and contextual ads. Mobile apps and digital platforms are working diligently to engage audiences and deliver relevant advertisements. Artificial intelligence (AI) tools in AdTech have become a game-changer, enabling apps and advertisers to leverage advanced technology and gain a competitive edge. These innovations have reshaped how digital platforms attract users and generate revenue. This article explores some of the leading AI tools in AdTech that improve the programmatic advertising experience overall. Criteo is a notable AI tool in the AdTech landscape. It employs predictive targeting, utilizing AI algorithms to anticipate user behavior and ensure ads reach the appropriate audience. This enhances the relevancy of served ads and increases engagement. Additionally, Criteo enables dynamic creative optimization by analyzing user preferences and historical interactions in real-time, allowing ad creatives to align with individual user interests. This makes Criteo a top choice for digital marketers. Criteo also optimizes campaigns across various platforms to maximize both reach and engagement, a crucial factor for maintaining consistent brand-user interactions. Skai offers an AI-powered suite for market insights, strategic planning, omnichannel media activation, and more. By helping publishers analyze vast data streams and identify patterns, Skai enables AdTech professionals to optimize campaigns easily across channels, improving return on investment and efficiency. Skai further refines audience targeting through segmentation and precision, enhancing user engagement. Its integration of AI into every aspect of the ad campaign—automating insights, optimizing performance, and facilitating personalization—makes Skai influential in the evolution of digital advertising. The Google Marketing Platform is another transformative force in AdTech, utilizing AI to analyze large data volumes and uncover trends in customer behavior. Its analytic capabilities provide advertisers with actionable insights while enabling real-time monitoring of campaign performance, audience engagement, and conversion rates. The platform dynamically adjusts strategies to reflect changing market conditions, ensuring ongoing campaign relevance. Google Marketing Platform excels in marketing personalization by tailoring ads to individual preferences, thus enhancing engagement and conversion potential. The ability to analyze cross-channel data offers comprehensive insights into the customer journey. Albert AI stands out for its advanced data analysis and optimization features. It can process large data sets, identify patterns, and help advertisers make informed, data-driven decisions. Albert AI is highly effective at real-time optimization, dynamically adjusting ad placements, budgets, and targeting using historical data. Its cognitive automation capabilities allow for the continuous refinement of ad creatives and messaging to boost engagement and optimize ad revenue. Albert AI updates campaign strategies based on emerging trends, helping campaigns remain relevant and effective. TensorFlow, an open-source library, powers advanced analytics within the AdTech industry. It enables the development of robust applications capable of analyzing massive datasets for valuable insights into user behavior, preferences, and trends. TensorFlow’s strength lies in building complex neural networks that enhance ad targeting and optimization, as well as solutions for fraud detection. Its customizable nature allows companies to tailor machine learning models to their specific needs, leveraging a wealth of community resources, tutorials, and pre-trained models to accelerate AI solution deployment. Framer.ai provides user-friendly features and drag-and-drop functionality. Advertisers and publishers can use Framer AI for AI-generated website designs, enabling quick creation of landing pages and microsites tailored to diverse campaigns and industries. This flexibility lets advertisers adjust landing pages for specific objectives, such as lead generation or product promotion, and allows publishers to optimize sites for optimal ad placement and higher click-through rates. Framer’s code-free approach empowers advertisers to create dynamic, interactive landing pages without relying on development teams. Firebase’s AI-powered extensions are making a notable impact in AdTech. Advertisers can incorporate AI-driven chatbots seamlessly into apps and websites to respond to user inquiries in real-time, boosting conversions and customer satisfaction. The PaLM API enables automatic text summarization for crafting concise ad copy, while the Convert Text to Speech extension diversifies content formats, assisting publishers in creating audio-based content for broader audience reach. The Transcribe Speech to Text feature helps transcribe audio files, improving ad targeting and relevance. The AdTech landscape is evolving rapidly, and AI tools are integral to this transformation. These leading AI solutions demonstrate not only increased efficiency but also expanded creative and personalization possibilities. As AI continues to evolve, it will become essential rather than optional for digital advertising, prompting marketers to focus on how best to harness AI’s potential to create meaningful experiences that resonate with audiences. article_content: After scoring 90 runs in Colombo, James Taylor felt more frustrated than fulfilled, reflecting on his limited opportunities with England despite consistent performances in domestic cricket. Having played only a handful of ODIs and Tests, Taylor feels overlooked by the selectors. As the England squad prepares for their fifth ODI against Sri Lanka, leadership questions persist. Alastair Cook, returning from a one-match suspension for a slow over-rate, and Eoin Morgan are both being considered for the ODI captaincy, though debates continue over the best leadership choice. England only arrived at a promising batting order in the fourth match, but Cook’s reinstatement might disrupt that progress. Selectors are still debating Cook’s role and seem indecisive about alternatives like Alex Hales. Cook’s ODI captaincy record—an average close to 40, strike rate around 80, and a decent win ratio—is solid by England’s standards. However, many supporters expect the team to compete aggressively on the world stage, and current performance metrics may not be enough for World Cup success. Eoin Morgan’s elevated performance as acting captain, including a rapid 62 in 47 balls, indicates he could invigorate the team. While his recent form strengthens his candidacy, England’s selectors have yet to fully commit to this change. The selection approach remains cautious, as seen when James Tredwell was omitted despite being suited to slow, turning pitches. Ben Stokes, favored instead, struggled, leading to frustration over missed opportunities. England’s World Cup prospects might improve with bolder, merit-based selections. Elsewhere in cricket, Michael Clarke was widely supported after retiring hurt during a Test against India, especially following the passing of Phil Hughes, which shifted public sentiment in his favor. Meanwhile, Kevin Pietersen continues to voice criticism of England’s management, particularly coach Peter Moores. However, former player Andrew Flintoff has publicly encouraged Pietersen to move past old conflicts and focus on the future.

article_content: Britain's response to the initial outbreak of COVID-19 in 2020 was too slow, according to the country's chief medical adviser, Chris Whitty. Speaking at the independent inquiry into the UK's handling of the pandemic, Whitty reflected on the early days and expressed particular concern about the negative consequences of measures like lockdowns, school closures, and isolation—especially for the most disadvantaged and those who live alone. He noted there was a difficult balance to strike between acting too soon and waiting too long. Whitty clarified that, contrary to suggestions from inquiry lawyer Hugo Keith, he did not caution the government against possibly overreacting to the pandemic. Instead, he emphasized to officials that severe consequences would follow if no action were taken. Looking back, he admitted, 'with hindsight, we acted a bit too late during the first wave.' However, he also acknowledged that the available choices at the time were all problematic. The inquiry, launched in 2021 by former Prime Minister Boris Johnson, is examining the nation's handling of COVID-19 to learn important lessons. During the pandemic, Whitty became widely recognized for his frequent appearances at government news briefings, alongside Johnson and other officials. With more than 232,000 COVID-related deaths, the UK has seen one of Europe’s highest fatality rates. Many bereaved families believe that policymakers failed them, resulting in needless loss and suffering. Revelations that parties were held at Prime Minister Johnson’s residence in breach of lockdown rules were a significant scandal and contributed to his resignation in 2022. Currently, the inquiry is focused on exploring decisions made during the pandemic, with both Boris Johnson and current Prime Minister Rishi Sunak, who was Treasury chief during the crisis, expected to testify. The UK’s national lockdown began in March 2020, shortly after similar measures were enacted in France, Spain, and Italy. Whitty also pointed out that the government’s existing flu pandemic plan was quickly realized to be inadequate for the challenges posed by COVID-19. He described the idea of having a ready-to-use, effective pandemic strategy as 'optimistic at best.'

article_content: Nintendo is developing a live-action film adaptation of its acclaimed video game franchise, The Legend of Zelda, the company announced Wednesday. Financing for the project will come from Sony Pictures Entertainment and Nintendo. The film will be directed by Wes Ball, known for the upcoming Planet of the Apes film, and will be co-produced by Nintendo and Arad Productions Inc., led by Avi Arad, who is known for producing the Spider-Man live-action films. This project is part of Kyoto-based Nintendo’s broader strategy to expand its business through theme parks, merchandising, and movies, aiming to increase hardware and software sales across its platforms. This approach has already proven successful—The Super Mario Bros. Movie, released earlier this year, earned more than $1.3 billion and attracted nearly 170 million viewers worldwide. Nintendo President Shuntaro Furukawa, speaking to reporters online, expressed satisfaction with the performance of the Super Mario film, which marked the company's first experience as a direct producer. The release date for the Zelda movie has yet to be announced. Shigeru Miyamoto, the Nintendo executive credited with decades of creative innovation, said the movie will be released only when it meets high standards, emphasizing the importance of satisfying Zelda's dedicated fanbase. Miyamoto also revealed that the project has been in development for ten years. On Tuesday, Nintendo reported an 18% increase in net profits for the first half of its fiscal year, reaching nearly 271.3 billion yen (about $1.8 billion), up from 230 billion yen the previous year. Officials noted that the success of the Super Mario film has contributed to higher sales of both Switch consoles and Mario-themed game software. The newly released Super Mario Bros. Wonder has set a record by selling 4.3 million copies in just two weeks. The latest Zelda game, Tears of the Kingdom, has also achieved strong sales, and Nintendo hopes the planned movie will benefit from the franchise’s popularity. The Switch console, now in its seventh year, continues to perform well, according to the company. Nintendo aims to grow its reach by introducing more people to its intellectual properties through official stores, pop-ups, theme parks, and movies. Nintendo World has opened at Universal Studios in Hollywood, with another location planned for Orlando. In Japan, the Universal Studios park will add a Donkey Kong area next year. Nintendo is also preparing to open a museum highlighting its history and legacy in Kyoto in March next year. Reporter Yuri Kageyama contributed to this story. She is active on X (formerly Twitter) at https://twitter.com/yurikageyama.

article_content: Electric vehicles (EVs) are becoming a more frequent sight on the roads, introducing buyers to some new factors to consider. While range—the distance an EV can travel on one charge—is most people’s first concern, another key factor is battery voltage. Automakers often call attention to battery voltage in their marketing. For instance, Hyundai highlights the 800-volt system found in models like the EV6, which doubles the voltage of the Tesla Model Y’s 400-volt system. But what practical difference does this make for drivers? Essentially, voltage can be thought of like water pressure in a pipe: higher voltage allows energy to flow into the battery more quickly, requiring less current. With greater voltage, less energy is lost as heat, leading to faster and more efficient charging. Charging an electric car involves three main measurements: volts (similar to pressure), amps (the amount flowing at once), and watts (the total power, calculated as volts times amps). Battery capacity is measured in kilowatt-hours (kWh), with larger capacities offering more stored energy. To speed up charging, you either increase voltage or current. However, boosting current increases heat and energy loss, so raising voltage is the more efficient route to fast charging. This is why high-voltage EVs can deliver more power to their motors while preserving battery health. Switching to higher-voltage systems has costs: manufacturers need to redesign vehicles with components that can safely handle the higher voltage, raising production expenses. This is the main reason 800V batteries are not standard in all EVs yet. Nonetheless, automakers like Hyundai, Kia, Porsche, Audi, and Lucid are adopting higher-voltage systems that allow for rapid charging speeds—up to 350kW, which is the fastest widely available. New entries, such as the upcoming Kia EV9, feature this technology, although some upcoming, more affordable Kia models will retain the older 400V systems. Some vehicles, like the Hummer EV, incorporate innovative solutions such as a dual-layer battery to achieve fast charging speeds with a 400V setup. Over time, however, experts anticipate the industry shift toward widespread 800V (or higher) systems as technology and economies of scale improve. Although not yet universal, the benefits of high-voltage EVs—including faster charging, reduced energy waste, and improved battery life—suggest they are the likely future of electric mobility.

جو ٹیسلا ماڈل وائی کے 400 وولٹ سسٹم سے دگنا ہے۔ مگر حقیقت میں یہ فیچر ڈرائیور کے لیے کیا فرق ڈالتا ہے؟ وولٹیج کو سادہ طور پر پانی کے پریشر کی طرح سمجھیں: جتنا زیادہ وولٹیج ہو گا، اتنی ہی تیز توانائی کم کرنٹ کے ساتھ بیٹری تک پہنچ سکتی ہے۔ اس سے کم توانائی حرارت کی صورت میں ضائع ہوتی ہے اور چارجنگ تیز و مؤثر ہو جاتی ہے۔ الیکٹرک گاڑی چارج کرتے ہوئے تین بنیادی پیمائشیں سامنے آتی ہیں: وولٹ (پریشر کی طرح)، ایمپئر (کتنی مقدار گزر رہی ہے)، اور واٹ (کل طاقت، یعنی وولٹ اور ایمپئر کا حاصل ضرب)۔ بیٹری کی گنجائش کلو واٹ آور (kWh) میں ماپی جاتی ہے اور بڑی بیٹری زیادہ توانائی سٹور کر سکتی ہے۔ تیز چارجنگ کے لیے یا تو وولٹیج بڑھانا چاہیے یا کرنٹ، لیکن کرنٹ بڑھانے سے زیادہ حرارت اور توانائی ضائع ہوتی ہے، اس لیے زیادہ تر وولٹیج بڑھانا مؤثر سمجھا جاتا ہے۔ اسی وجہ سے ہائی وولٹیج والی EVs اپنی موٹرز کو زیادہ طاقت دیتی ہیں اور بیٹری بھی زیادہ دیر تک اچھی رہتی ہے۔ ہائی وولٹیج سسٹم اپنانے کا خرچ زیادہ ہے: کمپنیوں کو گاڑی کے اہم حصے دوبارہ ڈیزائن کرنا پڑتے ہیں جو بڑے وولٹیج سنبھال سکیں، اس لیے یہ مہنگا پڑتا ہے۔ یہی بڑی وجہ ہے کہ ابھی ہر EV میں 800V بیٹریز نہیں آتیں۔ اس کے باوجود ہنڈائی، کیا، پورشے، آوڈی اور لوسڈ جیسی کمپنیاں اب ہائی وولٹیج سسٹم استعمال کر رہی ہیں، جو تیز رفتار چارجنگ (350kW تک) ممکن بناتی ہیں۔ جیسے کیا EV9 میں بھی یہ فیچر ہوگا، لیکن کیا کے بعض سستے ماڈلز ابھی پرانا 400V سسٹم ہی رکھیں گے۔ کچھ گاڑیاں، جیسا کہ ہممر EV، دو پرت والی بیٹری جیسی ترکیب سے 400V سسٹم میں بھی تیز چارجنگ کر لیتی ہیں۔ لیکن وقت کے ساتھ امید کی جاتی ہے کہ صنعت مکمل طور پر 800V یا اس سے بھی زیادہ وولٹیج پر چلی جائے گی جیسے ٹیکنالوجی اور قیمتیں بہتر ہوں گی۔ اگرچہ سب گاڑیوں میں یہ خصوصیات ابھی نہیں آئیں، ہائی وولٹیج EVs کے فائدے — تیز چارجنگ، کم توانائی کا ضیاع، بہتر بیٹری لائف — مستقبل میں الیکٹرک گاڑیوں کے لیے اہم ہیں۔

article_content: ITV executive Peter Fincham has recognized that more needs to be done to engage older viewers in television programming. He noted that although the industry has often focused on attracting younger audiences, it is the older demographic that drives viewing figures and deserves content that meets their interests. Fincham referred to successes like the BBC drama 'Last Tango in Halifax' and the popular film 'The Best Exotic Marigold Hotel' as evidence of the strong appeal of programming for mature audiences. To better serve this group, ITV is launching the family entertainment show 'Amazing Greys,' hosted by 69-year-old veteran presenter Angela Rippon. The show will feature young contestants competing against accomplished pensioners, highlighting ITV’s commitment to including older viewers. In an interview with the Radio Times, Fincham said, 'The simple truth, not to be resisted, is that as people go through life they watch more television. There’s no point in swimming against the tide. So we make programmes that appeal to that audience – though not at the expense of others.' He explained that television was previously preoccupied with youth, but this is changing as audiences age. Statistics show that 54% of BBC1 viewers are over 55, and 59% of BBC2 viewers are in the same age group. ITV1’s audience is similar, though the network is less public with its data. Presenter Michael Burke also observes the shift for older TV personalities, noting that many who were once sidelined are now returning to prominence. Well-known figures such as Mary Berry, David Dimbleby, and Angela Rippon are among those benefiting from this change. Talent agent Sue Ayton remarked on the industry’s new approach, noting that networks are now receptive to programs aimed at older audiences. Angela Rippon commented, 'Television has finally realised you need maturity and experience alongside youth and beauty. It’s finally come of age.'

article_content: Did you just get a drone for the holidays? If so, you're joining thousands of new drone owners this season, according to industry leaders. Once you've unpacked your high-tech gift, it's important to check out the Federal Aviation Administration's (FAA) guidelines to avoid risky situations—like getting too close to a Boeing 747 or accidentally injuring someone, both of which have actually happened. This month, three drone associations partnered with the FAA to launch the 'Know Before You Fly' campaign, which promotes safe drone operation. To help you stay out of trouble, here are the essential guidelines you need to know: 1. Don't use your drone to get close-up shots of airplanes in flight. It's illegal to fly recreational drones higher than 400 feet or within five miles of an airport. The FAA has already recorded 25 incidents where small drones came dangerously close to manned aircraft. Pilots have even reported drones flying thousands of feet in the air, sometimes just a few dozen feet from their planes. Remember the famous emergency landing on the Hudson River after a bird strike? Imagine if that bird were a drone. 2. Planning to take your drone to a sports game? Leave it at home. While it might be tempting to capture aerial views of stadiums or racetracks, drones should be kept away from large crowds. The FAA warns that drone blades can cause serious injuries, as seen in incidents like a TGI Friday's marketing event where a drone accidentally injured a photographer. 3. Always keep your drone away from power lines and sensitive areas. The FAA advises avoiding places like power stations, water treatment facilities, correctional facilities, heavy traffic roads, and government buildings. In one recent case in Australia, a man crashed his drone into power lines during a police operation, nearly hitting an officer, according to CNET. Keeping your drone within your line of sight at all times is key. 4. Using your drone for business purposes without an FAA permit is illegal. Whether you want to sell photos or videos, provide security services, or make a movie, you need official approval. The FAA has even fined individuals, including a $10,000 penalty for using a drone to film a promotional video. 5. Respect people's privacy. The Academy of Model Aeronautics urges drone users not to secretly photograph or spy on others. Privacy concerns are significant, as highlighted by Sen. Rand Paul, who has expressed worries over both government and civilian drone use.

article_content: Due to worsening air quality, all primary schools in Delhi will remain closed until November 10, as announced by Education Minister Atishi. For students in grades 6 to 12, schools have the option to conduct classes online. Air quality in Delhi has significantly deteriorated, with the Air Quality Index (AQI) rising from 415 at 4 pm on Saturday to 460 at 7 am on Sunday—well into the 'severe' category. Earlier, primary schools were ordered closed until November 5, but this has been extended as pollution levels remain high. Under the central government's air pollution control plan, emergency measures—including bans on polluting trucks, commercial four-wheelers, and all construction—are enforced in the NCR if the AQI exceeds 450. Levels of PM2.5, hazardous fine particulate matter, have far surpassed safe limits—recorded at 7 to 8 times above the Indian government's prescribed 60 micrograms per cubic meter, and 80 to 100 times above the World Health Organization's healthy limit of 5 micrograms per cubic meter at multiple sites. This decline in air quality is attributed to a drop in temperatures, stagnant wind conditions that trap pollutants, and an increase in post-harvest stubble burning in Punjab and Haryana. In other news, Sweden's Saab has received approval for 100% foreign direct investment to set up a new defense manufacturing facility in India. The State Bank of India reported an 8% increase in net profit in the second quarter, citing steady loan demand and reduced provisions. Byju's, an edtech company, disclosed a 2.3-fold increase in standalone business revenue to ₹3,569 crore for the year ending March 2022, with Ebitda losses declining to ₹2,253 crore.

article_content:
The Bharatiya Janata Party (BJP) has unveiled its manifesto for the upcoming Chhattisgarh assembly elections, aiming to attract farmers, women, and youth. The party has pledged to procure paddy at a higher minimum support price (MSP) and provide a one-time payment of Rs 12,000 under the Krishak Unnati Yojana. Additionally, married women would receive Rs 12,000 per year and the party promises to create one lakh jobs if elected to power.

Union Home Minister Amit Shah released the manifesto in Raipur, outlining several promises. These include full transparency in public service commission (PSC) selections, action against corruption and nepotism, procurement of 21 quintals of paddy per acre at Rs 3,100 per quintal under MSP, and offering LPG cylinders to poor families at Rs 500. The establishment of a cash counter at every panchayat bhawan to ease payments to farmers under the Krishak Unnati Yojana was also announced. The manifesto asserts that the one lakh vacant government posts will be filled transparently and promptly.

The BJP also promises to improve infrastructure, provide access to clean drinking water, build houses, and enhance health and education services. The elections are scheduled for November 7 and 17, in two phases.

In response, Congress leader Randeep Singh Surjewala criticized the BJP, claiming the party had previously failed to deliver on its promises to farmers. He alleged that crops were not procured at the MSP announced by the Centre, questioned allocations for government schemes, and highlighted the increased costs of essential supplies affecting farmers. Surjewala promised that the Congress would ensure higher MSPs for crops and provide financial relief for farmers.

بی جے پی نے یہ بھی وعدہ کیا ہے کہ وہ انفراسٹرکچر میں بہتری لائے گی، صاف پانی تک رسائی دے گی، رہائش فراہم کرے گی اور صحت و تعلیم کے شعبوں کو فروغ دے گی۔ انتخابات دو مرحلوں میں 7 اور 17 نومبر کو ہوں گے۔

اس کے جواب میں کانگریس کے رہنما رندیپ سنگھ سرجے والا نے بی جے پی پر تنقید کی اور کہا کہ پارٹی پہلے بھی کسانوں سے کئے گئے وعدے پورے نہ کر سکی۔ انہوں نے دعویٰ کیا کہ حکومت نے مرکز کی طرف سے اعلان کردہ ایم ایس پی پر فصلیں نہیں خریدیں، سرکاری اسکیموں کے فنڈز کو سوالیہ نشان بنایا اور کہا کہ کسان ڈیزل، بیج اور بجلی کی بڑھتی قیمتوں سے پریشان ہیں۔ سرجے والا نے کہا کہ کانگریس زیادہ ایم ایس پی اور مالی امداد دے گی۔

article_content: Paula Broadwell, a major in the Army reserves and former mistress of ex-CIA Director David Petraeus, has had her scheduled promotion revoked by the Army, according to a Department of Defense official. Broadwell was approved for promotion to lieutenant colonel in August, but following revelations in November of an illicit affair with Petraeus, the Army began investigating her for possession of classified information at her home without authorization. Army regulations state that if new information emerges within six months of a promotion date, the individual can be deemed ineligible. Because of the ongoing investigation, Broadwell has been found ineligible and her promotion revoked until the matter is resolved, as reported by an unnamed Defense Department official to CNN. If she is cleared of wrongdoing, Broadwell could become eligible for promotion again. Her security clearance, which was suspended last year, has not yet been reinstated. Petraeus' affair with Broadwell, who authored his biography 'All In: The Education of General David Petraeus,' began in late 2011 and ended in mid-2012. The affair came to light after Broadwell anonymously sent warning messages to Florida socialite Jill Kelley, a friend of the Petraeus family. FBI investigators traced the emails to Broadwell. She admitted to the affair when questioned, and the discovery of classified documents on her computer led to further investigation. The exposure of the affair led to Petraeus' resignation as CIA Director on November 9, 2012, causing significant embarrassment for the Army. The scandal also drew in Marine General John Allen, who exchanged thousands of emails with Kelley. Although Allen was cleared of any wrongdoing, he later announced his retirement to care for his seriously ill wife, Kathy, emphasizing that his decision was for family reasons, not related to the investigation. In a public statement, Allen said, 'For more than 35 years, my beloved Kathy has devotedly stood beside me and enabled me to serve my country.' He acknowledged the toll the investigation had taken on his family.

article_content: MADRID — Emergency services in the Spanish Canary Islands reported Wednesday that more than 650 migrants arrived on El Hierro island in five large wooden boats over the last two days. According to the islands’ emergency service on X (formerly Twitter), one of four boats arriving Tuesday carried 280 migrants, marking the largest number in a single boat since traffickers began using the Canary Island route regularly in 1994, state news agency EFE said. Three additional boats, with more than 200 migrants total, arrived at El Hierro on Tuesday, while another vessel with 128 migrants landed on Wednesday. Only five migrants required medical attention. In recent days, hundreds of other migrants have been intercepted attempting to reach other islands in the archipelago, located off northwest Africa, as well as mainland Spain. Upon arrival by boat, migrants in Spain are held for up to 72 hours by police for identification before being transferred to various reception or detention centers depending on their circumstances. While some migrants are deported, most apply for asylum and are relocated to mainland Spain while their cases are reviewed. Ultimately, many are released and ordered to leave the country if their asylum claims are denied. Spain’s Interior Ministry reported that nearly 15,000 migrants arrived in the Canary Islands by boat from January 1 to September 30, 2023—a 20% increase from the same period last year. Most migrants departed from Senegal. ___ Follow AP’s global migration coverage at https://apnews.com/hub/migration

article_content: Mark Cuban, the owner of the Dallas Mavericks, is selling a majority stake in the NBA team to Miriam Adelson and her family. Sources suggest the deal is valued at approximately $3.5 billion. Cuban will keep his existing shares and continue to oversee basketball operations for the Mavericks under the terms of the sale. The agreement requires final approval from the NBA Board of Governors before being completed. Previously, Cuban discussed a partnership with the Adelsons' Las Vegas Sands Corp. to develop a new arena at the center of a resort and casino complex in Dallas. He described this collaboration as central to his vision for the team’s future. Miriam Adelson recently sold $2 billion worth of Las Vegas Sands stock, reportedly to help finance the Mavericks acquisition. She is the widow of Sheldon Adelson, former CEO of Las Vegas Sands, and her family’s wealth is estimated by Forbes at $32.3 billion. Cuban bought the Mavericks in 2000 for $285 million. The team is now valued at $4.5 billion by Forbes, ranking as the NBA’s seventh most valuable franchise.

article_content: Morgan Beck, wife of Olympic ski champion Bode Miller, has shared an update on her pregnancy by posting a photo of her baby bump on Instagram. Now six months along with her first child, the 27-year-old professional volleyball player and model captioned her side-on selfie: '6 months, 28 lbs and an amazing appetite. This isn't so bad.' She noted in the comments that she was impressed by her weight gain. Morgan also shared that she and Bode, who married in 2012, have chosen not to learn the baby's sex before birth, saying, 'It's going to be a surprise!' and admitting it's difficult not knowing. The couple announced in December they were expecting their first child together. While this is Beck’s first, it will be Miller’s third; he has a six-year-old daughter with Chanel Johnson and a two-year-old son with ex-partner Sara McKenna. Previously, there was public controversy surrounding the conception of Miller and McKenna’s son. In an anonymous post on TheBump.com, Beck suggested McKenna became pregnant by retrieving a condom from the trash, but these posts were removed once Beck's identity was revealed. McKenna denied the claim, stating her child was conceived traditionally while on vacation. Miller and McKenna were involved in a custody dispute over their son, which was settled late last year. Notably, the child’s legal name is Samuel Bode Miller-McKenna, though Miller refers to him as Nathaniel in honor of his late brother. Beck and Miller first met and married in 2012, not long after he dated McKenna. In early 2013, Beck suffered a miscarriage, just before McKenna gave birth to her child with Miller.

article_content:
Gibraltar’s famous Barbary macaques are increasingly causing disturbances in the town’s streets, prompting authorities to consider relocating nearly half of them. Despite their reputation as friendly and inquisitive animals, these wild monkeys have become fearless around humans. Dr. John Cortes, Gibraltar’s Environment Minister, stated that the macaques now associate people with abundant food.

Recently, a grandmother named Rose Vinales was bitten in an unprovoked attack while she was pushing her baby grandson in a pram. She is one of almost sixty people this year who required hospital treatment after monkey bites. In response, the government launched the 'Get Our Monkeys Back To Nature' campaign, which aims to educate people about the dangers of feeding the macaques and restore their natural behaviors. Feeding the monkeys is illegal and punishable by a fine, but this law is often overlooked, especially by tourists visiting popular sites like Apes Den and the Siege Tunnels.

This campaign is part of a broader action plan, supported by primate experts at the Born Free Foundation. The plan includes stepping up a contraceptive program and considering the relocation of up to 120 monkeys to North Africa. Dr. Cortes indicated that the current macaque population is around 230 and emphasized that the government opposes culling. However, Selwyn Figueras, the colony’s shadow environment minister, suggested that culling should still be considered.

Although the Barbary macaque is a beloved symbol of Gibraltar, its origins on the Rock are shrouded in mystery. The species was first recorded in the early 17th century. The only wild populations outside Gibraltar exist in Algeria and Morocco, where they are endangered. From 1915 to 1991, the British Army and, later, the Gibraltar Regiment, cared for the monkeys. Sgt. Alfred Holmes, who oversaw the macaques from the mid-1950s for nearly thirty years, ensured the animals received attentive care, even arranging for sick monkeys to be treated by the same doctors as soldiers at the Royal Naval Hospital. The monkeys once received royal attention when Prince Charles and Princess Anne visited in 1954.

Local legend maintains that Gibraltar will remain British as long as the monkeys are present—a belief linked to Sir Winston Churchill’s decision during World War Two to import additional monkeys when the population dwindled to just seven. Though commonly called ‘Barbary apes,’ the animals are actually stubby-tailed monkeys.

Dr. Cortes acknowledged that returning the monkeys to their natural behaviors will be challenging, but he is confident the program will succeed with community support.

article_content: Jennice Lynch, aged 19, pleaded guilty to three burglaries at her family home and received a suspended sentence. Her parents, Ruth and John Lynch, expressed disappointment, believing the sentence would not change her behavior. Jennice stole jewelry worth thousands of pounds, including a £4,000 gold watch. In March, she was sentenced at Burnley Crown Court by Recorder Kevin Talbot to a 22-month suspended period and was barred from approaching her parents’ home in Whitworth, Lancashire. Jennice said she committed one of the burglaries after feeling neglected by her mother. Her parents described the penalty as insufficient and doubted its effectiveness, noting Jennice’s ongoing issues since age 14. About six weeks later, Jennice allegedly broke into the Bacup home of Mike and Phillipa Christie and stole keys to their specially-adapted Fiat Punto Evo, a crucial vehicle for their six-year-old autistic daughter, Catherine, used for hospital visits and daily activities. The abandoned car was found written off the next day. Jennice, who is unemployed and relies on benefits, was arrested on suspicion of theft and for breaching her suspended sentence. The Christie family now faces transportation challenges for their daughter and substantial replacement costs. Both families voiced distress at the continued pattern of criminal behavior. After her arrest, Jennice requested psychiatric assistance and is now in the mental health unit at Burnley General Hospital. Her parents have struggled with her since adolescence, feeling that previous efforts and the suspended sentence have failed to help her change.

article_content: Thanks to its unconventional premise, there are few shows quite like Bodies. The new Netflix series follows four British detectives from different points in history, each investigating the same crime—a fresh twist on the crime procedural. Because of this, finding series that feel exactly like Bodies can be challenging. Fortunately, we've gathered a few recommendations that capture some of the elements that make Bodies so compelling. First up is Dark, a German series on Netflix known for its intricate and gripping sci-fi narrative. Dark takes place in a small town where the disappearance of children forces residents to confront secrets from the past. The show weaves in time travel elements, linking the town's present to the year 1986. While the plot can get complex, those who stick with it will find Dark highly rewarding. Dark is available to stream on Netflix. Another recommendation is True Detective, particularly its acclaimed first season. This HBO/Max series uses shifting timelines, jumping between the present and decades after the original investigation, providing multiple perspectives on a mysterious case. While True Detective doesn't span as much time as Bodies, both shows examine how the passage of time can shape an investigation. True Detective is streaming on Max. Lastly, Twin Peaks holds a special place among crime shows for its eerie and influential storytelling. The show follows an FBI agent investigating the murder of a high school girl in a small Washington town, delivering a mix of detective drama and surreal, sometimes unsettling moments. While Bodies is more straightforward, Twin Peaks explores the darkness behind crime in unique ways and remains a cult favorite. Its impact is still seen in pop culture, including recent video games like Alan Wake 2. Twin Peaks can be streamed on Paramount+.

article_content: Asiana Airlines announced on Wednesday that it has dropped plans for legal action against San Francisco TV station KTVU-TV, following the use of racially offensive fake pilot names. However, 83 passengers from the crashed flight have stated their intent to sue Boeing and the airline. The South Korean carrier stated that KTVU-TV has already apologized for airing the erroneous names for four pilots on the plane that crashed in San Francisco on July 6th. The airline believes its efforts are better focused on supporting the recovery of survivors and their families. Asiana revealed that the four pilots of the Boeing 777 involved in the crash have been hospitalized in South Korea due to psychological trauma and injuries suffered during the incident. Last week, KTVU-TV anchor Tori Campbell read the fake pilot names live on air, attributing the confirmation to the National Transportation Safety Board. The broadcast, intended as a prank, included racially insensitive Asian-style puns. Both the TV station and the NTSB have since apologized for the error. Initially, Asiana Airlines said it would sue the TV station, citing the damage to its reputation, but has since decided not to pursue legal action given the apology and the need to focus on the aftermath of the accident. The crash resulted in the deaths of three Chinese teenagers visiting the U.S. for a summer camp and injured more than 180 people. The accident occurred as the plane approached the runway too low and slow, clipping a seawall, tearing off the tail, and catching fire. A Chicago law firm, Ribbeck Law Chartered, has filed a petition in Cook County Circuit Court to preserve evidence and plans to pursue legal action against Boeing and parts manufacturers. The lawsuit alleges possible mechanical malfunction of the Boeing 777's auto throttle and issues with emergency slides. Attorney Monica R. Kelly stated the aim is to determine the crash's cause and resolve any airline or aircraft problems to prevent future tragedies. Boeing has made no public comment. The pilots reported that they relied on automated cockpit equipment to control the plane's speed. Investigators found the autothrottle was 'armed' but are still determining if it was engaged at the time of the crash.

article_content: Darrin Campbell, a 49-year-old business executive, was found dead alongside his wife, Kimberly (51), and their two teenage children after their rented Florida home was set ablaze. Authorities believe Campbell fatally shot his wife and children with a .40-caliber handgun before starting the fire in a mansion rented from former tennis star James Blake. According to Campbell’s father-in-law, there were no indications of financial problems, and the family is in shock. Surveillance footage captured Campbell purchasing fireworks and gas canisters in the days prior, which investigators suspect were used to ignite the blaze. Campbell had recently started a position as Chief Operating Officer at a Tampa digital storage company after a period of unemployment. The Campbells, seen as a close-knit and successful family by acquaintances, had moved into the rented property to be near their children's private school, Carrollwood Day School. The family paid an estimated $6,000 a month in rent and had no known criminal record or prior trouble with authorities. Police are reviewing the family's finances but have not identified evidence of hardship. Friends, neighbors, and family have expressed shock, emphasizing the Campbells' strong relationships and apparent stability. The investigation continues.

article_content: Apple enthusiasts—including co-founder Steve Wozniak—lined up on Friday morning to buy the iPhone 4S, Apple’s latest smartphone featuring several internal upgrades. The large crowds at Apple Stores were motivated both by excitement for the device and a desire to honor Steve Jobs, Apple's co-founder, who passed away last week after battling pancreatic cancer. In New York, fans left flowers, photos, iPad boxes, and apples as memorials for Jobs. In Atlanta, several customers said Jobs’ passing encouraged them to purchase the phone, feeling it was the last model he influenced. 'I wanted it anyway, but Jobs’ death made me sort of want it more,' said Dwight Hill from the Atlanta area. 'I just hope the company keeps going in the same direction.' Around 200 people lined up early in New York for the new iPhone, which features a faster processor and Siri, an intelligent voice assistant that responds to commands and answers questions. Lines also formed in Asia and Europe. In Silicon Valley, Steve Wozniak waited at the front of a line started on Thursday afternoon, passing time with his iPad, Diet Dr. Pepper, and taking photos with fans. 'I want to get mine along with the millions of other fans,' Wozniak said. 'I just want to be able to talk to my phone.' Although initially criticized as a minor update, the iPhone 4S offers an improved A5 dual-core processor, an enhanced 8-megapixel camera, and Siri. Tech writer Brian X. Chen noted Siri’s usefulness and humor, sharing examples like, 'Me: I’m drunk. Siri: I found a number of cabs fairly close to you.' Siri was a key reason for many customers waiting in line. 'I just want the personal assistant,' said Atlanta nurse Teresa Sparks, who waited since 4:45 a.m. Scott England joked with a friend about the camera, saying, 'Siri is a big deal.' Becky Waddell, a real-estate agent, praised Siri for making phone use safer while driving and saving time. The launch generated excitement. Two Apple fans in New York arrived 18 days early and blogged about their experience on iPhoneWhatever, according to CNNMoney. Another customer, David Betz, attended despite recovering from foot surgery after a car accident. 'Is it worth it? We'll find out,' he said. Apple CEO Tim Cook introduced the iPhone 4S last week, one day before Jobs’ passing. Pre-orders began October 7 and reached 1 million in the first 24 hours, surpassing last year's 600,000 iPhone 4 pre-orders. The iPhone 4S launched Friday in all 245 US Apple stores and in Australia, Canada, France, Germany, Japan, and the United Kingdom. Apple plans to expand availability to 22 additional countries by the end of October. Retail and online sales began at 8 a.m. Friday, but pre-orders at the main carriers quickly sold out, with online Apple orders facing several weeks’ delay. Third-party retailers like Radio Shack, Best Buy, Target, and Sam’s Club also offer the device, but customers are advised to check stock before arriving, as inventories are limited and some pre-orders are still being filled. Apple retail stores offer free in-store setup and personalized instruction. The iPhone 4S is priced at $199 (16GB), $299 (32GB), and $399 (64GB)—the first time an iPhone has had this much storage. The excitement for the iPhone 4S is closely connected with mourning for Steve Jobs. Some fans say the '4S' in the name stands for 'For Steve,' reflecting Jobs’ legacy and fan devotion. However, this seems coincidental, as most development occurred when Jobs was still CEO.

بڑی قطاریں لگیں۔ سلیکن ویلی میں، اسٹیو ووزنیاک اس قطار کے سامنے موجود تھے جو جمعرات کی سہ پہر سے شروع ہوئی تھی، وہ اپنا وقت آئی پیڈ، ڈائیٹ ڈاکٹر پیپر اور مداحوں کے ساتھ تصاویر بنانے میں گزار رہے تھے۔ ووزنیاک نے کہا: 'میں اپنی ڈیوائس باقی لاکھوں مداحوں کے ساتھ حاصل کرنا چاہتا ہوں۔ میں بس اپنے فون سے بات کرنا چاہتا ہوں۔' اگرچہ ابتدائی طور پر اس ماڈل کو معمولی سمجھا گیا تھا، آئی فون 4 ایس میں بہتر اے article_content: Mike Hayhurst, a rodeo clown from Barstow, California, caused an uproar at the 17th annual Creston Classic Rodeo by making a racially insensitive joke about First Lady Michelle Obama over the loudspeaker. According to sources including the San Luis Obispo Tribune and Gawker, Hayhurst joked that Playboy offered Mitt Romney’s wife, Ann Romney, $250,000 to pose for the magazine, claiming the White House was upset because National Geographic only offered Michelle Obama $50. The joke drew boos from some in the crowd and led to strong condemnation from the Creston Classic Rodeo board. Board member Mike Barrett emphasized that the board did not support Hayhurst's remarks and said they would likely not invite him back. The board clarified that they were not responsible for what was said but would demand that Hayhurst issue a letter explaining and apologizing for his behavior. Initial confusion had some attributing the joke to announcer Ed Kutz, but the board later confirmed Hayhurst was the one who made the comment. Attempts to contact Hayhurst for a statement were unsuccessful, as he was hospitalised with injuries unrelated to the controversy, reportedly after being tossed by a bull. When approached for comment, Hayhurst ended the conversation abruptly. This incident came shortly after another controversy in Spain, where Magazine de Fuera de Serie placed Michelle Obama’s face onto an 1800 portrait of a black slave by French artist Marie-Guillemine Benoist. While the editors may have intended an artistic message, many online viewers saw the modified image as offensive and racist. The original painting, 'Portrait D’Une Négresse,' was once praised as an uplifting image symbolizing both women’s and black rights after the abolition of slavery in France. The modern use of Michelle Obama’s image in this context, however, was widely condemned as inappropriate and insensitive.

article_content:
Louisiana is advancing plans to reintroduce passenger train service between Baton Rouge and New Orleans. Governor John Bel Edwards has signed an important development agreement to help relaunch the rail line connecting the state capital to its largest city. The project, discussed since 2008, is aiming for a launch as early as 2027, beginning with a single daily round-trip and expanding service as demand increases.

The train will make stops in Gonzales, Laplace, and Jefferson Parish, improving transit for a wide range of communities. Funding includes $20 million from the Road Home Program settlement, backing the return of a train route that has been inactive since 1969.

Governor Edwards highlighted the potential for increased economic activity, workforce connections, and regional links, noting additional benefits such as less traffic congestion and more travel options for local events. Transportation Secretary Eric Kalivoda stressed that the new line will also attract tourists and provide a dependable alternative to highway travel.

Amtrak CEO Stephen Gardner mentioned that public interest in passenger rail remains strong in Louisiana and nationwide. The service will use tracks along the I-10 corridor owned by Canadian Pacific Kansas City and CN, with infrastructure upgrades scheduled for next year. The route will connect to the New Orleans-Mobile corridor—set to begin service in 2024—and will join other Amtrak lines in the state, such as the Sunset Limited, City of New Orleans, and Crescent lines. Ticket details and full schedules will be released closer to the launch date.

article_content: Veteran film festival director Marco Mueller is collaborating with the Macau government to launch the Asia-Europe Young Cinema Festival, set to take place in Macau from January 5 to 11. Former Cannes Marché chief Jerome Paillard will serve as Industry Coordinator, and Beijing-based Shanshan Cao, an independent producer and former CAA China executive, will lead the China and Asia initiatives. Organized with the Macau Cultural Affairs Bureau, the event aims to connect the mainland China film market with international buyers and sellers, support emerging Chinese talent, and offer film education programs. More than 30 European and Asian sales companies will screen films for theatrical and streaming buyers from China, Macau, and Hong Kong. International film festival programmers are also expected to attend. While venues are still being finalized, the event will be held in Macau’s upscale hotels with nearby screening facilities. Each sales company may showcase two features and a showreel of trailers. Speaking to Deadline, Mueller described Macau as an 'ideal meeting place' for bringing together sales companies and the Chinese film industry. He stated that both commercial and arthouse films will be presented, with a focus on buyers seeking theatrical releases, not just streaming rights. The festival will also feature about 20 works-in-progress from filmmakers in China, Macau, and Hong Kong, targeting festival programmers and sales agents. Additionally, the event will offer around 15 Master Classes led by notable filmmakers such as Japan’s Ryusuke Hamaguchi, Italian filmmaker Luca Guadagnino, and Iranian filmmaker Amir Naderi, some of which will include related screenings. Mueller added that the festival seeks to honor new talent and showcase films with confirmed release dates. A training camp is planned for students and young film enthusiasts from Macau, Hong Kong, and China. The festival is funded by the Macau government and supported by the Association for the International Promotion of Chinese-language Film, a local organization backed by mainland investors. Mueller mentioned future plans to expand the event into a larger, full-scale film festival, with possible dates in late 2024 or 2025 under discussion. Macau, traditionally known for its casinos, is working to diversify its economy by promoting cultural and other attractions. Currently based in Shanghai, Mueller was formerly the artistic director of the Pingyao International Film Festival, which he co-founded with Jia Zhangke. He has previously held leadership roles at film festivals in Locarno, Rome, Venice, and Beijing. He also briefly headed the International Film Festival and Awards Macao (IFFAM), but left the position over creative differences before its first edition.
