article_content: A new United Nations report predicts that global greenhouse gas emissions will decrease by only 2% below 2019 levels by 2030—a stark contrast to the 43% drop needed to prevent the most severe consequences of climate change. The findings are released ahead of the 28th UN Climate Change Conference (COP28) in Dubai, where nations are expected to push for stronger measures to keep global temperature rise within 1.5 degrees Celsius. Top scientists from the Intergovernmental Panel on Climate Change (IPCC) agree that reducing emissions by 43% from 2019 levels by 2030 is crucial to limiting warming and avoiding more frequent and severe droughts, heatwaves, and rainfall. The UN Framework Convention on Climate Change (UNFCCC) analyzed the Nationally Determined Contributions (NDCs) of 195 parties to the Paris Agreement, including updates submitted until September 2023. While emissions are projected to peak this decade, current commitments will likely lead to an 8.8% increase in emissions compared to 2010—an improvement over last year's projected 10.6% increase, but still far from the needed decline. The report emphasizes that reaching peak emissions before 2030 depends on implementing conditional elements of NDCs, which require enhanced financial resources, technology transfer, technical cooperation, and access to market-based mechanisms. COP28 President Designate Sultan Al Jaber highlighted the urgency for parties to commit to more ambitious actions, stating, "There is simply no time left for delays." He called the upcoming COP28 a 'historic turning point' in the fight against climate change. UN Climate Change Executive-Secretary Simon Stiell echoed this urgency, warning that while progress is being made, it is much too slow. He stressed that COP28 must result in clear commitments and implementation strategies for accelerating climate action. The Global Stocktake, a two-year UN process reviewing progress toward Paris Agreement goals, will conclude at COP28 in Dubai. The findings will guide the next round of climate action plans, aiming to increase ambition and accelerate progress. Stiell concluded, "Billions of people expect their governments to pick up the vast array of tools and solutions already identified and put them to work."
translated_content: اقوام متحدہ کی ایک نئی رپورٹ کے مطابق، 2019 کی سطح کے مقابلے میں 2030 تک عالمی گرین ہاؤس گیسوں کے اخراج میں صرف 2 فیصد کمی کی توقع ہے، جبکہ ماحولیاتی تبدیلی کے سنگین ترین اثرات سے بچنے کے لیے 43 فیصد کمی درکار ہے۔ یہ رپورٹ دبئی میں ہونے والی 28ویں عالمی ماحولیاتی کانفرنس (COP28) سے قبل جاری کی گئی ہے، جہاں ممالک سے توقع ہے کہ وہ عالمی درجہ حرارت 1.5 ڈگری سیلسیس تک محدود کرنے کے لیے مزید مضبوط اقدامات پر زور دیں گے۔ ماہرین موسمیات پر مشتمل بین الحکومتی پینل (IPCC) کے مطابق، 2019 کے مقابلے میں 2030 تک اخراج میں 43 فیصد کمی انتہائی اہم ہے تاکہ درجہ حرارت میں اضافے، شدید خشک سالی، ہیٹ ویوز اور بارشوں کے خطرات سے بچا جا سکے۔ اقوام متحدہ کے ماحولیاتی تبدیلی کے فریم ورک (UNFCCC) نے پیرس معاہدے کے 195 ممالک کی قومی سطح کی اخراج کی معلومات کا تجزیہ کیا، جن میں ستمبر 2023 تک کی نئی یا اپ ڈیٹ شدہ این ڈی سیز بھی شامل ہیں۔ جبکہ اخراج کی سطح اس دہائی میں بلند ترین ہونے کی توقع ہے، موجودہ وعدے 2010 کے مقابلے میں 8.8 فیصد اضافے کے مترادف ہیں، جو گزشتہ سال کے 10.6 فیصد کے مقابلے میں کچھ بہتری ہے لیکن مطلوبہ کمی سے بہت کم ہے۔ رپورٹ میں کہا گیا ہے کہ 2030 سے پہلے اخراج کی حد حاصل کرنے کے لیے مشروط این ڈی سیز کا نفاذ ضروری ہے، جس کے لیے مالی وسائل، ٹیکنالوجی کی منتقلی، تعاون اور مارکیٹ بیسڈ میکنزمز تک رسائی ضروری ہے۔ COP28 کے صدر نامزد سلطان الجابر نے ممالک پر زور دیا کہ وہ مزید جراتمندانہ اقدامات کریں۔ ان کے مطابق "اب وقت ضائع کرنے کی کوئی جگہ نہیں ہے"۔ انہوں نے COP28 کو موسمیاتی سرگرمیوں کے لیے تاریخی موڑ قرار دیا۔ اقوام متحدہ کے موسمیاتی تبدیلی کے ایگزیکٹو سیکرٹری سائمن اسٹیئل نے بھی فوری اقدامات پر زور دیا اور کہا کہ پیش رفت بہت سست ہے۔ انھوں نے کہا کہ COP28 کا نتیجہ واضح اقدامات اور عملی حکمت عملی ہونا چاہیے۔ عالمی اسٹاک ٹیک، جو پیرس معاہدے کی پیش رفت کی دو سالہ اقوام متحدہ کی جائزہ کاری ہے، دبئی میں COP28 پر مکمل ہوگی۔ اس کے نتائج آئندہ کلائمٹ ایکشن پلانز کے لیے رہنمائی فراہم کریں گے تاکہ رفتار اور عزم میں اضافہ ہو سکے۔ اسٹیئل نے کہا، "اربوں لوگوں کی امید ہے کہ ان کی حکومتیں موجود وسائل اور حل فعال طور پر آزمائیں گی۔"

article_content:
Two and a half years ago, my son Cole passed away from neuroblastoma, a common childhood cancer, after enduring multiple surgeries, rounds of chemotherapy, and painful radiation treatments. These procedures, while standard for this illness, were so grueling that I wouldn't wish them upon anyone. The suffering they caused—and the memory of watching my child endure them—remain with me every day. Cole was just five. He left behind not just me, but my wife Michelle, his twin brother Troy, and his big sister Tara; our family was shattered by his loss.

I've since discovered, through conversations with other parents who have lost their children to cancer, that this grief never truly fades. A week before Cole died in our arms, he looked at me and said, 'I'm not going to grow up to be or do anything.' Hearing those words broke my heart, and I promised him that he would have a lasting legacy. For the past two years, I've worked tirelessly to keep that promise. My hope is that increasing awareness will lead to much-needed funding and research so that children facing cancer can receive kinder treatments and better odds of survival.

Pediatric cancer claims more young lives in the United States than any other disease, and over 11,000 children are diagnosed each year. Despite this, the National Cancer Institute allocates just 4% of its budget to pediatric cancer research—underscoring the urgent need for expanded support.

I began my mission to raise awareness in August 2012, inspired by how the breast cancer community has mobilized for pink in October, achieving better treatments and outcomes through advocacy. I dreamed of seeing gold, the color for Childhood Cancer Awareness Month in September, become just as prominent. I reached out to officials across the U.S. to illuminate landmarks gold in September. Many responded—Boston's Prudential Building, Zakim Bridge, TD Garden, the Battleship New Jersey, and Greenville's Liberty Bridge all participated. This movement has spread nationwide and even internationally, with gold-lit displays in Ireland, Australia, Canada, and Switzerland.

Last September, more landmarks than ever before shone gold for childhood cancer awareness, but this is just the beginning. I urge everyone to display gold this September to help highlight the struggle and inspire change. Shining gold not only raises awareness and funding for research that could lead to better treatments and a cure—it also brings comfort to grieving families, showing us that our children aren’t forgotten. My son had most of his treatments at Floating Hospital for Children at Tufts Medical Center in Boston. Returning to Boston after his passing was difficult, but last September, seeing the familiar landmarks glow gold brought tears to my eyes and a bittersweet smile to my face. I knew, at that moment, Cole was truly doing 'something big.'

ڈھائی سال پہلے میرا بیٹا کول نیوروبلاستوما، جو کہ بچوں کا عام کینسر ہے، سے انتقال کر گیا۔ اس نے کئی سرجریز، کیموتھراپی اور تکلیف دہ ریڈی ایشن علاج سہے۔ یہ علاج معمول کے مطابق ہیں مگر اتنے سخت ہیں کہ میں کسی اور کے لیے نہیں چاہوں گا۔ اس اذیت اور اپنے بچے کو اس کیفیت میں دیکھنے کی یاد ہر دن میرے ساتھ ہے۔ کول کی عمر صرف پانچ برس تھی۔ وہ میرے ساتھ ساتھ میری بیوی مشیل، جڑواں بھائی ٹرائے اور بڑی بہن تارا کو چھوڑ گیا۔ ہمارے خاندان کو اس دکھ نے چور کردیا۔

دوسرے والدین سے بات کر کے جانا کہ یہ غم کبھی ختم نہیں ہوتا۔ کول کی وفات سے ایک ہفتہ پہلے اس نے کہا: 'میں بڑا ہو کر کچھ نہیں کر سکوں گا۔' یہ سن کر میرا دل ٹوٹ گیا، اور میں نے وعدہ کیا کہ وہ کچھ بڑا ضرور کرے گا۔ پچھلے دو سال سے میں اس وعدے کو پورا کرنے کے لیے کوشش کر رہا ہوں۔ میری امید ہے کہ آگاہی بڑھنے سے فنڈنگ اور تحقیق میں اضافہ ہو، تاکہ بچوں کے علاج بہتر اور زندہ رہنے کے امکانات زیادہ ہوں۔

article_content: A French toddler named Logan, age two, was abducted from a hotel room in Bali three days ago but has now been found safe. The incident occurred at the Three Brothers Bungalows in Legian, close to Kuta Beach, where Logan was staying with his father. Authorities withheld details for 24 hours. Some unverified accounts suggest the father may have contributed inadvertently—bringing a European woman to his hotel room and later discovering both she and Logan were gone. This aspect remains unconfirmed by officials. The public has raised questions about the whereabouts of Logan’s mother. Indonesian officials worry that high-profile kidnappings—including the recent abduction and safe release of 61-year-old oil worker Malcolm Primrose in Aceh—might inspire copycat crimes. The case has drawn comparisons to the 2007 disappearance of British toddler Madeleine McCann in Portugal. The incident has made some prospective travelers uneasy. Joanne Robertson, preparing for a Bali trip with her children, voiced her concerns on Facebook.

article_content: To commemorate the 100th anniversary of World War I, St Paul’s Cathedral is exhibiting two striking white crosses created by artist Gerry Judah. These 20-foot-tall sculptures, hanging at the entrance to the nave, feature detailed models symbolizing cities like Aleppo and Homs in Syria and Baghdad in Iraq—places severely affected by modern conflict. Judah’s works aim to show that the effects of World War I continue to influence present-day wars, as the redrawing of boundaries after that conflict set the stage for today’s turmoil in places such as Syria. His intention is to encourage visitors not only to remember the past but also to recognize current tragedies caused by war. The artist hopes that the installations inspire empathy and hope within the cathedral, providing a space for visitors to reflect on both history and the present day. The sculptures will be on display for eight months, including during the centenary in August, and will be unveiled to the public on Palm Sunday. Judah has previously contributed similar pieces to the Imperial War Museum and St Mary Brookfield Church. Reverend Canon Mark Oakley, Chancellor of St Paul’s, stated that the sculptures powerfully remind visitors of the human cost of war and the continuing relevance of remembrance today.

article_content: Singapore’s economy contracted by 4.2 percent in the fourth quarter of 2008, according to the Ministry of Trade and Industry on Thursday. The ministry also projected that the economy could shrink by between 2 and 5 percent in 2009. This follows robust growth the prior year, with the economy growing 7.8 percent, and an overall growth rate of 1.1 percent for 2008. The ministry described the outlook for Gross Domestic Product in 2009 as "weak" due to the pessimistic global economic climate. It stated that all major sectors, except for construction, business services, and information and communications, suffered contractions. Declines in private sector investment and consumption also contributed to decreased domestic demand. Weakened global demand for electronics, pharmaceuticals, and chemicals is expected to impact the manufacturing sector as well.

article_content: Homeowners can expect a seasonal gift as banks cut mortgage rates to record lows ahead of Christmas. HSBC is launching its most affordable five-year fixed-rate mortgage at 2.48% for borrowers able to put down 40% deposits. The offer will be available from Monday and includes a £999 fee. This is the first five-year fixed-rate mortgage below 2.5% since Yorkshire Building Society's 2.44% deal in summer 2013. Banks are engaging in a rate-cutting competition, with several lowering their offers since autumn. Experts predict more reductions are likely. Santander recently unveiled a two-year fixed-rate remortgage at 1.84% for customers with significant equity, plus a £995 fee—available for a limited time. Barclays has followed suit, now offering a five-year fixed remortgage at 2.79% for those with a 30% deposit and a £999 application fee. Skipton Building Society also announced a five-year fixed at 2.56% for borrowers with a 40% deposit and a £995 fee. Analysts suggest that lenders are keen to retain customers who might be tempted to switch if the Bank of England raises its base rate, which could happen in late 2015. Banks are also working to meet end-of-year loan targets, following the introduction of stricter lending rules in April, which initially disrupted the market and decreased the availability of mortgages. Though the lending market is bouncing back, certain groups—especially those over 40—are reportedly facing more hurdles when applying for home loans. Rachel Springall from Moneyfacts believes HSBC’s deal will appeal to those who want to lock in a low fixed rate for the long term. She cautions that buyers should look beyond just the attractive rates and consider the total cost of their mortgage, advising them to seek independent financial advice to find the best option.

article_content:
While spending a week in Las Vegas with our mothers to celebrate Mother's Day, I found the city's well-known atmosphere of excess striking—and was surprised by the absence of faith-based protests. In a place famous for its vices, I expected to hear at least some religious objections, but there were none.

This stands in contrast to the intense reaction that often greets efforts to expand protections for LGBT people or discussions about same-gender couples at events like school dances. Although Christian teachings are sometimes wielded as justification for these protests, the Bible itself does not rank some sins as worse than others.

Many Christians appear to focus selectively on passages like Leviticus 18:22 to denounce homosexuality, while ignoring other biblical mandates or so-called "sins" with similar severity. Issues such as greed, dishonesty, or even other sexual conduct are rarely the focus of the same concern, which highlights a pattern of inconsistency.

Over time, misunderstandings and mistranslations—like interpreting 'Sodomite' as a condemnation of homosexuality—have shaped certain beliefs, even though original biblical terms referred to ritual prostitution rather than sexual orientation. 

This tendency to use religion for personal prejudices isn't limited to sexuality. Historically, religious texts were used to justify slavery, keep women out of leadership, and support bans on interracial relationships. If Christians were truly following all biblical laws, outrage would extend to many other behaviors, not just those linked to the LGBT community.

These patterns suggest that, for some, religious objections often mask personal discomfort with difference. As a Christian, I find this departure from the foundational message of love deeply troubling, especially when scripture is selectively used to marginalize others.

(These opinions are those of the author, LZ Granderson.)

article_content: Education Secretary Nicky Morgan has declined to meet with 'Waterloo 200,' a charity organizing educational events and teaching materials for the 200th anniversary of the Battle of Waterloo. According to the Department for Education, neither Morgan nor her staff can meet due to a busy schedule. David Huse and Major General Sir Evelyn Webb-Carter, leaders of Waterloo 200, voiced concern, emphasizing the importance of engaging schools in commemorating this key event in British history. They have collaborated with academics, developed resources for teachers, and launched a website, with support from the Heritage Lottery Fund. The anniversary plans include a concert at the Royal Albert Hall and a memorial service at St Paul’s Cathedral on June 18. A government representative stated that with recent curriculum reforms, the French revolutionary wars, including Waterloo, are already included for students aged 11 to 14. They also noted that Waterloo 200 is working with the Department for Culture, Media, and Sport. Some organizers worry the Department for Education's lack of involvement downplays the significance of Waterloo’s bicentenary. Meanwhile, Nicky Morgan—who has reversed several of her predecessor’s policies and shifted her stance on certain issues—attended the PinkNews Awards but stands by her decision not to meet with the charity.

article_content: Father Gregory Grant, a Catholic priest in Bristol, has earned recognition by merging his religious calling with property development. At the helm of the PG Group—an enterprise he co-founded in 1998 alongside a parishioner—Father Gregory oversees operations from an office above his church, St Patrick’s, in Redfield. The PG Group is dedicated to revitalizing neglected city center buildings into affordable homes. Its latest accomplishment, Champion Court, featured 17 refurbished properties, of which 15 sold on the launch day following 66 viewings, and the remaining ones were snapped up within a week. Most buyers were young couples. Prices for these two- and three-bedroom homes, previously derelict council houses, ranged from £149,000 to £245,000, targeting first-time owners. Stuart Gaiger, Development Director at PG Group, emphasized Bristol’s evident need for accessible housing and revealed upcoming plans to transform a nearby office building into 140 apartments set to debut next spring. What sets Father Gregory’s work apart is his focus on charity: a third of the company’s profits go toward parish initiatives and charitable activities. Since the company’s start, more than £1 million has been contributed to such causes—a figure that continues to grow. Father Gregory sees generating revenue as a means to give back, stating that his main satisfaction comes from supporting community projects. His foray into property began in the early 1980s when he assisted Corpus Christi Church in Weston-super-Mare to redevelop an old Scout hall, using the proceeds to improve church facilities. When St Patrick’s faced shutdown due to poor condition and low attendance, Father Gregory led a revitalization that included building a new church, a convent, retirement homes, and a nursing home, boosting congregation numbers. Originally partnered with Peter Bradley, Father Gregory now collaborates with Fiona Bradley, who became a trustee after Peter's passing. In 2002, he also launched The Grant Bradley Trust, which funds housing and educational projects overseas. Despite his full schedule—working from early morning to late at night—Father Gregory balances his business, parish responsibilities, and charitable endeavors, maximizing his positive impact on the community.

article_content: Seven-year-old Zane Gbangbola died in his sleep during last winter’s floods at his home near Chertsey, Surrey. His parents suspect he was killed by hydrogen cyanide gas, believed to have entered their house from contaminated land at a nearby old landfill site, as floodwaters rose and reached their basement. Kye and Nicole Gbangbola, Zane’s parents, were both hospitalized due to the effects of hydrogen cyanide poisoning, with Kye now left paraplegic. They allege that authorities, including the Environment Agency (EA) and the local council, knew about the potential danger of ground gas from the landfill but did not warn residents. It emerged that the Environment Agency had previously installed a gas-proof membrane in a neighboring structure four years before the floods, but did not alert local homeowners about ground gas risks. Planning documents from as early as 2007 show that officials were aware of possible harmful substances in the ground but only informed residents if they applied to alter their homes. The Gbangbolas have been campaigning for eight months to uncover the truth behind their son’s death, meeting with government ministers and receiving public and celebrity support. They believe the official cause of death—carbon monoxide poisoning from a petrol pump—is inaccurate, as they insist they never used such a pump in their home. An initial pathology report was inconclusive but later changed to carbon monoxide poisoning after further tests. Scientific experts and neighbors have questioned the adequacy of the investigation, noting that hydrogen cyanide disappears from the body within 48 hours and suggesting that more thorough testing should have been done. Pollution expert Dr. Mark McKinney argues that installing a gas-proof membrane shows there was real concern about ground gases. Following the incident, police investigations have focused on the company that supplied the pump, and a file has been sent to the Crown Prosecution Service. The Environment Agency maintains they followed standard procedures and expresses sympathy for the family, stating they are cooperating fully with investigations. Spelthorne Council notes that basic ground gas protection methods were recommended as a standard precaution for the area. More than 15,000 people have signed a petition demanding the ‘Truth About Zane,’ with campaign support from public figures including Vivienne Westwood, Emma Thompson, and Peter Gabriel. The family plans a march on the local council offices to mark what would have been Zane’s eighth birthday.

In the fast-paced world of global finance, European cities are fiercely competing to establish themselves as premier financial centres. Earning this status can attract substantial investment and attention from business owners and policymakers alike. According to the latest Global Financial Centres Index (GFCI), seven European cities are ranked among the world’s top 20 financial hubs.

While the United States dominates the upper end of the list—with New York securing the number one position—London remains Europe’s leading financial city, ranked second globally. London has slightly narrowed the gap with New York compared to last year and sits just ahead of Singapore and Hong Kong, which take the third and fourth spots, respectively.

Geneva, Switzerland, is the only other European city in the global top 10. Having increased its rating by 29 points, Geneva climbed from 23rd to 10th place over the past year, now just five points behind fifth-placed San Francisco. Analysts attribute Geneva’s progress to Switzerland’s robust regulatory environment and low levels of corruption, which strengthen the financial standing of its cities.

Frankfurt, home to the European Central Bank and Germany’s Bundesbank, has overtaken Paris as Europe’s third most prominent financial centre—rising from 17th to 14th place globally, while Paris slipped from 14th to 15th. Only one ranking point distinguishes them. Frankfurt is also considered one of the 15 cities likely to gain importance in the near future.

Other European cities in the top 20 include Luxembourg (16th), Zurich (18th), and Amsterdam (19th).

Germany stands out with five cities in the global top 50—the highest number among European countries—though none appear in the top 10. In addition to Frankfurt, Berlin rose to 23rd place, Munich dropped to 26th, Stuttgart advanced to 46th, and Hamburg fell to 49th. Switzerland follows with Lugano at 47th, while the UK’s Edinburgh is 34th. Additional top 50 European cities are Dublin (25th), Stockholm (40th), Oslo (42nd), Milan (45th), Madrid (48th), and Helsinki (50th). Their scores are closely grouped, suggesting possible shifts in future rankings.

Three British Crown Dependencies—Jersey (52nd), Guernsey (58th), and the Isle of Man (59th)—are included in the top 60. Though they are not part of the UK, these self-governing jurisdictions remain British Crown possessions.

The GFCI divides Europe into Western and Eastern Europe/Central Asia groups, revealing a pronounced east-west divide. Up to 60th place, all of Europe’s leading financial hubs are in Western Europe. Kazakhstan’s Astana, ranked 60th, holds the highest spot in the Eastern Europe and Central Asia group. Prague is next at 79th, followed by Tallinn at 87th.

Beyond Europe, the US boasts five financial centres in the global top 10, underscoring its economic strength. Top Chinese centres also appear in the global top 20.

According to GFCI 34, a city’s reputation and business environment are closely linked to its financial competitiveness. The Corruption Perception Index and the Economic Freedom of the World Index highlight that increases in economic freedom and decreases in perceived corruption correlate with higher financial centre ratings. City branding also plays a key role: Factors such as safety, stability, cultural amenities, and quality of life enhance a city’s reputation, attracting businesses, professionals, and investors.

تیزی سے تبدیل ہونے والی عالمی مالیاتی دنیا میں، یورپی شہر اپنی شناخت مضبوط مالیاتی مراکز کے طور پر قائم کرنے کی بھرپور کوشش کر رہے ہیں۔ یہ مقام حاصل کرنا کاروباری مالکان اور پالیسی سازوں کی توجہ کے ساتھ سرمایہ کاری بھی لا سکتا ہے۔ تازہ ترین گلوبل فنانشل سینٹرز انڈیکس (GFCI) کے مطابق، سات یورپی شہر دنیا کے ٹاپ 20 مالیاتی حبز میں شامل ہیں۔

اگرچہ امریکہ اس فہرست کے اوپر سرِ فہرست ہے—نیو یارک نمبر ایک پر ہے—لندن بدستور یورپ کا سرفہرست مالیاتی شہر ہے اور عالمی سطح پر دوسرا نمبر رکھتا ہے۔ لندن نے پچھلے سال کی نسبت نیو یارک کے ساتھ فاصلہ کچھ کم کیا ہے اور یہ سنگاپور اور ہانگ کانگ سے ذرا آگے ہے، جو بالترتیب تیسرے اور چوتھے نمبر پر ہیں۔

سوئٹزرلینڈ کا جنیوا واحد اور یورپی شہر ہے جو عالمی ٹاپ 10 میں ہے۔ اس نے اپنے اسکور میں 29 پوائنٹس اضافہ کیا اور گزشتہ سال کے 23 ویں سے دسویں نمبر تک پہنچ گیا۔ اب وہ پانچویں درجے پر موجود سان فرانسسکو سے صرف پانچ پوائنٹس پیچھے ہے۔ ماہرین سوئٹزرلینڈ کے مضبوط ریگولیٹری نظام اور کم بدعنوانی کو اس ترقی کی وجہ قرار دیتے ہیں۔

فرینکفرٹ، جو یورپی سینٹرل بینک اور جرمنی کے بنڈس بینک کا مرکز ہے، نے پیرس کو پیچھے چھوڑ کر یورپ میں تیسرا سب سے اہم مالیاتی مرکز بن گیا ہے۔ وہ عالمی سطح پر 17 ویں سے 14 ویں نمبر پر آنے کے ساتھ، پیرس 14 ویں سے 15 ویں پر چلا گیا ہے۔ دونوں کے درمیان صرف ایک رینکنگ پوائنٹ کا فرق ہے۔ فرینکفرٹ ان 15 شہروں میں سے ایک ہے جن کے بارے میں سروے میں پیش گوئی کی گئی ہے کہ ان کی اہمیت مزید بڑھے گی۔

دیگر یورپی شہروں میں جو ٹاپ 20 میں ہیں: لگژمبرگ (16 واں)، زیورخ (18 واں) اور ایمسٹرڈیم (19 واں) شامل ہیں۔

جرمنی کے پانچ شہر گلوبل ٹاپ 50 میں شامل ہیں—جو یورپ میں کسی بھی ملک سے زیادہ ہے—اگرچہ کوئی بھی ٹاپ 10 میں نہیں۔ فرینکفرٹ کے ساتھ، برلن 23 ویں، میونخ 26 ویں، شٹوٹگارٹ 46 ویں اور ہیمبرگ 49 ویں پوزیشن پر ہیں۔ سوئٹزرلینڈ کا لوگانو 47 ویں پر ہے، جبکہ برطانیہ کا ایڈنبرا 34 ویں نمبر پر ہے۔ اضافی ٹاپ 50 یورپی شہروں میں ڈبلن (25 واں)، اسٹاک ہوم (40 واں)، اوسلو (42 واں)، میلان (45 واں)، میڈرڈ (48 واں) اور ہیلسنکی (50 واں) شامل ہیں۔ ان کے اسکور ایک دوسرے کے قریب ہیں، جو اگلے GFCI رپورٹ میں ممکنہ تبدیلیوں کی نشاندہی کرتے ہیں۔

تین برطانوی کراؤن ڈپینڈنسیز—جرسی (52 واں)، گرنزی (58 واں)، اور آئل آف مین (59 واں)—ٹاپ 60 میں شامل ہیں۔ یہ برطانیہ کا حصہ نہیں ہیں بلکہ برطانوی کراؤن کے تحت خودمختار علاقے ہیں۔

GFCI یورپ کو دو گروپوں میں تقسیم کرتا ہے: مغربی یورپ، اور مشرقی یورپ و وسط ایشیا۔ اس سے مشرق و مغرب میں واضح فرق سامنے آتا ہے۔ 60 ویں نمبر تک، یورپ کے سارے بہترین مالیاتی مراکز مغربی یورپ میں ہیں۔ قازقستان کا آستانہ 60 ویں، پراگ 79 ویں اور ٹالین 87 ویں نمبر پر ہیں۔

یورپ سے باہر، امریکہ کے پانچ مالیاتی مراکز عالمی ٹاپ 10 میں شامل ہیں، جو اس کی معاشی طاقت کو ظاہر کرتا ہے۔ صف اول کے چینی مالیاتی مراکز بھی عالمی ٹاپ 20 میں آتے ہیں۔

GFCI 34 کے مطابق، کسی شہر کی ساکھ اور کاروباری ماحول اس کی مالیاتی مسابقت سے منسلک ہے۔ کرپشن پرسیپشن انڈیکس اور اکنامک فریڈم آف دی ورلڈ انڈیکس سے پتا چلتا ہے کہ معاشی آزادی میں اضافہ اور بدعنوانی کی کمی سے شہروں کی درجہ بندی میں اضافہ ہوتا ہے۔ شہر کی برینڈنگ جیسے عوامل—حفاظت، استحکام، ثقافتی سہولیات اور معیار زندگی—ایک شہر کی شہرت بڑھاتے ہیں اور کاروبار، پیشہ ورانہ افراد اور سرمایہ کاروں کو راغب کرتے ہیں۔

article_content: Police in Rustenberg, South Africa, clashed on Tuesday with more than 1,000 striking miners who were blocking public roads near the Anglo American Platinum mine. Authorities used tear gas and rubber bullets to disperse the crowd, and sporadic confrontations continued, according to Capt. Dennis Adrio of the North West police. Police and firefighters also responded after a power substation on the Anglo American Platinum property was set on fire at 4 a.m., Adrio said. Tuesday's violence is part of an ongoing wave of unauthorized strikes and confrontations in South Africa's mining sector, described as the worst labor unrest since the end of apartheid. Earlier this month, Anglo American Platinum fired about 12,000 striking workers who refused to attend disciplinary hearings following a three-week walkout. Last week, Gold Fields Limited also dismissed 8,100 workers after they did not return to work. Around 15,000 workers at Gold Fields' KDC East mine near Johannesburg had joined the strikes demanding higher pay, alongside miners from several other South African mines. Repeated clashes have occurred since August, when police opened fire on strikers at Lonmin's Marikana platinum mine, killing 34 workers and injuring dozens more. Mining remains South Africa's largest industry.

article_content: A majority of those seeking help for substance abuse at Bengaluru's Cadabams Hospital are between 36 and 55 years old, often accompanied by family members such as parents, siblings, or spouses, hospital officials report. Neha Cadabam, senior psychologist and executive director, explains that 60–64% of patients generally stay in recovery for the first three to six months post-discharge, although maintaining recovery over longer periods depends on personal circumstances, motivation, and support networks. The hospital treats not only substance use disorders but also other forms of addiction and behavioral issues. Treatment duration is tailored to the individual, depending on the addiction’s severity and any existing mental health problems. For patients with both addiction and psychiatric conditions, a specialized dual diagnosis program is available, typically lasting about six months to provide thorough care and improve long-term outcomes. Cadabams offers several treatment programs, including a comprehensive de-addiction plan based on evidence-based methods to lower risks and foster self-understanding, an intensive 90-day program to help patients avoid relapse and develop independence, and a dual diagnosis program combining therapy for those facing substance use alongside conditions like psychosis or bipolar disorder. Program selection is informed by factors such as the level of substance dependence, impact on social or occupational life, medical conditions, motivation, and the person’s history with addiction. The hospital acknowledges that relapse is a natural part of recovery and provides ongoing support through a relapse prevention program. This holistic approach includes medical treatment, psychological counseling, dietary guidance, and diverse activities to help patients recover. For individuals experiencing both addiction and mental health disorders—including substance-induced psychosis, bipolar disorder, or schizophrenia—a six-month dual diagnosis program is recommended. Factors contributing to dual diagnoses may involve genetic predisposition, chronic substance use, overdose, and significant life stressors. The National Mental Health Survey (2015–16) found that 0.6% of respondents were dependent on substances, including cannabis, stimulants, opioids, and prescription medications, based on interviews with 39,532 people. The National Institute of Mental Health and Neurosciences, Bengaluru, identifies signs of substance abuse as including: looking intoxicated (droopy eyelids, red eyes, strange smells), altered sleep habits (being too sleepy, sleeplessness, or restless), declining health (frequent sickness, nasal or chest symptoms), worsening personal hygiene, and significant appetite or weight changes.

Male, Maldives — Maldives president-elect Mohamed Muiz has reaffirmed his campaign pledge to expel Indian military personnel stationed in the island nation. Addressing his supporters Monday night after his election victory, Muiz stated he would not permit a foreign military presence in the Maldives against the desires of its people.

“The people have told us that they don't want foreign military here,” Muiz declared. His stance is considered a setback for India in its ongoing geopolitical competition with China in the Indian Ocean, with Saturday’s presidential runoff widely viewed as a referendum on which regional power would dominate the Maldives.

Outgoing President Ibrahim Mohamed Solih, who took office in 2018, faced accusations from Muiz that he had tolerated unchecked Indian influence in the country. Muiz’s party, the People’s National Congress, is seen as pro-China, and his campaign has centered on concerns about national sovereignty related to the presence of Indian military personnel — part of a long-running "India Out" movement.

Solih, for his part, argued that Indian troops were present solely to build a dockyard under a bilateral agreement, insisting this did not compromise the Maldives’ sovereignty. The exact number of Indian troops in the Maldives remains undisclosed. Critics indicate that secrecy surrounding the agreement and the troops’ specific roles has fueled rumors and suspicion.

Indian forces have participated in activities such as operating helicopters donated by India and assisting with rescue operations at sea. During his 2013–2018 presidency, former president Abdulla Yameen, who leads the People’s National Congress, aligned the Maldives with China’s Belt and Road Initiative, which aims to expand trade and infrastructure networks across Asia, Africa, and Europe. 

On Sunday, Yameen was transferred from prison to house arrest, a campaign promise delivered by Muiz ahead of his official swearing-in scheduled for November 17th. The Maldives—a chain of 1,200 coral islands—lies along a key shipping route between East and West in the Indian Ocean.

article_content: The United Nations Security Council is now set to vote on Wednesday, October 18, on a resolution drafted by Brazil that calls for humanitarian pauses in the ongoing conflict between Israel and Palestinian group Hamas, to allow aid access to the Gaza Strip. The council is also expected, at the request of the United Arab Emirates and Russia, to discuss the recent blast at a Gaza hospital, which killed hundreds of people, diplomats said. Palestinian UN envoy Riyad Mansour blamed Israeli forces for the hospital attack, describing it as a massacre and calling for an immediate ceasefire. Israel's UN Ambassador Gilad Erdan accused the Palestinian Islamic Jihad militant group of being responsible for the explosion, but Islamic Jihad has denied the allegation. Reuters was unable to independently verify responsibility for the blast. The 15-member council was originally scheduled to vote on the Brazilian draft on Monday, but the vote was postponed for further negotiations. The United States then requested another delay, as President Joe Biden prepares to visit Israel on Wednesday. It is unclear whether the US, which holds veto power and often supports Israel in Security Council matters, will allow the resolution to pass. The proposed text also urges Israel—without naming the country directly—to rescind its order instructing Gaza civilians to move to the south of the enclave.

article_content: House Democratic Leader Nancy Pelosi has appointed Reps. James Clyburn (South Carolina), Xavier Becerra (California), and Chris Van Hollen (Maryland) to the bipartisan congressional 'super committee' on deficit reduction, finalizing the 12-member panel established under last week's debt ceiling agreement. This committee is tasked with developing a comprehensive plan to address the nation’s growing deficit. The Democratic appointees join three Senate Democrats—Patty Murray, Max Baucus, and John Kerry—as well as six Republican members named by GOP leaders. Pelosi emphasized the importance of a 'grand bargain' that reduces the deficit while strengthening Medicare, Medicaid, and Social Security. The House Democratic leadership affirmed their commitment to working with the appointees toward this goal. Clyburn, the third-ranking House Democrat, and Van Hollen, the top Democrat on the House Budget Committee, both pledged to uphold Democratic priorities, while Becerra insisted on bipartisan negotiations free of rigid preconditions. Among the Republicans, the House appointees are Jeb Hensarling (Texas), Dave Camp (Michigan), and Fred Upton (Michigan), while the Senate appointees are Jon Kyl (Arizona), Pat Toomey (Pennsylvania), and Rob Portman (Ohio), all known for fiscal conservatism. Hensarling, set to co-chair the panel alongside Patty Murray, stressed the urgency of addressing the debt crisis and the importance of bipartisan cooperation. Statements from committee members reflected a shared acknowledgement of the challenge and the need to find common ground without abandoning core principles. The committee’s assignment follows earlier debt reduction efforts in Congress, including those by President Obama’s bipartisan commission and the 'Gang of Six.' President Obama has called for a balanced approach that asks major corporations and the wealthy to contribute their fair share. The committee must propose at least $1.5 trillion in deficit reduction by November 23, after which Congress has until December 23 to vote on the package without amendments. Failure to reach an agreement triggers automatic, across-the-board federal spending cuts, including defense. A new CNN/ORC International poll showed that 63% of Americans support higher taxes for wealthier individuals and businesses, 57% endorse major domestic spending cuts, and most oppose significant changes to Social Security and Medicare. Also, most Americans do not favor tax increases for the middle and lower classes. Recent highly partisan negotiations, unresolved disputes over taxes and spending, and the uncertainty regarding a debt ceiling deal, were factors in Standard & Poor's downgrading the U.S. credit rating. The competing visions for deficit reduction remain: Democrats advocate a mix of spending cuts, increased revenue, and entitlement reforms, while Republicans favor spending cuts and entitlement changes without raising revenue.

(مشیگن)، اور فریڈ اپٹن (مشیگن) ایوان سے جبکہ جان کیل (ایریزونا)، پیٹ ٹومی (پنسلوانیا)، اور راب پورٹ مین (اوہائیو) سینیٹ سے شامل ہیں، یہ سب مالی طور پر قدامت پسند جانے جاتے ہیں۔ ہنسارلنگ جو پینل کے article_content: While India vs New Zealand is not seen as one of cricket’s greatest rivalries, their matchups have produced many thrilling, high-stakes moments. In the 1980s, 1990s, and early 2000s, both teams were evenly matched, but over the past decade, India has typically had the advantage. However, India’s defeat to New Zealand in the 2019 World Cup semifinal still resonates, building anticipation for every knockout clash between the sides. Here are five of the most nail-biting India-New Zealand ODI matches in the past 40 years: 1. 1985 Benson and Hedges Semifinal, SCG (India won by 7 wickets): The score suggests an easy win, but India had to dig deep on a tough pitch chasing 207. At 102/3, the required rate rose above six per over—challenging for that era. Captain Sunil Gavaskar promoted Kapil Dev up the order; his unbeaten 54 from 37 balls turned the match. Dilip Vengsarkar’s steady 63* saw India into the final against Pakistan, which India won. 2. 1990 Rothman’s Cup Tri-series, Wellington (India won by 1 run): With Mohd Azharuddin in his first stint as captain and India desperate for a win, runs from Kapil Dev (46) and Sachin Tendulkar (36) took India to a total of 221. New Zealand seemed to have control, but Manoj Prabhakar (3/37) bowled a brilliant penultimate over. With 10 needed from the last, Kapil Dev bowled out Richard Hadlee with the final ball and India clinched victory by a single run. 3. 2000 ICC Champions Trophy Final, Nairobi (NZ won by 4 wickets): Sourav Ganguly’s superb 117 led India to 264/6. New Zealand’s Chris Cairns returned from injury to play a match-winning knock of 102* not out, helping the Kiwis surpass the target with two balls to go. 4. 2003 Bilateral Series, 6th ODI, Auckland (India won by 1 wicket): The series was already decided, but pride and World Cup spots were at stake. After bowling NZ out for 199, Virender Sehwag attacked for a fluent 112. Late wickets saw India collapse to 198/9, but Javagal Srinath and Ashish Nehra held on for a narrow win. 5. 2019 World Cup Semifinal, Old Trafford (NZ won by 18 runs): Rain interrupted the match, and India seemed poised for victory after holding NZ to 239/8. But a new ball and seaming conditions saw India reduced to 5/3. Ravindra Jadeja’s 77 and MS Dhoni steadied the innings, but a superb Martin Guptill run out ended Dhoni’s international career and India’s World Cup campaign. Honourable Mentions: - Chetan Sharma took India’s first ODI hat-trick, and Sunil Gavaskar struck his only ODI hundred against New Zealand in the 1987 World Cup. - Mohd Azharuddin’s 108 off 65 balls in Baroda held the Indian record for fastest ODI hundred until Sehwag broke it in 2009. - Sachin Tendulkar’s debut as ODI opener in 1994 at Auckland’s Eden Park—scoring 82 off 49 balls—is still celebrated.

آخری وکٹ پر جیت یقینی بنائی۔ 5۔ 2019 ورلڈ کپ سیمی فائنل، اولڈ ٹریفورڈ (نیوزی لینڈ نے 18 رنز سے جیتا): بارش سے متاثرہ اس میچ میں بھارت نے نیوزی لینڈ کو 239/8 تک محدود کر دیا، مگر نئے گیند نے بھارت کو 5/3 تک گرا دیا۔ رویندر جڈیجہ کی 77 رنز اور ایم ایس دھونی کی مزاحمت نے امید بحال کی، مگر مارٹن گپٹل کے شاندار تھرو پر دھونی رن آؤٹ ہوئے اور بھارت کا ورلڈ کپ سفر اور دھونی کا انٹرنیشنل کیریئر ختم ہو article_content: Elon Musk, owner of X (formerly Twitter), criticized competitor Meta, expressing skepticism about CEO Mark Zuckerberg's activity on Threads, Meta's social media platform designed to rival Twitter. Musk made these remarks during the latest episode of 'The Joe Rogan Experience' podcast, aired on Tuesday, where he also discussed a variety of topics like Tesla's Cybertruck and courtroom sketches of former FTX founder Sam Bankman-Fried. When host Joe Rogan described Threads as a 'ghost town' despite its initially strong launch, Musk responded, 'Yeah, it's eerily quiet. I mean, Zuck himself doesn't post. You’ve got to use your own product.' However, Mark Zuckerberg appears to be active on Threads, currently having 3.5 million followers and generally posting every one to two weeks. His most recent post was about the platform introducing polls and GIF attachments, which he shared five days ago, according to Insider’s review. He also regularly interacts with users by replying to their posts. In contrast, Musk posts multiple times daily on X and is highly engaged with platform users. During the podcast, Musk also joked about Instagram, another Meta-owned platform, saying, 'There was a time when I posted on Instagram, but I found myself just doing selfies. And I’m like, “What is going on? Why am I posting selfies to get likes? This is crazy,”' while laughing. This was not the first time Musk criticized Zuckerberg’s competitive efforts. Previously, he challenged Zuckerberg to a cage fight and mocked Instagram when Threads was launched. Meta introduced Threads in July, following speculation about a new Twitter competitor. The app saw more than ten million sign-ups in its first seven hours. According to Apptopia, monthly active users on Threads reached 120 million by October, up from 100 million in July. While user engagement slowed after the initial boom, Zuckerberg remains optimistic, saying, 'Once we’re in a good place with basic functionality, I’m confident we can drive more growth,' during Meta’s second-quarter earnings call. Representatives for Musk and Zuckerberg did not immediately respond to requests for comment from Insider sent outside regular business hours.

article_content: The Karnataka High Court has clarified that merely accepting guilt is not sufficient grounds for a Motor Accident Claims Tribunal to make a decision. In a recent case, Justice Lalitha Kanneghanti observed that claimants must provide independent evidence when filing under Section 166 of the Motor Vehicles Act. This ruling came while allowing an appeal by United Insurance Company Limited. The case concerned an accident on November 24, 2009, involving two motorcycles in Kundapur, Udupi district. The tribunal had previously awarded Rs 60,670 in compensation to victim Ganesh Achar, based mainly on the alleged admission of guilt by Raghavendra Achar, the owner of the other vehicle. Both the insurer and Ganesh Achar contested the tribunal’s verdict, with the claimant seeking Rs 5.7 lakh. The insurance company argued the legitimacy of the claim, citing the late complaint (filed on January 30, 2010), delayed spot inspection (February 6, 2010), and wound certificate (issued on February 20, 2010), all casting doubt on the vehicle’s involvement. The insurer also alleged possible collusion between the vehicle owner and the claimant. Ultimately, Justice Kanneghanti noted that despite the charge-sheet supporting the claimant's case, the discrepancies in the timeline led the court to reject both parties' contentions regarding the involvement of the alleged vehicle, overturning the tribunal's finding.

article_content: Pope Francis has shared that he sometimes feels 'like he is in a cage' due to the security measures that come with his role. While on his first overseas trip in Brazil, he told young Roman Catholics at Rio de Janeiro Cathedral that he longs to be closer to them, but public order concerns prevent it. He asked for their prayers, saying, 'I need your prayers.' During his visit to Rio, Pope Francis expressed regret at not being able to get closer to the crowds. His desire to connect has led to spontaneous walkabouts, sometimes worrying Vatican officials. Despite the large crowds and his global influence, Francis appeared relatable when gusts of wind tangled his robes during a mass at Copacabana Beach. Unfazed, he continued the service as thousands braved rain to attend. Staying true to his modest approach, Francis celebrated Mass with fellow Jesuits and heard confessions from young pilgrims in a Rio park. Five young people, chosen by raffle, had the personal experience of confessing to the Pope. Estefani Lescano from Venezuela said Francis told them that young people are responsible for keeping the Church alive. Persistent rain over several days forced the main Mass of the festival to move from Guaratiba Field to Copacabana Beach. Francis also met with juvenile detainees, continuing his commitment to marginalized people from his time as Archbishop of Buenos Aires. On Thursday, Francis visited the Varginha slum, one of Rio’s most violent neighborhoods, showing support for the poor. He was warmly received, mingling with residents and assuring them of the Church’s support. At World Youth Day events, Francis called on young Catholics to be active in their faith and 'shake up' the Church. Speaking to thousands of Argentine pilgrims, he encouraged them to 'make a mess' in their dioceses, warning against the Church becoming closed and isolated. His spontaneous style and reform-minded leadership have begun to reshape traditional Vatican practices since his election.

article_content: OpenAI, the artificial intelligence company, experienced major internal upheaval when CEO Sam Altman was abruptly dismissed and then rehired within days. This incident highlighted ongoing disagreements about the company’s direction and underlying structure. Founded in 2015 by Sam Altman, Elon Musk, and others, OpenAI began as a nonprofit with the mission to develop AI for humanity's benefit rather than for profit. After Elon Musk left the board in 2018—citing a lack of funding—the organization's leadership acknowledged the high costs of AI development and established a for-profit arm, capping investor returns and channeling extra funds back into the company. Despite major financial backing from Microsoft, which invested $13 billion, the nonprofit board retained ultimate decision-making power, including over the CEO. Disputes over how fast OpenAI should commercialize its AI products, and debates about the ethical risks involved, led to Altman's firing. The board vaguely cited issues with Altman’s transparency. However, the vast majority of OpenAI's employees, 702 out of 770, threatened to resign unless Altman was reinstated, prompting both his return and the formation of a new, temporary board. This new board retains one previous member, Adam D’Angelo, and adds tech veteran Bret Taylor and former Treasury Secretary Larry Summers, with the possibility of Microsoft getting a board seat in the future. OpenAI’s charter advocates for AI advancement that benefits all people and avoids excessive power concentration. Yet, as OpenAI gains more financial supporters, tension persists between its original mission and the realities of operating in a competitive industry. The new board must now evaluate if OpenAI’s hybrid model can effectively serve both its ethical vision and business goals.

article_content: An 18-year-old woman, Jordan Armstrong, was rescued after her arm became lodged in her sister's letterbox in Colchester, Essex. Returning from a night out, she arrived at her sister Anja-Marie’s home in the early morning and found the front door locked. Unable to walk home after attending a nearby party, she attempted to unlock the door by reaching through the letterbox but got stuck. Her friends called firefighters at 2:30 a.m. on Saturday, who freed her with a crowbar. Paramedics were also at the scene, but she did not need hospital treatment. Friends shared photos of the predicament on Snapchat. Jordan praised the emergency teams and admitted she’d had too much to drink. Her sister discovered the incident after reading about it online. The East of England Ambulance Service confirmed medics attended but did not take her to hospital.

article_content: AIX-EN-PROVENCE, France – England head coach Steve Borthwick has made notable changes for Sunday’s Rugby World Cup quarter-final against Fiji. George Ford has been moved to the bench, with Owen Farrell starting at flyhalf and Marcus Smith at fullback. Manu Tuilagi will partner Joe Marchant in the centres, while Elliot Daly returns on the left wing and Jonny May lines up on the right. Borthwick revealed his team on Friday, including experienced prop Dan Cole in the starting lineup ahead of Kyle Sinckler. Ellis Genge and Jamie George complete the front row, preparing for a tough battle against Fiji’s strong and improved scrum. “Everyone knows just what an unpredictably dangerous opposition Fiji can be,” Borthwick said. “However, we have shown in the group stages how we can win games, and we will rely on that experience and determination as we continue our journey.” Ford was named man of the match in the first two games while Farrell was suspended, but the pairing struggled against Samoa, leading to Ford’s early substitution. Borthwick reiterated his support for Farrell throughout the week, with Ford moving to the bench as a result. The most significant tactical change is Smith, usually a flyhalf for Harlequins, starting at fullback. Smith has been England’s most dynamic player in the tournament. Freddie Steward, after starting 28 consecutive matches at fullback, was rested for the Chile game, returned against Samoa, but is left out of the squad for Sunday due to Smith’s attacking prowess. With Ford on the bench, Smith is set to assume the secondary playmaker role. “I’ve always been impressed with Marcus,” said Farrell. “He always wants the ball and to make a difference. He’s played and won big games, including the Premiership, and as a fullback has made a notable impact.” Moving Farrell back to flyhalf allows the inclusion of two specialist centres, Tuilagi and Marchant, to handle Fiji’s direct runners. Borthwick said, “You have a great blend: Manu’s power and defense, and Joe’s attacking skills and connections. The starting back three fits our needs this week. Marcus has embraced the opportunity, and having players able to perform at the highest level in multiple roles is a true asset.” England hold seven wins over Fiji, with the only defeat in their most recent encounter at Twickenham in August. “That feels a long time ago,” Farrell remarked. “We’ve reviewed that match, but we feel we’ve moved forward now.” England Team to face Fiji: 15. بورتھوک نے جمعہ کو اپنی ٹیم کا اعلان کیا، جس میں تجربہ کار پروپ ڈین کول کو کائل سنکلر پر ترجیح دے کر ابتدائی ٹیم میں شامل کیا گیا ہے۔ ایلس گینج اور جیمی جارج فرنٹ رو مکمل کرتے ہیں، جو فجی کے مضبوط اور کر دیا گیا۔ بورتھوک نے ہفتہ بھر فیریل کی بھرپور حمایت کا اظہار کیا، اس وجہ سے فورڈ اب بینچ پر ہیں۔ سب سے نمایاں تبدیلی یہ ہے کہ اسمتھ، جو عام طور پر ہارلی کوئنز کے لیے فلائی ہاف کھیلتے ہیں، اب فل بیک کے طور پر کھیلیں گے۔ اسمتھ اس ٹورنامنٹ میں انگلینڈ کے سب سے متحرک کھلاڑی رہے ہیں۔ فریڈی سٹیورڈ، جنہوں نے فل بیک پر 28 مسلسل میچز کھیلے، چلی کے میچ کے لیے آرام کیا، پھر ساموا کے خلاف واپس آئے لیکن اسپیشلسٹ سینٹرز، تولگی اور مارچنٹ کو موقع ملا ہے، جو فجی کے ڈائریکٹ رنرز کو سنبھالیں گے۔ بورتھوک نے کہا: “یہاں بہترین امتزاج ہے: مانو کی طاقت اور دفاع، اور جو کی اٹیکنگ مہارتیں اور کنکشن۔ ہماری بیک article_content: Two Iranian warships have passed through Egypt's Suez Canal into the Mediterranean Sea, according to Iran's semi-official Mehr news agency. This is only the second time Iranian ships have crossed the canal since the Islamic Republic's 1979 revolution. The first crossing occurred in February 2011, shortly after Egypt's government, following the departure of Hosni Mubarak, approved the passage—placing Egypt's new leadership in a delicate position with neighboring Israel. Rear Admiral Habibollah Sayyari said, as reported by Mehr, 'The Navy's 18th fleet will carry the message of peace and friendship to regional countries and demonstrate the strength of the Islamic Republic of Iran.' The report did not specify the destination of the two vessels, a destroyer and a supply ship, but Iran's ISNA news agency indicated they are likely headed to Syria. The Suez Canal is controlled by Egypt, which is bound by the 1978 Camp David Accords, guaranteeing free passage for all nations' ships, consistent with the Constantinople Convention of 1888. This movement comes amid ongoing tensions between Iran and Israel, with discussions about a possible Israeli strike on Iran's suspected nuclear weapons program. Israel has also accused Iran of orchestrating attacks on Israeli targets in India, Georgia, and Thailand. The United States and the European Union tightened sanctions on Iran following a November International Atomic Energy Agency report suggesting Iran may be pursuing nuclear weapons. Iran insists its nuclear program is for civilian energy purposes. Western nations recently welcomed a letter from Iran offering to resume stalled nuclear talks, although they are still assessing Iran’s intentions. The Suez Canal is a vital route for international trade, linking the Mediterranean and Red Seas and allowing ships to travel between Europe and Asia without circumnavigating Africa. Millions of barrels of oil pass through the canal daily en route to Europe and North America. CNN's Shirzad Bozorgmehr contributed to this report.
translated_content: ایران کے دو جنگی جہاز مصر کی سویز نہر سے گزر کر بحیرہ روم میں داخل ہو گئے، ایران کی نیم سرکاری خبر ایجنسی مہر کے مطابق۔ یہ اسلامی جمہوریہ ایران کے 1979 انقلاب کے بعد صرف دوسرا موقع ہے کہ ایرانی جہازوں نے سویز نہر عبور کی ہے۔ پہلی بار فروری 2011 میں، مصر کی حکومت میں تبدیلی کے فوراً بعد، یہ اجازت دی گئی تھی، جس سے نئی قیادت کو اسرائیل کے ساتھ حساس صورتِ حال کا سامنا کرنا پڑا۔ مہر کے حوالے سے، ریئر ایڈمرل حبیب اللہ سیاری نے کہا، 'بحریہ کا اٹھارہواں فلیٹ علاقائی ممالک کے لیے امن اور دوستی کا پیغام لے کر جائے گا اور اسلامی جمہوریہ کی طاقت دکھائے گا۔' رپورٹ میں دونوں بحری جہازوں، ایک ڈسٹرائر اور ایک سپلائی شپ، کی منزل واضح نہیں، لیکن ایران کی آئی ایس این اے خبر ایجنسی نے بتایا ہے کہ وہ غالباً شام کی طرف جا رہے ہیں۔ سویز نہر مصر کے کنٹرول میں ہے، جو 1978 کے کیمپ ڈیوڈ معاہدے کے تحت تمام ممالک کے بحری جہازوں کی آزادانہ آمد و رفت کی ضمانت دیتا ہے، جیسا کہ 1888 کے کانسٹینٹینپل کنونشن میں بیان کیا گیا ہے۔ یہ پیش رفت ایران اور اسرائیل کے درمیان موجودہ کشیدگی کے دوران ہوئی ہے، جس میں ایران کے ممکنہ جوہری ہتھیاروں کے پروگرام پر اسرائیلی حملے کی قیاس آرائیاں جاری ہیں۔ اسرائیل نے الزام لگایا ہے کہ ایران نے بھارت، جارجیا اور تھائی لینڈ میں اسرائیلی اہداف پر حملوں کی منصوبہ بندی کی۔ امریکہ اور یورپی یونین نے ایران پر پابندیاں اس وقت سخت کیں، جب نومبر میں آئی اے ای اے کی رپورٹ میں کہا گیا کہ ایران جوہری ہتھیار بنا سکتا ہے۔ ایران کا مؤقف ہے کہ اس کا جوہری پروگرام صرف سول توانائی کے لیے ہے۔ مغربی ممالک نے حال ہی میں ایران کے اس خط کا خیرمقدم کیا ہے جس میں رکی ہوئی جوہری بات چیت دوبارہ شروع کرنے کی پیشکش کی گئی، اگرچہ وہ اب بھی ایران کی سنجیدگی کا جائزہ لے رہے ہیں۔ سویز نہر بین الاقوامی تجارت کا ایک اہم راستہ ہے جو بحیرہ روم اور بحیرہ احمر کو ملاتی ہے اور بحری جہازوں کو بنا افریقہ کے گرد چکر لگائے یورپ اور ایشیا کے درمیان سفر کی سہولت دیتی ہے۔ روزانہ لاکھوں بیرل تیل اس نہر سے یورپ اور شمالی امریکہ منتقل ہوتے ہیں۔ سی این این کے شرزاد بزرگمہر نے اس رپورٹ میں تعاون کیا۔

article_content: A Canadian military surveillance plane conducting a United Nations sanctions enforcement mission near North Korea was approached by a Chinese fighter jet in international airspace off the coast of China, according to Canada’s defence minister. The Chinese jet reportedly flew within five meters (16 feet) of the Canadian plane over international waters, posing significant risk to the crew. Defence Minister Bill Blair told reporters that the incident occurred on Monday. He emphasized this was not the first such encounter between Canadian and Chinese aircraft. In June 2022, after similar accusations by Canada, China claimed Ottawa was using UN Security Council resolutions to justify increased reconnaissance near Chinese territory. Chinese Ministry of National Defence spokesperson Senior Colonel Wu Qian stated this in comments reported by the state-run Global Times. Blair said that while the Chinese Air Force routinely interacts with UN mission aircraft, this particular episode was especially dangerous. "I am very concerned about the unprofessional way in which this was done. It was quite frankly dangerous and reckless. Such behaviours are never acceptable, and we will express that to the People's Republic of China in the most appropriate way," he said, without providing further details. Canadian journalists from Global News, who were on board the surveillance flight, filmed the encounters. According to their report, at least two different Chinese jets intercepted the plane multiple times over the mission, which lasted more than eight hours. Most intercepts were described by crew and the military as professional, but the final encounter involved a jet, armed with air-to-air missiles, flying aggressively and in close proximity, sometimes appearing in the Canadian plane’s blind spot. In May, the Pentagon reported that a Chinese fighter jet conducted an "unnecessarily aggressive" maneuver near a US military aircraft in international airspace over the South China Sea.
translated_content: ایک کینیڈین فوجی نگرانی کا طیارہ، جو شمالی کوریا پر اقوام متحدہ کی پابندیوں کے نفاذ کے مشن پر تھا، کو چین کے ساحل کے قریب بین الاقوامی فضائی حدود میں ایک چینی لڑاکا طیارے نے قریب آکر روکا، کینیڈا کے وزیر دفاع کے مطابق۔ بتایا گیا ہے کہ چینی طیارہ کینیڈین جہاز کے پانچ میٹر (16 فٹ) کے اندر آ گیا، جس سے عملے کو شدید خطرہ لاحق ہو گیا۔ وزیر دفاع بل بلیئر نے رپورٹرز کو بتایا کہ یہ واقعہ پیر کے روز پیش آیا۔ انہوں نے زور دیا کہ یہ پہلا ایسا واقعہ نہیں ہے جب کینیڈین اور چینی طیاروں کے درمیان اس طرح کا سامنا ہوا ہو۔ جون 2022 میں، کینیڈا کی طرف سے اسی طرح کے الزامات کے بعد، چین نے دعویٰ کیا کہ اوٹاوا اقوام متحدہ کی سلامتی کونسل کی قراردادوں کو چینی سرزمین کے قریب اپنی نگرانی بڑھانے کے لیے جواز کے طور پر استعمال کر رہا ہے۔ چین کی وزارت دفاع کے ترجمان سینئر کرنل وو کیان نے یہ بات سرکاری میڈیا گلوبل ٹائمز کو بتائی۔ بلیئر نے کہا کہ اگرچہ چینی فضائیہ عام طور پر اقوام متحدہ کے مشن کے طیاروں کے ساتھ رابطے میں رہتی ہے، لیکن یہ واقعہ خاص طور پر خطرناک تھا۔ "مجھے اس غیر پیشہ ورانہ رویے پر بہت تشویش ہے۔ یہ بالکل خطرناک اور لاپرواہی تھا۔ اس طرح کے رویے کبھی بھی قابل قبول نہیں ہیں، اور ہم اس پر عوامی جمہوریہ چین سے مناسب طریقے سے اظہار خیال کریں گے،" انہوں نے بغیر مزید تفصیلات دیئے کہا۔ کینیڈین ویب سائٹ گلوبل نیوز کے صحافی، جو نگرانی کے اس مشن میں طیارے پر سوار تھے، نے ان مناظر کو فلمایا۔ ان کی رپورٹ کے مطابق، کم از کم دو مختلف چینی طیاروں نے آٹھ گھنٹے سے زائد دورانیے کے اس مشن کے دوران متعدد بار کینیڈین جہاز کو روکا۔ بیشتر مواقع پر انٹرسیپٹ کو عملے اور فوجی حکام نے پیشہ ورانہ قرار دیا لیکن آخری بار ایک ایسے جہاز نے، جو فضاء سے فضاء میں مار کرنے والے میزائل سے لیس تھا، خطرناک انداز میں قریب آ کر پرواز کی اور گاہے بہ گاہے کینیڈین جہاز کے بلائنڈ اسپاٹ میں آتا رہا۔ مئی میں پنٹاگون نے بتایا تھا کہ ایک چینی لڑاکا طیارے نے جنوبی چین کے سمندر میں بین الاقوامی فضائی حدود میں امریکی فوجی جہاز کے قریب 'غیر ضروری طور پر جارحانہ' حرکت کی تھی۔

article_content: After years of planning, Santiago Puértolas is now saving nearly all of his low six-figure income. At 26, Puértolas began mapping out his savings strategy over seven years ago while in college. His plan focused on maximizing his earnings, building multiple streams of passive income, and keeping expenses low. According to documents reviewed by Insider, he has recently achieved his goal of saving about 95% of his income from his corporate strategy job at a tech company. Puértolas is among those who choose to live below their means, spending only a small percentage of their income on living expenses. For him, this approach means making sacrifices now for a more comfortable life later, though he says it has not affected his well-being. His minimalist philosophy centers on minimizing spending and leading as simple a life as possible. He believes happiness does not depend on spending. This mindset has led him to coach young professionals and businesses on reaching financial and professional goals. Realizing he would need to buy a home, he found a property in a small, relatively inexpensive town in the Canary Islands, negotiating for a price below market value. The area’s low cost of living, closeness to nature, and real estate opportunities appealed to him. He and his partner paid for the house in full from savings and are dividing it into three parts: one for themselves, one for Airbnb rentals, and one for long-term rentals. Puértolas is also building his investment portfolio to further grow passive income. He prepares about 80% of his meals at home on a monthly food budget of around 200 euros (about $210) and only dines out twice a week at affordable restaurants. He travels mainly on low-cost flights to see family and friends, spending about 150 euros per month. He rarely buys new clothes and owns just enough to fit in one suitcase. "There’s no one-size-fits-all—this lifestyle isn’t for everyone," Puértolas says. Most of his purchases are focused on utility and happiness, with a preference for experiences like nature and travel instead of costly items. "If you need a fancy laptop for work, buy it, but don’t get an expensive phone just to have one," he says. Puértolas attributes his frugality to his grandparents, who lived simply but comfortably, and to his parents’ lessons about working hard for both money and respect. After the 2008 financial crisis, his family became even more careful with spending. He held his first paid job at 16, which he says is unusual for teenagers in Spain, and started businesses during college to cover tuition. These ventures included a POS system for restaurants, ecommerce sites, and consulting work. While in college, he created a financial plan to determine how much he would need to save 1 million euros, deciding on the lowest practical spending possible without compromising his goals. Eventually, he moved away from a city—where, in his words, "just stepping outside costs $20"—and traveled worldwide to discover sources of happiness that didn’t rely on money. A trip to Myanmar, where he met a Buddhist monk, and adopting stoic principles further motivated him to live minimally. He invests only in purchases that add value. "I buy a car because it makes my life easier, but I choose the cheapest one because a more expensive car won’t improve my quality of life," Puértolas explains, noting he learned to repair his own car. His ultimate aim is to retire by 40 and live off passive income, while mentoring people and companies. The recent wave of layoffs in his industry pushed him to intensify his savings for greater security. "I just want peace and comfort and to reach a point where I don’t need to depend on a company salary," he says.

Sanel Sahbaz, a Bosnian national living in Hertford, UK, cannot be deported after a court found that doing so would violate his human rights. Sahbaz, who arrived in Britain as a child refugee in 1993, has been convicted of multiple offenses since 2005, including assault, theft, handling stolen goods, public order violations, and assaulting a police officer. In one incident, he attacked his landlord, knocking him to the floor and repeatedly kicking and stamping on his head, which rendered the landlord unconscious.

Sahbaz, now 30, became eligible for automatic deportation following a four-year prison sentence. The Home Office had initially ordered his removal from the country. However, Sahbaz challenged the decision in court, arguing that deportation would separate him from his parents, brother, and cousin—all of whom live in the UK—thereby breaching his right to a private and family life under Article 8 of the European Convention on Human Rights.

The High Court judge ruled in Sahbaz’s favor, allowing him to stay in the UK indefinitely. Critics of the decision say it highlights the urgent need for reform of immigration laws in the country.

article_content: Martin Castrogiovanni, formerly of Leicester Tigers and now with Toulon, has been found guilty of misconduct following a post-match outburst. The European Professional Club Rugby (EPCR) announced that after Toulon's 25-21 defeat to Leicester in the European Champions Cup, Castrogiovanni confronted journalists, directing harsh criticism and strong language toward his old club and Leicester’s director of rugby, Richard Cockerill, at Welford Road on December 7. The 33-year-old Italy international, who has 107 Test caps, appeared before an independent disciplinary committee in London. During the hearing, he admitted to the misconduct and expressed genuine regret for his actions. After considering all evidence and testimony, the committee concluded that Castrogiovanni was guilty of misconduct. As a result, he received a suspended four-match ban, which will only be imposed if he commits another similar offense before April 30, 2016. He must also donate 10,000 euros (about £7,926) to a Leicester-based charity and cover legal costs. The committee, chaired by Antony Davies, noted that although some remarks—such as calling Leicester 'amateur'—were made ironically and not as direct criticism, the overall comments were unacceptable. Richard Cockerill, who was the focus of much of the criticism, said the comments had harmed Castrogiovanni’s own reputation. Present with Castrogiovanni at the hearing were his lawyer Julian Pike, Toulon team manager Tom Whitford, and agent Matthew Ginvert. Notably, Castrogiovanni did not participate in the subsequent fixture between Toulon and Leicester.

article_content: The International Labour Organisation (ILO) has clarified that no country has national laws mandating a 70-hour work week. Instead, the global trend, especially among developed nations, has been moving towards a 40-hour work week, following the ILO’s Forty-Hour Week Convention. India stands among the earliest countries to have ratified ILO Convention 1 in 1921, which set the precedent for an eight-hour workday and a 48-hour work week in public and private industry. Previously, many nations had 60-hour work weeks. Anoop Satpathy, a wage expert at ILO India, points out that almost two dozen Indian labor laws confine working time to eight hours per day and 48 per week. Countries like Australia, New Zealand, and Korea are among the 15 that have accepted the ILO's Forty-Hour Week Convention, 1935. As a result, a standard 40-hour work week is now common in developed countries, while 48-hour weeks are prevalent in developing countries. While no law enforces a 70-hour work week, such long schedules can occur in particular jobs or sectors, sometimes as a matter of compliance. The ILO states that there is no strong link between lengthy working hours and higher productivity. In fact, routinely working excessive hours can reduce hourly efficiency and overall morale, and can lead to increased absenteeism and turnover, as shown in an ILO report from 2018.

article_content: Google, the internet giant, is acquiring leading robotics companies, including Boston Dynamics, famous for advanced robots such as Atlas and BigDog. This move is fueling debates about the future of automation and artificial intelligence, especially concerns about robots replacing humans in various jobs. Boston Dynamics is well-known for its innovative robots. BigDog can recover balance after slips or kicks, Cheetah can run at 28 mph (faster than Usain Bolt), and Atlas, a 6’2” bipedal robot, can drive, walk on rough terrain, and maintain balance after heavy impacts. Petman tests protective clothing, can climb stairs, and do push-ups. Wildcat can gallop swiftly, and Sand Flea is a small robot that can jump up to 30 feet. Much of Boston Dynamics’ work is backed by DARPA (the Defense Advanced Research Projects Agency) for military and hazardous environment tasks. While robots offer benefits in dangerous situations, their potential use in warfare raises concerns. Google’s purchase of Boston Dynamics is part of a wider plan, having acquired multiple robotics firms recently. Its robotics division, led by Andy Rubin, is described as a ‘moonshot’ project. Google remains secretive about exact plans, often shutting down newly acquired companies’ websites. Co-founder Larry Page and Andy Rubin believe robotics can free people from repetitive or risky work. Google also hired AI expert Ray Kurzweil, who suggests future technologies like nanobots could improve human health and lifespan. Other companies like Amazon are investing in automation too; both are developing delivery drones and driverless cars. Amazon’s CEO, Jeff Bezos, has predicted that drones could start delivering packages within a few years. Experts such as Professor Illah Nourbakhsh at Carnegie Mellon University highlight potential social impacts, including privacy issues and increased surveillance or ‘robot smog.’ There are worries about how much control humans will maintain as robots become widespread in daily life. Robots may have a big impact on elder care. Research shows older adults are open to having robots help with daily chores but prefer humans for more personal care. While there is no exact timeline for widespread use, many experts believe the rise of robots could happen sooner than most expect.

کریں گے۔ ماہرین جیسے پروفیسر الاہ نوربخش (کارنیگی میلن یونیورسٹی) اس بات کو اجاگر کرتے ہیں کہ سماجی مسائل جیسے پرائیویسی کے خدشات اور 'روبوٹ اسموگ' بڑھ سکتے ہیں۔ جیسے جیسے روبوٹس روزمرہ زندگی میں داخل ہوں، انسانوں کے کنٹرول میں کمی پر بھی فکر ظاہر کی جاتی ہے۔ روبوٹس بزرگوں کی دیکھ بھال میں بڑا کردار ادا کر سکتے ہیں۔ تحقیق سے پتا چلتا ہے کہ بڑی عمر کے افراد گھریلو کاموں میں روبوٹس کی مدد قبول کرتے article_content: Dan Lydiate has completed his move back to Wales, rejoining the Ospreys from Racing Metro in France under a National Dual Contract with the Welsh Rugby Union. The decision was also influenced by his desire to be near his wife’s family in West Wales after his previous tenure with the Newport Gwent Dragons. His return marks a significant attempt by Welsh rugby authorities to keep top players in the country. Now joining Sam Warburton, Lydiate is among the first to benefit from these National Dual Contracts, which are a joint initiative by the WRU and Welsh regions to prevent player migration to England and France. WRU Chairman Gareth Davies called Lydiate’s move a strong signal to Welsh players about the benefits of staying in Wales on such contracts. After facing difficulties adjusting to the French Top 14 league with Racing Metro, Lydiate is set to start training immediately with the Ospreys. The contract offers him clarity about his future and the ability to focus completely on rugby. Chief executive Roger Lewis described the deal as the end result of years of effort to secure dual contracts for Welsh players, calling it a landmark moment for Welsh rugby. This measure aims to strengthen both regional sides and the national team, while head coach Warren Gatland is confident the policy will improve Wales’s competitiveness and help retain talented players domestically.

article_content: In a lawsuit filed Monday night, X (formerly Twitter), led by Elon Musk, alleges that a report on content moderation by Media Matters drove away advertisers such as Apple and IBM. Last week, the media watchdog reported that advertisements from major brands appeared next to antisemitic content on the platform. However, Musk may also have influenced advertisers, as he shared controversial posts about Jewish people last week. The lawsuit claims Media Matters manipulated its findings by following both extremist accounts and those of major brands, presenting an unrealistic view of typical user experience. According to X, only two accounts out of the platform's 500 million reportedly saw antisemitic content beside Apple ads—Media Matters and one other user. These figures have not been independently verified. Media Matters President Angelo Carusone called the lawsuit 'frivolous' and accused X of trying to silence critics, stating the organization stands by its reporting. Since the report, Disney, Warner Bros. Discovery, Lionsgate, Paramount, Sony, and NBC Universal—the former employer of X CEO Linda Yaccarino—have all withdrawn advertising from X. Yaccarino, a veteran advertising executive brought on to reassure brands, remains supportive of Musk despite pressure, including criticism from Tesla investors and condemnation from the White House over Musk's statements. On Monday night, Yaccarino posted on X, 'When you’re this consequential, there will be detractors and fabricated distractions, but we’re unwavering in our mission. Thank you for standing with us.' During an all-hands meeting, Yaccarino told employees that the Media Matters report was misleading and manipulated. She emphasized that antisemitism has no place on X or anywhere in the world and that X is working to combat it. She also highlighted financial challenges, urging employees to find new revenue streams. X claims Media Matters aimed to damage its reputation by linking the platform to racist content. Despite X's claims, the platform recently hosted viral antisemitic materials, including Osama bin Laden’s ‘Letter to America,’ which received over 40 million views. Advertisers are seeking assurances that their ads will not appear alongside such content. It is currently unclear whether the Media Matters report or Musk’s own posts were more influential in sponsors withdrawing. Last week, Musk endorsed a white supremacist conspiracy theory accusing Jewish groups of hostility toward white people and suggesting that minorities and immigrants are the real threat. Musk responded to a tweet claiming that the American Defamation League, a Jewish advocacy group, cannot criticize minority groups they view as a threat.

article_content: A recent study suggests that women who have weight-loss surgery before becoming pregnant are less likely to have children who struggle with obesity. The research, led by Dr. Marie-Claude Vohl of Laval University, found evidence that the genes of children born after their mothers underwent procedures like gastric bypass behave differently than those of their siblings born before the surgery. Traditionally, scientists thought that overweight mothers passed on obesity to their children primarily through shared habits, like diet and exercise. However, the study reveals that there could be biological changes—specifically, how genes work—that influence a child’s chance of being overweight. Researchers analyzed blood samples from children born to 20 women, both before and after they had surgery to reduce their stomach size and reroute digestion. The mothers lost about 100 pounds on average after their operations. Among more than 5,600 genes, the team found variations in chemical tags that control how genes involved in blood sugar and heart health work. Children born after their mothers' surgery tended to have healthier weights and fewer risk factors for diabetes and heart disease than their older siblings. Dr. John Kral, a co-author from SUNY Downstate Medical Center, likened the womb to a marinade, saying that the conditions inside it change based on the mother's weight and health, affecting how babies' genes are 'switched on or off.' Obese women have higher sugar and fat levels in their blood, which can affect the developing fetus in ways scientists are still studying. Chemical changes, known as epigenetic tags, can adjust how genes function throughout a child’s life. While these results are promising, Dr. Susan Murphy of Duke University, who studies uterine effects (but did not work on the study), urges caution. She points out that positive changes in the family's habits after surgery may also help explain why younger siblings are healthier. This research highlights that a mother’s health before and during pregnancy can have long-term effects on her children. As Dr. Murphy notes, maternal obesity is not only a personal health issue but can also influence a child's future well-being. Gaining weight during pregnancy is normal. For example, much of the increase is due to the baby, placenta, and amniotic fluid (about 4.8kg). Other gains come from changes such as a larger uterus, extra blood and fluid, increased breast size, and stored fat for breastfeeding. By the end of pregnancy, women may gain about 12.5kg on average. UK guidelines do not set strict rules for pregnancy weight gain, but generally recommend women of normal weight gain between 11.3 and 15.8kg, and those who are obese to gain only 4.9 to 9.1kg.
