article_content: Li Weilei, a 26-year-old entrepreneur and model enthusiast from Shanghai, constructed a remarkable Batmobile replica for just £7,000. With assistance from four mechanics, Li spent two months assembling this full-size model from ten tons of scrap metal in a quiet workshop in Shanghai’s Minhang district. Although the replica closely mirrors the Batmobile from the Dark Knight trilogy, it lacks an engine. To maneuver it, the team used a scrapyard hoist. To minimize costs, they opted for hand-polished bodywork and budget-friendly materials, keeping expenses to 70,000 yuan (£7,000). Images of the car went viral online, attracting widespread interest. Li's group created multiple replicas, with two models on view in Shanghai and others displayed in various Chinese cities. Due to legal and copyright reasons, this vehicle isn’t officially named the Batmobile. Police officer Feng Dohan, who photographed the car, commended the craftsmanship but clarified that it isn’t roadworthy. In contrast to the movie Batmobile, which boasts a V8 engine, street-legal status, and a much higher cost, Li’s version is purely a display piece. The replica spans more than ten feet in width, with rear wheels nearly reaching the height of an adult—capturing the original’s essence, despite being non-functional.

The All India Organisation of Chemists and Druggists (AIOCD) has urged pharmaceutical companies to stop advertising their products on e-pharmacy platforms, which it alleges are operating illegally. In a letter dated November 23, the AIOCD stated its commitment to upholding the rules and regulations and expressed concern that several pharmaceutical companies continue to advertise on these platforms.

The organization claims that some e-pharmacy platforms violate the Drugs & Cosmetics Act, 1940, and the Drugs & Cosmetics Rules, 1945, by bypassing prescription and dispensation requirements. It also referred to an injunction order and contempt of court proceedings in the Delhi High Court against certain e-pharmacy operations. Furthermore, the AIOCD warned companies about the issuance of show-cause notices by the Drugs Controller General of India to some e-pharmacy operators.

According to the AIOCD, e-pharmacy platforms engage in predatory pricing practices that create monopolistic conditions and manipulate sales of competitor brands. The organization argued that such practices demotivate members who combat monopolistic activities and contradict the group's values.

The Delhi High Court is currently hearing petitions seeking a ban on the online sale of medicines. In a November 16 order, the court directed the government to draft a policy on the matter within eight weeks, listing the next hearing for March 4, 2024. The court stated that if the government failed to frame a policy within this period, the responsible joint secretary would have to appear in person at the next hearing.

article_content: Karnataka's Information Technology exports are approaching the $100 billion mark, up from $91 billion in the 2022 fiscal year—a significant achievement for the state's tech sector. Karnataka hosts over 5,500 IT and IT-enabled services (ITeS) companies, employing 1.8 million people directly and supporting an additional 5.5 million jobs indirectly. This momentum sets a positive backdrop for the Bengaluru Tech Summit 2023, a flagship event launching on November 29. Now in its 26th edition, the summit adopts the theme 'Breaking Boundaries', and will convene tech leaders, startups, investors, and research labs from 30 countries. The summit includes multi-track conferences on IT, electronics, deep tech, startups, and biotech, alongside an international exhibition, the Global Innovation Alliance, and the India-US Tech Conclave. Prominent speakers scheduled for the event include RA Mashelkar, former Director-General of the Council of Scientific and Industrial Research; Nobel laureate H Robert Horvitz; and Infosys founder NR Narayana Murthy, who will engage in a fireside chat with Nikhil Kamath, co-founder of Zerodha. This year, the Karnataka government is amplifying its 'Beyond Bengaluru' initiative, encouraging businesses to explore opportunities throughout the state. IT Minister Priyank Kharge states, 'The entire world is looking at India—and at Bengaluru in particular.' A major attraction this year is the Chandrayaan-3 ISRO industry pavilion. The summit will feature over 75 sessions, 400 speakers, 350 startups, 600 exhibitors, and over 20,000 expected business attendees. Bengaluru also leads India in women-led startups, ahead of Mumbai and Delhi. Karnataka’s grant-in-aid program, offering Rs 50 lakh to innovators, has led to 30% of grant recipients being women founders. According to Tracxn, notable women-led startups include Zomato, Byjus, Ofbusiness, Upstox, Lenskart, and the neobank Open, co-founded by Mabel Chacko and Deena Jacob. Other major unicorns with women founders are Nykaa, Mamaearth, Hasura, Pristyn Care, Mobikwik, The Good Glamm Group, and Livspace. On the international front, OpenAI has reinstated Sam Altman as CEO following an employee-led protest against his firing. The board of directors is being restructured to include Lawrence Summers, Bret Taylor, and Adam D'Angelo. Microsoft, OpenAI’s leading investor, is expected to have increased board participation, although Altman is not on the new board. OpenAI’s governance model will undergo review in the coming six months.

article_content: California Governor Gavin Newsom is set to name a successor for the late Senator Dianne Feinstein. The selected appointee will have the option to run in the 2024 Senate race, as confirmed by Newsom's spokesperson. This marks a change from Newsom's previous intention to appoint a temporary caretaker who would not participate in the upcoming election. Senate Democratic leadership expects the new senator to be sworn in by midweek, although an official announcement about the appointee's identity is still pending. Senator Feinstein died at 90 after a prolonged period of declining health. Progressive groups have been advocating for Newsom to pick Representative Barbara Lee. Newsom had earlier pledged to appoint a Black woman to the seat if a vacancy occurred and had mentioned Oprah Winfrey as a potential candidate earlier this year.

article_content: Ray Parlour, former Arsenal midfielder, believes Rudi Garcia could be the right choice to replace Arsene Wenger if the club pursues a managerial change. Parlour expressed his opinion in a Q&A on Sportlobster.com, referencing the growing uncertainty regarding Wenger’s tenure. He stated that it would be a significant decision for Arsenal and stressed the importance of having a suitable successor in line. Parlour noted Garcia’s success with Roma, leading the team to second place in Serie A and placing them firmly in contention for the title, just three points behind last season’s champions Juventus after their recent draw with AC Milan. Emirates Stadium supporters have become increasingly dissatisfied, having seen Arsenal win only two major trophies since 2005, and with just three victories in their last seven Premier League games. Parlour added that, despite his current tough season, a manager like Jurgen Klopp, known for his tactical flexibility and Champions League experience, could also be a strong candidate. While Garcia remains a viable option, Parlour highlighted that Wenger’s voice would likely be influential during any managerial transition, considering his longstanding contributions in shaping the club’s success and overseeing the move to Emirates Stadium. Arsenal is presently sixth in the Premier League standings, trailing behind Chelsea by 12 points and sitting four points away from a Champions League qualification berth. Squad depth remains an issue, especially at defensive midfield, where only Mathieu Flamini is available—and he often faces disciplinary challenges. With the January transfer window approaching, Parlour recommended Arsenal recruit Morgan Schneiderlin because of his age and potential, also mentioning Winston Reid and Sami Khedira as notable options. He argued that acquiring players familiar with high-stakes matches could enhance Arsenal’s prospects for securing a Champions League spot.

article_content: England's hopes for World Cup success heavily rely on the fitness and form of James Anderson, especially after his outstanding performance against India. While Steven Finn received much of the praise for his five-wicket haul in the team's nine-wicket victory at the Gabba, it was Anderson's four wickets for just 18 runs that set the tone for a near-flawless bowling display, bowling India out for 153. Anderson, who had previously missed the one-day tour of Sri Lanka and was not fit enough to play Australia in Sydney due to a knee injury, looked back to his best in Brisbane. 'I felt good and the wickets were a bonus,' Anderson said after the match. He has been working on his fitness since returning from South Africa before Christmas, aiming for peak form. Finn also impressed, claiming five wickets a year after being sent home from Australia, and Anderson empathizes with Finn's journey. 'I’ve been talking to him here and was texting him during his time in Sri Lanka,' Anderson shared, noting the similarities between their experiences. 'He deserved his performance after all his hard work, and his return boosts our attack because he delivers wicket-taking balls.' Next, England travel south to Tasmania to face Australia at the Bellerive Oval on Thursday. Australia will be playing without several stars—Mitchell Johnson, David Warner, George Bailey, and Michael Clarke—while England know a win will secure them a spot in the tri-series final. Despite Finn's standout performance, questions remain about the variety in England's bowling attack. Anderson, however, disagrees, stating, 'We’re all very different bowlers. We may not have a left-armer, but our attack is strong enough to bowl teams out.' Australia has insisted that Warner's absence is due to a sore hamstring, not disciplinary reasons, despite recent player behavior coming under the spotlight following his altercation with India’s Rohit Sharma. Anderson argues there is no new problem with attitudes in cricket: 'I don’t think there are more verbals than before. There’s just more focus with stump mics and cameras. It’s been happening for over a hundred years, and it isn’t going to disappear.'

article_content: Sony Corp. reported a record loss of $5.7 billion for the fiscal year ending in March, the company announced today. This figure is lower than the electronics giant's earlier estimate of a $6.4 billion loss. However, it marks the fourth consecutive year Sony has finished with losses. Sony is not alone among Japanese electronics makers facing challenges. Panasonic Corp. is expected to announce nearly $10 billion in annual losses on Friday, according to previous company estimates. Both Sony and Panasonic have struggled with unprofitable television manufacturing divisions, losing market share to lower-cost competitors such as Samsung and LG. Additionally, a stronger yen has reduced profit from overseas sales. Sony's television division has operated at a loss for the past eight years. Earlier this week, Sony's stock fell to its lowest point in 25 years. Both Sony and Panasonic have announced restructuring plans, and each has appointed new leadership. Sony's new CEO, Kazuo Hirai, took over on April 1 and last month promised to cut 10,000 jobs—about 6% of the workforce—within the next year. The company forecasts a net profit of 30 billion yen ($376.5 million) in the current fiscal year. Panasonic's new CEO, Kazuhiro Tsuga, was appointed earlier this year. Both Tsuga and Hirai plan to reduce the volume of televisions produced. According to a report on Wednesday by the Japanese economic newspaper Nikkei, Panasonic may post a $626 million profit this fiscal year, which resulted in a nearly 5% rise in its share price. Panasonic declined to comment on the report, stating it would release official figures Friday.

article_content: Loic Remy trained at Chelsea’s Cobham training ground on Tuesday morning as he recovered from his recent international duty with France. The former Queens Park Rangers forward hopes to be in contention for a place in Jose Mourinho’s squad on Saturday, when the Blues face Swansea at Stamford Bridge. Remy may even make his home debut if Mourinho decides to start him, as there are fitness concerns about star striker Diego Costa. Costa, who has already scored four goals for Chelsea this season, left Spain’s international camp last week due to a hamstring worry. This same injury nearly kept him out of Chelsea’s match against Everton last weekend, but the 25-year-old proved his fitness by scoring twice in Chelsea’s impressive 6–3 win. Speaking about the competition at Chelsea, Remy told the club’s official website: 'We have two great strikers already and if I want to be in the team, I have to play at a very high level.'

article_content: A United Airlines flight traveling from Los Angeles to Vancouver was forced to make an emergency landing in San Francisco after a bomb threat was reportedly sent by a passenger. Flight UA1909, carrying 148 passengers, took off from LAX at 7:13 p.m. on Monday but changed course about an hour into its journey to land in San Francisco, according to flight tracking data. Airport officials reported that the incident began when a bomb threat was delivered to passengers via AirDrop, a wireless file-sharing service. It was not immediately clear who sent the message. Once the flight landed safely, FBI agents boarded the plane to investigate, interviewing several passengers—including those who received the AirDrop message. Authorities later determined the threat was not credible. Due to the disruption, passengers had to stay overnight at San Francisco International Airport. United Airlines arranged for them to continue to Vancouver the following morning, with the replacement flight scheduled to arrive at 9 a.m. Pacific Time—eleven hours behind the original arrival time. United Airlines confirmed in a statement that the flight was diverted due to a potential security issue and that law enforcement met the plane upon landing. Incidents involving bomb threats and unruly behavior aboard U.S. flights have increased, with the FAA receiving 1,780 such reports by November this year. A comparable incident occurred in March, when another United flight made an emergency landing in Vermont after a bomb threat note was found onboard—no hazardous items were discovered in that case.

article_content: A study published on November 7 in Nature Communications reveals that the largest floating ice shelves in the polar ice sheet have lost more than a third of their volume since 1978. Led by scientists from CNRS and partners in Denmark and the United States, the research attributes most of this thinning to rising ocean temperatures, which are melting the floating extensions of glaciers. Previously, these ice shelves in North Greenland were thought to be stable, unlike other more vulnerable parts of the polar ice cap that started weakening in the mid-1980s. Acting as massive frozen dams, the North Greenland shelves play a crucial role in regulating the flow of ice into the ocean. Since Greenland already accounts for 17% of current sea level rise, any further weakening of these ice barriers could speed up ice loss into the ocean, further raising sea levels. The study's conclusions are based on fieldwork, aerial photography, satellite data, and regional climate models.

article_content: Arsene Wenger, the long-serving Arsenal manager, will no longer serve as a commentator for TF1, France’s leading television network. This change comes after his contract with TF1 ended, closing a chapter of over ten years providing analysis mostly for the French national team’s matches. While initial reports noted that Wenger was surprised by the development, later statements described the decision as mutually agreed upon by both Wenger and the channel. Wenger did not participate in coverage of France’s recent 1-0 win over Spain at the Stade de France, where Chelsea’s new signing Loic Remy scored the decisive goal. During his years with TF1, Wenger offered commentary on major tournaments, including the World Cup in Brazil, as well as Champions League games. Now stepping back from his media commitments, Wenger is set to devote additional time to managing Arsenal. His focus will be on leading the team in the Premier League following their FA Cup win last season, as they seek to add more silverware after a start of one win and two draws.

article_content: New Zealand has asked the global governing body, World Rugby, to clarify some of the refereeing decisions made during their Rugby World Cup final defeat to South Africa, outgoing coach Ian Foster said. The Springboks won 12-11 in a dramatic match that saw four yellow cards issued, including one upgraded to a red for All Blacks captain Sam Cane after a high tackle, forcing New Zealand to play with 14 men for more than half the game. South Africa’s captain Siya Kolisi also received a yellow card early in the second half for what appeared to be a similar shoulder-to-head incident involving Ardie Savea. New Zealand was left puzzled when a try by Aaron Smith was overturned by the Television Match Official due to a knock-on elsewhere on the field. "We've already sent a file to World Rugby and asked them for feedback," Foster told New Zealand media with a smile. "Hopefully they respond." Foster declined to specify which incidents the team was most interested in reviewing. "I think you can guess," he said. The final marked Foster’s last match as head coach, with Scott Robertson set to take over. Now back in New Zealand, Foster said his final responsibilities would include a review of the team's performance with his coaching staff, a process likely to exclude the players. "It probably won't officially involve the players. But it certainly will be done by me and my coaching group," he said.

article_content: Thug and Nicky, two endangered pygmy hippos, are now the newest residents at ZSL London Zoo's 'Into Africa' enclosure. The pair, aged 17 and 19, explored their custom-built home on Thursday morning. Their spacious enclosure features heated pools, specially designed gardens, and a dedicated team providing their favorite snack—freshly sliced watermelon. Pygmy hippos originate from West Africa and are classified as endangered, with fewer than 3,000 left in the wild due to threats like poaching, habitat loss, and logging. The 'Into Africa' exhibit also features giraffes, zebras, and African hunting dogs, offering visitors a look at a variety of African wildlife. Pygmy hippos are known for being solitary and primarily active at night. The zoo is committed to the conservation of this species and hopes these new residents will inspire visitors to support wildlife protection. Thug and Nicky will be viewable by the public starting Saturday.

article_content: President Barack Obama announced a new set of sanctions against Russia on Tuesday, responding to President Vladimir Putin's refusal to withdraw Russian support from military activities in eastern Ukraine. Speaking at the White House, Obama stated that Russia is isolating itself from the international community, undermining decades of progress. He emphasized that this isolation is a choice made by Russia and President Putin. Obama stressed that the U.S. administration does not see the sanctions as a return to a Cold War-style conflict. 'No, it's not a new Cold War,' he said, responding to a question from CBS News. Obama announced the new economic measures from the White House's South Lawn, targeting key sectors of the Russian economy in an attempt to pressure President Putin to end his support for Ukrainian separatists. According to Obama, Russia continues to support, train, and arm separatists, and American satellite surveillance has shown Russian forces firing artillery into Ukraine. He stated, 'Today is a reminder that the United States means what it says.' The sanctions include targeted actions against banks, defense contractors, and individuals closely linked to Putin, according to senior administration officials. The list of sanctioned financial institutions was expanded to include three more major Russian state-owned banks. These moves are in response to the significant flow of heavy weaponry and ongoing support from Russia to Ukrainian separatists. Russia is supporting the separatist movement accused of shooting down a Malaysian Airlines passenger plane the previous week. Obama criticized the Russian government's efforts to prevent international inspectors from accessing the entire crash site. Most of Obama's remarks focused on his administration's belief that economic sanctions can influence Russian policy and persuade Putin to withdraw support from Ukraine. He pointed out that hurting the Russian economy is the main tool available. Obama declined to answer directly when asked if the U.S. would provide lethal aid to Ukraine, stating that 'the issue is not the ability of the Ukrainian military to outfight the separatists,' and mentioned a new round of European Union sanctions signaling Europe's support for Ukraine. A senior Obama official said Russia is now more isolated than at any time since the end of the Cold War. The new EU sanctions, announced before Obama's remarks, impose restrictions on Russian state banks, ban arms trading, and limit the export of sensitive technologies to Russia's oil sector. Obama's announcement coincided with these EU sanctions, which also target the Russian banking, defense, and oil industries. A European Council statement said, 'Illegal annexation of territory and deliberate destabilization of a neighboring sovereign country cannot be accepted in 21st century Europe.' Obama noted that Russia's annexation of Crimea and continued support for rebels has brought widespread consequences across Europe. Another senior administration official commented that the EU's measures are significant and mark a new step for Europe, taken in coordination with the United States. A third official highlighted that Russia is currently not an attractive option for international investors. When asked about U.S. expectations for Putin, an official said Russia still has an opportunity to reduce tensions if it recognizes the legitimacy of Ukraine's government, stops the flow of arms across the border, withdraws its troops, and encourages a diplomatic dialogue. 'We will continue to hold that door open,' the official said.

گفتگو کرتے ہوئے اوباما نے کہا کہ روس خود کو بین الاقوامی برادری سے الگ کر رہا ہے اور دہائیوں پر محیط پیش رفت کو نقصان پہنچا رہا ہے۔ انہوں نے اس بات پر زور دیا کہ یہ تنہائی روس اور صدر پوتن کی اپنی پسند ہے۔ اوباما نے اس بات پر زور دیا کہ امریکی انتظامیہ ان پابندیوں کو سرد جنگ کے انداز کے تنازعے کی واپسی نہیں سمجھتی۔ انہوں نے سی بی ایس نیوز کے سوال کے جواب میں کہا، 'نہیں، یہ نئی سرد جنگ نہیں ہے۔' اوباما نے وائٹ ہاؤس کے ساؤتھ لان سے روسی معیشت کے اہم شعبوں کو ہدف بنانے والی نئی معاشی پابندیوں کا اعلان کیا، جس کا مقصد صدر پوتن پر دباؤ ڈالنا ہے کہ وہ یوکرینی علیحدگی پسندوں کی حمایت ختم کریں۔ اوباما کے مطابق، روس علیحدگی پسندوں کی تربیت، مسلح کرنے اور حمایت جاری رکھے ہوئے ہے، اور امریکی سیٹلائٹ نگرانی نے روسی افواج کو یوکرین میں توپ خانے سے حملے کرتے دیکھا ہے۔ انہوں نے کہا، 'آج یہ یاد دہانی ہے کہ ریاست ہائے متحدہ اپنے الفاظ پر قائم ہے۔' سینئر حکومتی عہدیداروں کے مطابق، پابندیوں میں ان اداروں، دفاعی کنٹریکٹرز اور پوتن کے قریبی افراد کے خلاف اقدامات شامل ہیں۔ ان پابندیوں کے تحت تین مزید بڑی روسی ریاستی بینکوں کو بھی شامل کیا گیا ہے۔ یہ اقدامات روس کی طرف سے یوکرینی علیحدگی پسندوں کے لیے بھاری ہتھیاروں اور مسلسل حمایت کے ردعمل میں کیے گئے ہیں۔ روس اس علیحدگی پسند تحریک کی حمایت کر رہا ہے جس پر گزشتہ ہفتے ملائیشین ایئر لائن کے مسافر طیارے کو گرانے کا الزام ہے۔ اوباما نے روسی حکومت پر تنقید کی کہ اس نے بین الاقوامی معائنہ کاروں کو پورے حادثے کی جگہ تک رسائی سے روکا۔ اوباما کی زیادہ تر گفتگو اس بات پر مرکوز رہی کہ ان کی انتظامیہ سمجھتی ہے کہ معاشی پابندیاں روسی پالیسی کو متاثر کر سکتی ہیں اور پوتن کو یوکرین سے حمایت واپس لینے پر مجبور کر سکتی ہیں۔ انہوں نے کہا کہ روسی معیشت پسندوں سے بہتر لڑنے کی صلاحیت نہیں ہے'۔ اس کے ساتھ ساتھ انہوں نے یورپی یونین کی نئی پابندیوں کا بھی ذکر کیا جو یوکرین کی حمایت کی نشاندہی کرتی ہیں۔ ایک سینئر امریکی عہدیدار نے کہا کہ روس اب سرد جنگ کے اختتام کے بعد سے پہلے سے کہیں زیادہ تنہائی کا شکار ہے۔ نئی یورپی یونین کی پابندیاں، جو اوباما کے اعلان سے قبل جاری کی گئیں، روسی بینکوں پر پابندیاں، اسلحہ کی تجارت پر پابندی اور روس کے تیل کے شعبے کے لیے حساس ٹیکنالوجیز کی برآمد پر پابندیاں عائد کرتی ہیں۔ اوباما کا اعلامیہ ان ہی یورپی پابندیوں کے ساتھ آیا ہے، جو کہ روسی بینکاری، دفاع اور تیل کی صنعتوں کو بھی نشانہ بناتی ہیں۔ یورپی کونسل کے ایک بیان میں کہا گیا ہے، 'کسی علاقے کا غیر قانونی الحاق اور ہمسایہ خود مختار ملک میں دانستہ عدم استحکام 21ویں صدی کے یورپ میں قبول نہیں کیا جا سکتا۔' اوباما نے کہا کہ روس کے کریمیا کے الحاق اور باغیوں کی جاری حمایت سے پورے یورپ پر اثرات مرتب ہو رہے ہیں۔ ایک اور سینئر امریکی عہدیدار نے کہا کہ یورپی یونین کے یہ اقدامات اہم ہیں اور یہ امریکا کے ساتھ مل کر یورپ کے نئے قدم کی نمائندگی کرتے ہیں۔ ایک تیسرے article_content: The Alfred Dunhill Links Championship is a singular event on the European Tour, uniting leading golfers, sports icons, and Hollywood celebrities. The tournament is played over Scotland's famed St Andrews, Carnoustie, and Kingsbarns courses and features both professional competition and a star-studded amateur lineup. Among the field are defending champion Martin Kaymer, as well as top-ranked players Luke Donald, Lee Westwood, Rory McIlroy, and Dustin Johnson. They are competing for a share of a $5 million prize purse. High-profile amateurs this year include Johan Cruyff, former Dutch football star; Australian cricketer Shane Warne; and actors Andy Garcia and Michael Douglas. Hugh Grant described competing as ‘going to golfing heaven,’ and Kaymer referred to St Andrews as ‘paradise’. Douglas, who is making his return following cancer treatment, called it ‘a magical place’ and said the current weather makes it even better. The event has a dual format: professionals compete in a 72-hole strokeplay tournament and also team up with amateurs for a team event. Michael Douglas partners again with Colin Montgomerie—his teammate from Montgomerie’s 2005 victory. Douglas shared that the championship motivated him during his recovery. Among the notable pairings, Simon Dyson—former winner and Dutch Open champion—teamed up with musician Huey Lewis, who praised the course's unique landscape. Some pros, including Kaymer, Ernie Els, and Rory McIlroy, have chosen to partner with their fathers rather than celebrities in the team event. This year, participants and fans are enjoying exceptionally warm and sunny weather, a departure from the usual cold and rainy conditions expected at the championship.

article_content: A series of printed roadside banners has been displayed in Sinaloa, Mexico, declaring a prohibition on the production and sale of fentanyl. The messages allegedly come from 'Los Chapitos,' the sons of renowned drug lord Joaquin 'El Chapo' Guzman, who have led the Sinaloa cartel since his extradition and subsequent life sentence in the United States in 2017. The banners warn: 'In Sinaloa, the sale, manufacture, transport, or involvement in any fentanyl business, including related chemicals, is strictly prohibited. You have been warned. Respectfully, Los Chapitos.' Mexican authorities have not officially determined whether these messages originate from Los Chapitos, although local sources claim they are authentic. News agencies, such as ABC News, have also been unable to independently substantiate the claim. Even if these banners are legitimate, experts note that it is unlikely the Sinaloa cartel will abruptly terminate its fentanyl operations, given the vast scale of the trade, its global involvement, and substantial profits. There is also the likelihood that, if halted in Sinaloa, production and trafficking could continue in other Mexican regions under cartel control. Fentanyl's deadly effect in the United States has intensified focus on the issue. The synthetic opioid is responsible for tens of thousands of overdose deaths among Americans in the past year, and combating its spread is a major subject in US-Mexico relations. The US Drug Enforcement Administration has increased rewards—up to $10 million each—for information that could lead to apprehending two of El Chapo’s sons, who are currently among the agency’s most-wanted fugitives. Insiders familiar with the Sinaloa cartel suggest that the leadership, particularly El Chapo’s sons, are aware of the political and law enforcement scrutiny surrounding fentanyl. Heightened pressure from the US results in more police raids and arrests, which threaten cartel operations, possibly prompting the banners as a strategic move. Although fentanyl is officially approved for treating severe pain, its illegal versions are a leading cause of US overdose deaths. The CDC reports that out of around 109,680 overdose deaths nationwide last year, roughly 75,000 were related to fentanyl and other synthetic opioids. It remains uncertain whether these new bans will truly affect fentanyl trafficking between Mexico and the US.

article_content: The first decade of the 21st century in the United States was defined by terrorism, crises, and uncertainty. The optimism and economic growth of the 1990s ended, and many Americans were left unsettled by nine challenging years, even as the decade closed with a presidential election that offered hope for the future. Any list identifying the 'most important' events is the beginning of a conversation, not a final judgment. Historians know it is difficult to predict which events will have lasting impact. Some events initially seen as significant, such as Operation Desert Storm (1990-1991), may fade in perceived importance over time. Others, like the first World Trade Center bombing in 1993, can appear more consequential as years pass. September 11, 2001 was a defining moment, with devastating terrorist attacks in New York and at the Pentagon. 9/11 represents a central national security challenge: stateless terrorism. While the U.S. had experienced terrorism before (e.g., the 1993 World Trade Center bombing, the 1995 Oklahoma City bombing), the scale of 9/11 was unprecedented. The attack shattered Americans' sense of safety and reshaped national security policy. The government expanded and reorganized homeland defense, increased surveillance and interrogation efforts, and refocused foreign policy on combating terror networks and their supporters, including invading Afghanistan to remove the Taliban. Years later, these struggles continue. The Iraq War quickly became one of the most controversial aspects of the war on terrorism. Challenges in post-war reconstruction and false claims about weapons of mass destruction led to strong criticism of President Bush’s administration. The war eroded Bush’s political capital, affecting his ability to pursue other goals, such as Social Security reform. Ongoing difficulties in creating a stable democracy and fighting insurgents in Iraq, as well as Afghanistan, raised doubts about the effectiveness of American military power. Hurricane Katrina devastated New Orleans in 2005, exposing poor living conditions for many inner-city Americans after years of neglect. Inadequate response from multiple levels of government highlighted limited attention to protecting African-American communities, even after such a severe disaster. The lack of substantial federal aid for reconstruction suggested urban America was not a government priority. The 2008 financial crisis dealt a severe blow to the U.S. economy. Just as 9/11 ended a sense of physical security, the financial crisis shattered economic confidence built in the 1990s and set the agenda for President Obama’s administration. The crisis challenged long-held beliefs in deregulation and market solutions. The Bush administration's expansive bailout package showed both the public's expectation of federal intervention and the limits of previous economic policies. The 2008 election was a defining moment for the country’s potential. Though the United States had not become a post-racial society, as underscored by the response to Katrina, electing an African-American president was historic in a nation once reliant on slavery. Combined with growing acceptance of gay rights, the election signaled progress away from deeply rooted discriminatory attitudes. Any list of major events is necessarily incomplete and only captures a fraction of national experience. Passage of health care reform, if achieved, may be another turning point. These five events—the September 11 attacks, the Iraq War, Hurricane Katrina, the 2008 financial crisis, and the election of Barack Obama—are likely to remain key points for historians studying this era. The views expressed in this commentary are solely those of Julian Zelizer.

سالوں کے بعد پریشان رہے، حالانکہ اس دہائی کا اختتام ایک صدارتی انتخاب کے ساتھ ہوا جس نے مستقبل کے لیے امید پیدا کی۔ 'سب سے اہم' واقعات کی کوئی بھی فہرست گفتگو کی ابتدا ہے، حتمی فیصلہ نہیں۔ مورخ جانتے ہیں کہ پیش گوئی کرنا مشکل ہوتا ہے کہ کون سے واقعات دیرپا اثرات چھوڑیں گے۔ کچھ واقعات جنہیں ابتدا میں نمایاں سمجھا گیا، جیسے آپریشن ڈیزرٹ اسٹورم (1990-1991)، وقت کے ساتھ کم اہم لگنے لگتے ہیں۔ کچھ دوسرے، مثلاً 1993 میں ورلڈ ٹریڈ سینٹر بم دھماکہ، برسوں بعد زیادہ سنگین نظر آ سکتے ہیں۔ 11 ستمبر 2001 ایک فیصلہ کن لمحہ تھا، جب نیویارک اور پینٹاگون میں دہشت گرد حملے ہوئے۔ 9/11 مرکزی قومی سلامتی کا چیلنج بن گیا: بغیر ریاست کے دہشت گردی۔ اگرچہ امریکہ پہلے بھی دہشت گردی کا سامنا کر چکا تھا (جیسے 1993 میں ورلڈ ٹریڈ سینٹر بم دھماکہ، 1995 میں اوکلاہوما سٹی بم دھماکہ)، لیکن 9/11 کا پیمانہ بے مثال تھا۔ اس حملے نے امریکیوں کے تحفظ کے احساس کو جھٹکا دیا اور قومی سلامتی کی پالیسی کو بدل دیا۔ حکومت نے ہوم لینڈ ڈیفنس کو وسعت دی، نگرانی اور تفتیش میں اضافہ کیا، اور خارجہ پالیسی کو دہشت گرد نیٹ ورکس اور ان کے حمایتی ممالک کے خلاف مرکوز کیا، جس میں طالبان کو ہٹانے کے لیے افغانستان پر حملہ بھی شامل تھا۔ کئی سال بعد بھی یہ جدوجہد جاری ہے۔ عراق جنگ انسداد دہشت گردی جنگ کا سب سے متنازعہ پہلو بن گئی۔ جنگ کے بعد تعمیر نو میں مشکلات اور وسیع پیمانے پر تباہی کے ہتھیاروں سے متعلق جھوٹے دعوؤں کی وجہ سے صدر بش کی انتظامیہ کو سخت تنقید کا سامنا کرنا پڑا۔ جنگ نے بش کی سیاسی پوزیشن کو کمزور کیا، جس سے وہ دیگر مقاصد، جیسے سوشل سیکیورٹی اصلاحات، حاصل کرنے سے قاصر رہے۔ عراق اور افغانستان میں جمہوریت کے قیام اور شورش کے خاتمے میں مسلسل مشکلات نے امریکی عسکری طاقت کی مؤثریت پر شکوک پیدا کیے۔ ہریکین کترینا نے 2005 میں نیو اورلینز کو تباہ کر دیا، جس سے کئی سالوں کی نظراندازی کے بعد شہر میں بسنے والے کم آمدنی والے امریکیوں کی خراب حالت سامنے آئی۔ حکومت کی کئی سطحوں پر ناکافی ردعمل نے ثابت کیا کہ افریقی نژاد امریکی برادریوں کی حفاظت پر توجہ نہ ہونے کے برابر رہی، چاہے اتنی بڑی آفت ہی کیوں نہ ہو۔ بحالی کے لیے وفاقی مدد کی کمی نے ظاہر کیا کہ شہری امریکہ حکومت کی ترجیح نہیں رہا۔ 2008 کے مالیاتی بحران نے امریکی معیشت کو شدید نقصان پہنچایا۔ جس طرح 9/11 نے جسمانی تحفظ کے احساس کو ختم کیا، اسی طرح مالی بحران نے 1990 کے عشرے میں قائم شدہ معاشی اعتماد کو توڑ دیا اور صدر اوباما کی انتظامیہ کے لیے ایجنڈا متعین کیا۔ بحران نے طویل عرصے سے رائج ڈی ریگولیشن اور منڈی پر مبنی پالیسیوں کو چیلنج کیا۔ صدر بش کی بڑی مالیاتی امدادی پیکیج سے ظاہر ہوا کہ عوام معاشی بحران میں وفاقی مداخلت کی توقع رکھتے ہیں، اور پچھلی پالیسیوں کی حدود نمایاں ہوئیں۔ 2008 کا انتخاب ملک کی صلاحیت کے لیے ایک اہم لمحہ تھا۔ اگرچہ امریکہ اب بھی مکمل غیر نسلی معاشرہ نہیں بنا، جیسا کہ کترینا کے ردعمل سے ظاہر ہوتا ہے، لیکن ایک افریقی نژاد امریکی کا صدر منتخب ہونا ایک ایسی قوم کے لیے تاریخی تھا جو کبھی غلامی پر معاشی طور پر انحصار کرتی تھی۔ ہم جنس پرستوں کے حقوق کی بڑھتی ہوئی قبولیت کے ساتھ، یہ انتخاب روایتی امتیازی رویوں سے پیشرفت کی علامت بن گیا۔ اہم واقعات کی کوئی بھی فہرست مکمل نہیں ہوتی اور یہ قومی تجربے کا صرف ایک حصہ ظاہر کرتی ہے۔ اگر ہیلتھ کیئر اصلاحات منظور ہوئیں تو وہ بھی ایک اور اہم موڑ ہو سکتا ہے۔ ان پانچ واقعات — گیارہ ستمبر کے حملے، عراق جنگ، ہریکین کترینا، 2008 کا مالیاتی بحران، اور باراک اوباما کا انتخاب — ممکنہ طور پر اس دور کا مطالعہ کرنے والے مورخین کے لیے کلیدی نقاط رہیں گے۔ اس تبصرے میں ظاہر کی گئی آراء صرف جولین زیلائزر کی ہیں۔

article_content: New York City officials were scrutinized on Monday as they addressed the city’s delayed reaction to last month’s major blizzard. They conceded that declaring a snow emergency could have reduced the chaos. With forecasts warning of another snowstorm potentially depositing up to a foot of snow, City Council Speaker Christine C. Quinn said the last storm’s impact was unmatched and questioned why no emergency was declared. Deputy Mayor Stephen Goldsmith explained that the city refrained from declaring an emergency to avoid forcing thousands of drivers to relocate their cars, though he admitted this decision was a mistake. Goldsmith highlighted that shortcomings included not having sufficient real-time data on street conditions, slow deployment of snow-clearing equipment, delayed use of private contractors, and weak communication with the public. Additionally, only half the sanitation trucks were equipped with radios, hampering coordination as snowfall sped up. Sanitation Commissioner John Doherty described the blizzard as the hardest he’d ever faced, with the holiday season bringing increased traffic into the city. Councilman Peter Vallone criticized the city’s lack of preparation, particularly inadequate salting of roads and the failure to alert the public to the storm’s seriousness. Mayor Bloomberg faced backlash for encouraging New Yorkers to attend Broadway shows during the crisis. In response to criticism, he restructured the Sanitation Department and introduced plans to equip all sanitation trucks with GPS and launch teams to relay real-time updates. Nonetheless, some outer borough neighborhoods remained snowbound for days. Many vehicles and ambulances were immobilized, 911 calls piled up, and officials asked for out-of-state ambulances to support overwhelmed emergency crews. Tragically, a newborn in Brooklyn died after emergency responders took nine hours to arrive. During the hearing, officials were pressed on why more caution was not exercised. Goldsmith proposed that future emergency declarations need more flexible options. Sanitation union leaders, under scrutiny due to rumors of an intentional slowdown related to budget issues, did not comment. The Department of Investigations is conducting an independent probe into these allegations, which relate to worker conditions and funding cuts. To manage the snow, the city combined public sector efforts with those of more than 80 private contractors; however, total costs are still unclear. Budget limitations continue to strain resources, as state deficits threaten the ability to deal with ongoing severe weather. Mayor Bloomberg stressed that the multibillion-dollar state deficit could hinder emergency efforts. New York is facing potential budget shortfalls of up to $14 billion in the next fiscal year, while New Jersey may be looking at a $10 billion deficit. Governors Cuomo of New York and Christie of New Jersey are preparing new state budgets as another significant snowstorm approaches—meaning the region must prepare for continued financial and logistical difficulties.

article_content: At the Manus Island Regional Processing Centre in Papua New Guinea, groups of asylum seekers have blocked the Delta and Oscar compounds, preventing staff and officials from entering by stacking boxes at the gates. Protesters say their actions are motivated by fear and distrust of the guards. The situation has intensified, with some detainees commencing a hunger strike and about 30 reportedly sewing their lips together in protest. In response, security teams have detained protest leaders, placing them in high-security isolation. Refugee advocacy groups state that riot officers raided the compound early Sunday to target protest organizers. Advocates further allege that security personnel tried to force water into unconscious hunger strikers and warned that a special force from Port Moresby would intervene if the protest persisted. These details come from Refugee Action Coalition spokesperson Ian Rintoul. Government officials have been cautious in their commentary. Deputy Premier Warren Truss said some reports are unconfirmed, while Immigration Minister Peter Dutton is currently investigating. The government has received updates indicating that food and water remain available, but acknowledges that protests have disrupted normal services in parts of the centre. In contrast, refugees claim they are being refused essential supplies, sharing images of men tunneling beneath fences to access bottled water placed outside. Separately, a letter supposedly signed by 80 people in another compound urgently calls for intervention, warning that forced resettlement in Papua New Guinea could lead to disaster. The protest began after plans emerged to move some recognized refugees to a transit facility on Manus Island. The Australian government insists that asylum seekers arriving by boat will not be settled in Australia regardless of protests or claims of mistreatment. Despite the crackdown, refugee advocates believe these government actions will not put an end to the hunger strike or the broader protest movement.

article_content: Alexandra O'Shea, a 20-year-old from Bedminster Down in Bristol, now has to pay over £1,000 after she threw a cigarette butt out of her car and refused to pay the original £75 littering fine. This happened in Hartcliffe, where two Police Community Support Officers noticed her tossing the cigarette while driving. O'Shea didn't respond to reminders and failed to appear in court when the Bristol City Council took action. Because of her non-compliance, magistrates increased the penalty: she now owes a £600 fine, £361.08 in court costs, and a £60 victim surcharge. Carol Donovan from Bristol City Council said they tried to contact her several times before going to court. Jonquil Maudlin, the council’s neighbourhood enforcement manager, pointed out that cigarette butts, which contain plastic and toxins, pose a major problem for the environment and wildlife. Andy Walker from the Keep Britain Tidy Campaign stressed that littering is a costly issue, causing about £1 billion in expenses across the UK each year. He added that the situation could have been easily resolved if O'Shea had paid the initial fine and replied to council notices.

article_content: The Biden administration has rolled out revised regulations for the Public Service Loan Forgiveness (PSLF) program, which helps forgive federal student loan debt for people working in nonprofit or government jobs. These changes refine and broaden the definition of full-time work, making it easier for borrowers to qualify. Importantly, more job categories—including certain religious roles—now count toward forgiveness. Previously, PSLF criteria were much stricter, requiring 120 on-time monthly payments under limited repayment plans, and only counting full-time employees at eligible government or nonprofit entities. Recent efforts, including the Limited PSLF Waiver and the ongoing Income-Driven Repayment (IDR) Account Adjustment, have allowed borrowers to count additional types of repayment and deferment periods toward forgiveness. Over 700,000 borrowers have benefited from these changes so far. With new regulations effective July 1, qualifying employment definitions and eligible payment histories are expanded further. The Department of Education’s new 'safe harbor' policy lets borrowers buy back previously ineligible loan periods, helping them get closer to loan forgiveness.

article_content: Later this year, twin brothers John and Rob Snaza will make history by both serving as sheriffs in neighboring counties in western Washington. John Snaza, who has been the Thurston County Sheriff since 2010, recently maintained his position following the latest election. Meanwhile, Rob Snaza has been elected Lewis County Sheriff for the first time and will formally start his role in December, Q13Fox reported. In a joint interview, Rob described the achievement as 'pretty awesome' and both brothers expressed how humbling the experience feels. Their connection to the area is strong; they grew up in Thurston County, and their parents are from Lewis County. John shared that he entered law enforcement after going on a ridealong with Rob, describing it as a transformative moment. The brothers also talked about the unique situations they encounter as identical twins serving as sheriffs in neighboring counties. John humorously noted that responding together to DUI calls sometimes puzzled people who saw two identical sheriffs. Both emphasized how meaningful it is to serve the communities connected to their family history, and how being able to share ideas and stories with each other enriches their work.
translated_content: اس سال کے آخر میں، جڑواں بھائی جان اور راب سنازا تاریخ رقم کریں گے کیونکہ وہ مغربی واشنگٹن کی ہمسایہ کاؤنٹیز میں شیرف بنیں گے۔ جان سنازا، جو 2010 سے تھرسٹن کاؤنٹی کے شیرف ہیں، نے حالیہ انتخابات میں اپنی پوزیشن برقرار رکھی ہے۔ ادھر، راب سنازا کو پہلی بار لیوس کاؤنٹی کا شیرف منتخب کیا گیا ہے اور وہ دسمبر میں اپنی ذمہ داریاں سنبھالیں گے، جیسا کہ Q13Fox نے رپورٹ کیا۔ ایک مشترکہ انٹرویو میں راب نے اس کامیابی کو 'کافی لاجواب' قرار دیا اور دونوں بھائیوں نے کہا کہ یہ ان کے لئے بہت عاجزانہ تجربہ ہے۔ دونوں بھائی تھرسٹن کاؤنٹی میں پلے بڑھے ہیں جبکہ ان کے والدین کا تعلق لیوس کاؤنٹی سے ہے۔ جان نے بتایا کہ انہں اپنے بھائی راب کے ساتھ رائیڈ الونگ میں جاکر قانون نافذ کرنے والے ادارے میں شامل ہونے کا شوق ہوا، اور اسے اپنی زندگی بدلنے کا لمحہ کہا۔ دونوں نے بطور جڑواں شیرف ہمسایہ کاؤنٹیز میں کام کرنے کی منفرد صورتحال کا ذکر کیا۔ جان نے ہنستے ہوئے کہا کہ جب وہ ایک ساتھ ڈی یو آئی کالز میں جاتے تھے تو لوگ ان جیسے دکھنے والے دو شیرف کو دیکھ کر حیران رہ جاتے تھے۔ دونوں بھائیوں نے اس بات پر زور دیا کہ اپنے خاندانی علاقوں میں خدمت کرنا ان کے لیے کتنا اہم ہے، اور ایک دوسرے کے ساتھ خیالات اور کہانیاں بانٹنا ان کے لئے اسے خاص بنا دیتا ہے۔

article_content: Glen Campbell, a legendary figure in country music and a member of the Country Music Hall of Fame, has released a deeply moving music video for his last-ever recorded song, 'I'm Not Gonna Miss You.' Diagnosed with Alzheimer's disease in 2011, Campbell worked with producer Julian Raymond in 2013 to finish this final track. The song opens with heartfelt lyrics about his ongoing battle with Alzheimer's, while the music video weaves together moments from Campbell’s career and personal life, including scenes of him performing and with his family, alongside footage of medical consultations. As his illness advanced, Campbell, aged 78, was admitted to a specialized care facility in Nashville earlier this year. His family expressed their appreciation for the exceptional care he receives and thanked supporters for their prayers and encouragement. Campbell remained optimistic throughout his diagnosis, sharing in a 2012 CNN interview that he accepted his challenges with grace. Over his five-decade career, Campbell was celebrated for hits like 'Rhinestone Cowboy' and 'Wichita Lineman.' He concluded his musical journey with the 2011 album 'Ghost on Canvas' and a farewell tour, leaving behind a powerful legacy admired by many.
translated_content: گلن کیمبل، جو کنٹری میوزک کے ایک عظیم گلوکار اور کنٹری میوزک ہال آف فیم کے رکن ہیں، نے اپنی آخری گانے 'آئی ایم ناٹ گونا مس یو' کا جذباتی میوزک ویڈیو جاری کیا ہے۔ 2011 میں الزائمرز بیماری کی تشخیص ہونے کے بعد، کیمبل نے پروڈیوسر جولیان ریمونڈ کے ساتھ 2013 میں یہ آخری گانا مکمل کیا۔ یہ گانا ان کے مرض سے جدوجہد کی دل سے نکلی ہوئی شاعری کا آغاز ہے، جبکہ ویڈیو میں ان کی زندگی اور کیریئر کے لمحات دکھائے گئے ہیں، جیسے کہ اسٹیج پرفارمنس، فیملی کے ساتھ مناظر اور ڈاکٹر کے ساتھ ملاقاتیں۔ جب بیماری نے شدت اختیار کی، تو 78 سالہ کیمبل کو اس سال کے شروع میں نیش وِل کے ایک خصوصی نگہداشت کے مرکز میں داخل کرنا پڑا۔ ان کے خاندان نے شاندار نگہداشت اور سپورٹرز کی دعاؤں اور محبت کے لیے شکریہ ادا کیا۔ کیمبل نے ہمیشہ اپنی تشخیص کو حوصلے سے قبول کیا۔ 2012 کے ایک سی این این انٹرویو میں انہوں نے کہا کہ وہ مشکلات کو وقار کے ساتھ لیتے ہیں۔ پانچ دہائیوں پر مشتمل اپنے کیریئر میں کیمبل 'رائن اسٹون کاؤبائے' اور 'وچیتا لائن مین' جیسے اپنے سپر ہٹ گانوں کے لیے جانے جاتے ہیں۔ انہوں نے 2011 میں آخری البم 'گھوسٹ آن کینوس' اور الوداعی ٹور کے بعد موسیقی کا سفر مکمل کیا اور ایک قوی وراثت چھوڑی جسے لوگ آج بھی پسند کرتے ہیں۔

The negotiations to secure the release of hostages held by Hamas ultimately hinged on two crucial phone calls, forcing both sides to make difficult compromises. Israel insisted that releasing only 50 out of approximately 240 hostages was insufficient, demanding more. President Joe Biden persuaded Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu to accept the current terms while vowing continued efforts to free the remaining hostages.

Senior U.S. officials reported that Hamas wanted a five-day pause in fighting as part of the agreement. However, Israel would agree to no more than four days. Biden communicated to Qatar’s emir—who was mediating talks with Hamas—that four days was the maximum allowable pause at this stage.

The journey toward this deal was marked by slow progress, deep mistrust, difficult choices, and moments when negotiations nearly fell apart. Neither side obtained all of their demands, but if the deal is fully implemented, it could serve as a framework for future negotiations and potentially extend the temporary cease-fire.

“Last night’s deal is a testament to the tireless diplomacy and dedication of many across the U.S. government to bring Americans home,” Biden said Wednesday on X (formerly Twitter). “Now, it’s important that all aspects are fully implemented.”

The article is based on discussions with senior Biden administration officials, speaking anonymously to avoid jeopardizing diplomatic channels. The push to free the hostages began immediately after the Oct. 7 attack, in which Hamas killed roughly 1,200 people and took 240 hostages. Qatar, with connections to Hamas and strong U.S. ties, approached the White House about exploring a possible exchange. A select group of U.S. officials was designated to work secretly with Qatari and Israeli counterparts, led by Jake Sullivan, Brett McGurk, and Joshua Geltzer.

To preserve secrecy, other government agencies were excluded. McGurk coordinated daily with Sheikh Tamim, the emir of Qatar, later updating Sullivan and President Biden. Sullivan, in turn, kept frequent contact with Netanyahu’s close advisers, Ron Dermer and Tzachi Hanegbi.

The issue was especially personal for Biden, who met virtually with families of American hostages on October 13. He extended the meeting to ensure every family could share their story—an experience described by aides as one of the most challenging moments of his presidency.

On October 23, negotiations with Qatar led to the release of American citizens Natalie and Judith Raanan, with top U.S. officials closely monitoring their exit from Gaza in real time. This success reinforced the Biden administration’s belief in the effectiveness of the Qatari diplomatic channel.

For Israel, David Barnea, head of Mossad, took the lead in negotiations. He coordinated closely with William Burns, director of the CIA. Biden and Netanyahu spoke several times in late October, always focusing on the hostages.

Hamas signaled willingness to release women and children if Israeli forces delayed their planned ground offensive. Israel, wary of the deal’s firmness and lacking proof of life, proceeded with a phased campaign, allowing flexibility for a potential pause if needed.

As Israeli operations advanced, talks continued with both Qatar and Egypt. Biden personally called the emir of Qatar, shaping a proposal built around a phased release—starting with women and children—for Palestinians held in Israeli prisons. Israel required proof of life for the hostages, and details of who would be released.

On November 9, top officials including Burns, Sheikh Tamim, and Barnea met in Doha to review the draft. Shortly after, Biden told the emir that without detailed information about the hostages, there could be no deal. In response, Hamas provided criteria identifying the initial 50 hostages.

Sullivan met again with hostage families to reassure them. Meanwhile, Netanyahu continued pushing for the release of more hostages, but Biden urged him to accept the current terms with plans for future efforts.

As the agreement appeared near, talks stalled due to a communication blackout in Gaza. After restoration, Hamas temporarily withdrew, citing Israeli actions at Shifa Hospital—a site Israel and the U.S. claim Hamas uses as a military base. Israel refused to withdraw but maintained hospital operations, prompting talks to resume.

While in San Francisco, Biden made clear to the emir of Qatar that this was the final opportunity and Israel would stand firm on a four-day pause. McGurk and Sheikh Tamim finalized the text, involving CIA and Mossad leaders in the process. The proposal was transmitted to Hamas.

On the following morning in Cairo, U.S. officials were informed that Hamas accepted almost all terms. Final details were negotiated, and both Hamas and the Israeli government endorsed the agreement.

“This deal should bring home additional American hostages,” Biden said in a late-night statement, “and I will not stop until they are all released.”

حماس کے قبضے میں یرغمالیوں کی رہائی کے مذاکرات بالآخر دو اہم فون کالز پر آکر رُکے، جس میں دونوں فریقین کو مشکل سمجھوتے کرنا پڑے۔ اسرائیل کا اصرار تھا کہ تقریباً 240 میں سے صرف 50 یرغمالیوں کی رہائی کافی نہیں، مزید لوگوں کی رہائی چاہیے۔ صدر جو بائیڈن نے وزیراعظم بنیامین نیتن یاہو کو موجودہ شرائط قبول کرنے پر آمادہ کیا اور باقی یرغمالیوں کی رہائی کیلئے کوششیں جاری رکھنے کا وعدہ کیا۔

سینئر امریکی حکام کے مطابق، حماس نے معاہدے کے تحت لڑائی میں پانچ دن وقفہ مانگا، جبکہ اسرائیل چار دن پر ہی راضی تھا۔ بائیڈن نے قطر کے امیر، جو حماس سے بات چیت کے ثالث تھے، کو بتایا کہ فی الحال یہی زیادہ سے زیادہ وقفہ مل سکتا ہے۔

یہ معاہدہ سست روی، بے اعتمادی، مشکل فیصلوں اور ایسے مواقع سے بھرا ہوا راستہ تھا جب مذاکرات تقریباً ناکام ہو چکے تھے۔ کسی بھی فریق کو سارے مطالبات پورے نہیں ملے، لیکن اگر اس معاہدے پر عملدرآمد مکمل ہوا تو یہ مستقبل میں مزید مذاکرات اور عارضی جنگ بندی بڑھانے کے لیے ایک مثال بن سکتا ہے۔

"گزشتہ رات کا معاہدہ امریکی حکومت کی تھکادینے والی سفارتکاری اور عزم کا ثبوت ہے جو اپنے لوگوں کو واپس لانے کے لیے کوشاں رہی،" بائیڈن نے X (سابقہ ٹوئٹر) پر بدھ کو کہا۔ "اب ضروری ہے کہ معاہدے کے سارے نکات مکمل طور پر لاگو ہوں۔"

یہ رپورٹ سینئر بائیڈن انتظامیہ کے افسران کی بات چیت پر مبنی ہے، جو سفارتی رابطوں کو متاثر ہونے سے بچانے کے لیے گمنام رہنا چاہتے تھے۔ یرغمالیوں کی رہائی کی کوششیں 7 اکتوبر کے حملے کے بعد فوراً شروع ہوئیں، جس میں حماس نے تقریباً 1200 افراد کو ہلاک اور 240 کو یرغمال بنایا۔ قطر، جو حماس سے روابط رکھتا ہے اور امریکہ سے قریبی تعلقات ہے، نے وائٹ ہاؤس سے ممکنہ تبادلے کے بارے میں بات کی۔ صرف چند امریکی افسران کو خفیہ طور پر قطری اور اسرائیلی ہم منصبوں کے ساتھ کام کرنے کے لیے نامزد کیا گیا، جن میں جیک سولیوان، بریٹ مکگرک اور جوشوا گیلٹزر شامل تھے۔

مکمل رازداری کو یقینی بنانے کے لیے دیگر اداروں کو اس عمل سے دور رکھا گیا۔ مکگرک نے روزانہ قطر کے امیر شیخ تمیم سے رابطہ کیا اور بعد میں سولیوان اور صدر بائیڈن کو اپ ڈیٹ کیا۔ سولیوان نے نیتن یاہو کے قریبی مشیروں رون ڈرمر اور زاخی ہانگبی سے بھی بار بار رابطے میں رہے۔

یہ معاملہ صدر بائیڈن کے لیے ذاتی طور پر بہت اہم تھا، جنہوں نے 13 اکتوبر کو امریکی یرغمالیوں کے اہل خانہ سے ویڈیو کال پر ملاقات کی۔ انہوں نے کال کا وقت بڑھا دیا تاکہ ہر خاندان اپنی بات کہ سکے۔ حکام نے اسے ان کی صدارت کے مشکل ترین لمحات میں سے ایک قرار دیا۔

23 اکتوبر کو قطر کے ذریعے مذاکرات سے امریکی شہری نٹالی اور جڈت راعنان کی رہائی ممکن ہوئی، جسے اہم امریکی حکام نے حقیقی وقت میں دیکھا۔ اس کامیابی سے انتظامیہ کو قطر کے سفارتی کردار پر یقین مزید پختہ ہوا۔

اسرائیل کی طرف سے موساد کے سربراہ ڈیوڈ برنیا مذاکرات کی قیادت کر رہے تھے، جو سی آئی اے ڈائریکٹر ولیم برنز سے قریبی رابطے میں تھے۔ بائیڈن اور نیتن یاہو نے اکتوبر کے آخر میں کئی بار بات کی، جس میں یرغمالیوں پر توجہ مرکوز رہی۔

حماس نے خواتین اور بچوں کو رہا کرنے کی خواہش ظاہر کی، بشرطیکہ اسرائیلی فوج گراؤنڈ آپریشن میں تاخیر کرے۔ اسرائیل کو معاہدے کی یقین دہانی اور حیات کی تصدیق نہ ہونے پر بے یقینی تھی، اس لیے فوجی مہم مرحلہ وار چلائی تاکہ جب ضرورت ہو لڑائی روکی جا سکے۔

اسرائیلی آپریشن جاری رہنے کے ساتھ قطر اور مصر سے بھی بات چیت چلتی رہی۔ بائیڈن نے خود امیر قطر کو کال کی اور خواتین اور بچوں کی مرحلہ وار رہائی کے بدلے اسرائیلی جیلوں میں قید فلسطینیوں کی رہائی پر مبنی تجویز تشکیل دی۔ اسرائیل نے یرغمالیوں کی شناخت اور حیات کی تصدیق مانگی۔

9 نومبر کو اہم حکام، بشمول برنز، شیخ تمیم اور برنیا، نے دوحہ میں مسودہ کا جائزہ لیا۔ اس کے بعد بائیڈن نے امیر کو واضح کیا کہ یرغمالیوں کی تفصیلات کے بغیر کوئی معاہدہ نہیں ہو سکتا۔ جواباً، حماس نے ابتدائی 50 یرغمالیوں کی شناختی معیار فراہم کیے۔

سولیوان نے دوبارہ یرغمال خاندانوں سے ملاقات کی۔ ادھر نیتن یاہو مزید یرغمالیوں کی رہائی پر مصر رہے، مگر بائیڈن نے انہیں فوری طور پر موجودہ معاہدہ قبول اور آئندہ مزید کوششوں کا وعدہ کیا۔

جب معاہدہ قریب آیا تو غزہ میں مواصلاتی بلیک آؤٹ کے سبب بات چیت رک گئی۔ بحالی کے بعد، حماس نے شفا ہسپتال پر اسرائیلی کارروائی کا حوالہ دیتے ہوئے بات چیت سے ہٹ گئی—یہ وہ جگہ ہے جسے اسرائیل و امریکہ حماس کا فوجی مرکز سمجھتے ہیں۔ اسرائیل نے انخلاء سے انکار کیا مگر ہسپتال چلتا رہا، جس پر مذاکرات بحال ہوئے۔

A 161-foot luxury superyacht named 'Rockstar' became stuck under a drawbridge near Bay Harbour Islands, Florida, on Tuesday afternoon. The multimillion-dollar vessel, valued at just under $21 million and costing over $250,000 per week to charter, was carrying 15 people at the time. Fortunately, everyone on board escaped without injury.

The yacht was being towed from Fort Lauderdale to Miami by two tugboats when the eastern section of the Broad Causeway drawbridge—connecting North Miami with Harbor Islands and Bal Harbour—collapsed onto the upper portion of the vessel. The crash severely damaged the area near the yacht's hot tub, reportedly causing tens of thousands of dollars in damages, according to WTSP.

The Rockstar remained pinned beneath the bridge for more than 20 minutes before it was dislodged and towed away. The impressive yacht, built by Trinity Yachts in 2009 and registered in George Town, Cayman Islands, boasts five staterooms, a two-level master suite with a private lounge and his-and-her bathrooms, and offers expansive 280-degree ocean views. The yacht also features a saloon and dining room adorned with classic Hollywood photographs, as well as a seven-person spa pool.

Originally named 'Blind Date,' Rockstar is currently for sale through International Yacht Collection with an asking price of just under $21 million, as listed on boatinternational.com.

In the aftermath of the incident, the drawbridge remained closed for several hours while city engineers conducted a safety inspection. CBS Miami reported the 60-year-old Broad Causeway is set for a $13 million renovation beginning in January, which will involve replacing parts of the drawbridge’s mechanism. The cause of the accident is being investigated by authorities. 'We’re not sure what collided with what yet,' US Coast Guard spokesperson Mark Barney told the Miami Herald.

اس یاٹ کا سابقہ نام 'بلائنڈ ڈیٹ' تھا، اور یہ اس وقت انٹرنیشنل یاٹ کلیکشن کے ذریعے boatinternational.com پر تقریباً 21 ملین ڈالر طلب قیمت پر فروخت کے لیے دستیاب ہے۔

article_content: Jordan Higgins, 31, has admitted to robbing a newsagent near his home at dawn and stealing £2,000 worth of cigarettes. Higgins, son of former snooker champion Alex 'Hurricane' Higgins, along with an accomplice, entered a shop in Cheadle, near Manchester, in January. They pushed shopkeeper Steven Gee from his stool and filled a duvet cover with cigarettes taken from the shelves. Both men wore headgear to conceal their identities; no weapons were reported during the incident. At Minshull Street Crown Court, Higgins—whose middle name is Alexander after his father—pleaded guilty to robbery. He stood before the court in a suit, speaking quietly, and confirmed his name and personal details. Sentencing was deferred pending the completion of pre-sentence reports. Higgins, of Cheadle, was granted bail ahead of sentencing scheduled for November 13. Judge Andrew Lowcock noted the likelihood of an immediate custodial sentence. After court, Higgins was seen outside smoking with friends. Jordan was born a year after his father won the World Snooker Championship, a victory remembered for Alex Higgins embracing his wife Lynne and daughter Lauren. Jordan's online posts sometimes pay tribute to his father's snooker achievements. He served as a pallbearer at Alex Higgins' funeral alongside snooker greats Jimmy White and Ken Doherty. Alex Higgins completed snooker's Triple Crown, winning the UK Championship in 1983 and the Masters in 1978 and 1981. Despite his success, Alex Higgins faced personal and financial difficulties, including addiction and legal issues, and died from throat cancer in 2010.
translated_content: جوردن ہیگنز، 31 سالہ، نے اپنے گھر کے قریب ایک نیوز ایجنٹ کو طلوع فجر کے وقت لوٹ کر £2,000 کی سگریٹ چوری کرنے کا اعتراف کیا ہے۔ ہیگنز، سابق اسنوکر چیمپیئن ایلکس 'ہریکین' ہیگنز کے بیٹے، نے اپنے ساتھی کے ساتھ جنوری میں مانچسٹر کے قریب چیڈل میں ایک دکان میں داخل ہو کر یہ واردات کی۔ انہوں نے دکان کے مالک اسٹیون جی کو اسٹول سے دھکیل دیا اور شیلف سے سگریٹس نکال کر ایک رضائی میں ڈال دیں۔ دونوں افراد نے اپنی شناخت چھپانے کے لیے سر پر کپڑا پہنا ہوا تھا؛ واقعے کے دوران کوئی ہتھیار استعمال نہیں ہوا۔ منشل اسٹریٹ کراؤن کورٹ میں ہیگنز—جن کا درمیانی نام ان کے والد کے نام پر ایلگزینڈر ہے—نے ڈکیتی کا اعتراف کیا۔ انہوں نے عدالت میں خاموشی سے سوٹ پہن کر موقف پیش کیا اور اپنے نام اور ذاتی تفصیلات کی تصدیق کی۔ سزا سنانے سے قبل ابتدائی رپورٹس تیار کی جائیں گی۔ چیڈل کے ہیگنز کو سزا سنانے سے پہلے ضمانت پر رہا کیا گیا، جو 13 نومبر کو متوقع ہے۔ جج اینڈریو لوکاک نے فوری جیل کی سزا کا امکان ظاہر کیا۔ عدالت کے بعد ہیگنز کو دوستوں کے ساتھ باہر سگریٹ پیتے ہوئے دیکھا گیا۔ جوردن ایک سال بعد پیدا ہوئے جب ان کے والد نے ورلڈ اسنوکر چیمپیئن شپ جیتی تھی—a کامیابی جس میں ایلکس ہیگنز نے اپنی بیوی لن اور بیٹی لارین کو بانہوں میں لیا تھا۔ جوردن کی آن لائن پوسٹس اکثر اپنے والد کی اسنوکر کامیابیوں کو خراج تحسین پیش کرتی ہیں۔ انہوں نے ایلکس ہیگنز کی تدفین میں اسنوکر کے مشہور کھلاڑی جمی وائٹ اور کین ڈوہرٹی کے ساتھ مل کر جنازہ اٹھایا تھا۔ ایلکس ہیگنز نے اسنوکر کا ٹرپل کراؤن مکمل کیا، 1983 میں یوکے چیمپیئن شپ اور 1978 اور 1981 میں ماسٹرز جیتے۔ اپنی کامیابیوں کے باوجود، ایلکس ہیگنز کو ذاتی اور مالی مشکلات، نشے اور قانونی مسائل کا سامنا کرنا پڑا اور وہ 2010 میں گلے کے کینسر کی وجہ سے انتقال کر گئے۔

article_content: The family of Dirk Schroeder, a 74-year-old patient from Germany, is seeking £80,000 in compensation after surgeons left 16 items inside his body during routine prostate cancer surgery. Initially told he could expect to live another six years, Mr. Schroeder experienced severe pain following the operation. Months later, a nurse visiting his home in Hanover noticed a large gauze pad protruding from his surgical wound. Further examination revealed that surgeons had left behind a variety of equipment—including a needle, a six-inch roll of bandage, a six-inch-long compress, several swabs, and a fragment of a surgical mask. It took two additional operations to remove all the foreign objects. The incident occurred in 2009; although Mr. Schroeder initially survived, his cancer progressed, and he died the following year. His family has now filed a lawsuit against the unnamed hospital, citing gross negligence. Family lawyer and medical expert Annette Corinth described the extent of foreign objects left inside Schroeder as unprecedented in medical literature. While the hospital claimed the objects entered the body after surgery, it did not provide an explanation. The family devoted significant resources to Mr. Schroeder’s care and home modifications, arguing that the negligence caused additional suffering and may have shortened his life.

article_content: Team India was defeated by Australia in the ICC World Cup 2023 final held at Ahmedabad's Narendra Modi Stadium. Many celebrities, including Shah Rukh Khan, Kajol, Kareena Kapoor, Ajay Devgn, and Sidharth Malhotra, shared supportive messages for the cricket team. Arjun Kapoor also expressed his admiration with a heartfelt note on Instagram. On Monday, Arjun Kapoor posted on his Instagram Stories, stating: "It feels strange to write that we didn’t win. This Indian team was flawless, yet Australia managed to outperform on the day and stop what is arguably the best team in world cricket. This doesn't take away from the amazing @indiancricketteam and their skills as a team and as individuals. My love for cricket grew watching this team play; it made me feel proud to be an Indian! Thank you, Team India." After the match, Shah Rukh Khan posted on his social media account: "The way the Indian team has played throughout this tournament is honorable; they have shown great spirit and determination. It’s sport—bad days happen. Unfortunately, today was one of them, but thank you, Team India, for making us proud of our cricketing legacy. You bring joy to the whole country. Love and respect. You make us a proud nation."

article_content: Sainsbury's has issued a recall for 500g packets of its So Organic Sultanas purchased over the past five months, after tests detected salmonella contamination in some packets. The supermarket, with more than 1,000 UK stores, notified affected customers—particularly those with online purchase records—about the recall. Chris Dennis, a father of two from Tunbridge Wells, Kent, received an email alert after buying the product earlier in the month, expressing concern for families unaware of the potential risk. He stated that he felt reassured because his family had not yet opened the packet. The email from Sainsbury's explained that routine testing found a low level of salmonella in the 500g Organic Sultanas, and urged customers not to consume the product but to return it for a full refund. The company apologized for the inconvenience and provided a helpline for further questions. Salmonella infection can affect anyone but is especially dangerous for young children, elderly people, and those with weakened immune systems. Symptoms can include watery diarrhea, stomach cramps, vomiting, and fever, typically lasting four to seven days. Severe cases may require treatment for dehydration. Transmission of salmonella often occurs through contaminated food, especially of animal origin, or by contact with fecal matter from infected people or animals. Sainsbury’s confirmed all affected products have been removed from shelves and stated that no other products are impacted.

article_content: A legendary U.S. postage stamp, famous for its printing mistake, sold for a remarkable $2 million at auction. The Inverted Jenny, originally issued in 1918, is highly prized among collectors because it features an upside-down airplane—a rare printing error. This mistake, combined with the stamp’s scarcity, has cemented its status as one of the most coveted collectibles in philately. The Inverted Jenny was exhibited at Sotheby’s auction house in 2021, drawing significant attention from stamp enthusiasts. Scott Trepel, president of Siegel Auction Galleries in New York and a leading expert, has termed it the ‘icon of stamp collecting.’

article_content: Seattle Seahawks cornerback Richard Sherman has reignited the pre-Super Bowl trash talk, claiming that New England Patriots quarterback Tom Brady isn’t quite the clean-cut nice guy many fans believe him to be. Sherman, a two-time Pro Bowler, famously clashed with Brady after a close 24-23 Seahawks win in 2012. After that game, Sherman approached Brady on the field, exchanged heated words, and later posted a photo of the encounter on Twitter with the caption, 'U mad bro?' On Wednesday, Sherman provided more insight into the incident and their rivalry as the February 1 Super Bowl approaches. 'People think Tom Brady always does everything right and never says a bad word to anyone—but we know that’s not always true,' Sherman said at a press conference. 'In that moment, he said some things, and we responded. He apparently doesn’t remember what he said.' Sherman alleges that Brady taunted the Seahawks defense throughout the 2012 matchup, telling them they were 'nobodies', and implying they should approach him after the game if his team won. Sherman recalled, 'Are we supposed to take that well? Should I ask for your autograph too?' With a touch of sarcasm, Sherman also commented on Brady’s interactions with game officials: 'I’m sure when he’s yelling at the refs, he’s just saying “good job, fantastic job, keep it up.”' Sherman is currently managing an elbow injury sustained during the Seahawks' thrilling 28-22 overtime victory over the Green Bay Packers in the NFC Championship Game. However, he remains optimistic about his readiness for the Super Bowl: 'It should be better by game day. Honestly, there shouldn’t be any limitations. My left stiff-arm might not be perfect, but other than that, I’ll be fine.' Jokingly, when asked about his range of motion, Sherman said, 'If I had to slap my brother, I’d be able to do it.'

article_content: The best sangrias for fall and winter capture the rich, comforting flavors of the season. Instead of settling for simple mixes, opt for well-crafted recipes featuring ingredients like cinnamon apples, pumpkin spice, cranberries, and pears.  Here are five exceptional sangrias to enliven your autumn:  1. The Only Sangria Recipe You’ll Ever Need: This foolproof sangria requires no steeping. Choose a rich red wine (like Rioja or Tempranillo) to stand up to the added fruit flavors. Ingredients: 1 bottle (750ml) rich red wine, 1 cup spiced rum, 1/4 cup maple syrup, 2 blood oranges (one sliced, one for garnish), 1 cup cranberries, 1 cup cherries, 2 cups ginger beer. Instructions: Combine all ingredients in a large pitcher and serve over ice. Garnish with fruit on cocktail sticks.  2. Sittin’ On The ‘Orch (Apple Cider Autumn Sangria): Filled with cozy fall flavors, this sangria emphasizes apples and cinnamon. Wine Recommendation: Medium-bodied orange wine. Ingredients: 1 bottle (750ml) orange wine, 1 cup apple cider, sliced red apples, 2 cinnamon sticks, 1/4 cup brandy. Instructions: Mix all ingredients in a pitcher (no ice), refrigerate for at least 4 hours, then serve over ice. For a mulled wine, heat with orange slices and star anise.  3. Crimson Wave (Cranberry-Orange Red Wine Sangria): A returning favorite; makes great use of cranberries and oranges. Wine Recommendation: Fruity and tart red, such as Zinfandel or Cabernet Sauvignon. Ingredients: 1 bottle (750ml) red wine, 1/2 cup cranberry juice, 1/2 cup orange juice, 2 oranges (sliced), a splash of Grand Marnier. Instructions: Mix everything in a pitcher and, for extra flair, top with sugared cranberries.  4. PSS – Pumpkin Spice Sangria: Inspired by pumpkin spice lattes, this sangria is a must-try for autumn. Wine Recommendation: Medium to full-bodied floral white, like Viognier or Moscatel. Ingredients: 1 bottle (750ml) white wine, 200g golden caster sugar, 50g light brown sugar, 1 tsp vanilla extract, 1 tsp cinnamon, ¼ tsp ground cloves, 2 tsp ground ginger, nutmeg to taste, 2 tbsp canned pumpkin purée, 2 shots bourbon. Instructions: Simmer sugars, spices, vanilla, and pumpkin purée with 125ml water to make a syrup (5-10 min). Add 2 shots of syrup to a pitcher with wine and bourbon, serve over ice. Store leftover syrup up to 2 weeks.  5. The Pear Tree (White Wine Pear Sangria): A festive, elegant option for holiday parties. Wine Recommendation: Medium to full-bodied white wine, such as Chardonnay. Ingredients: 1 bottle white wine, 1 cup pear juice, 1 tbsp manuka honey, 2 pears, 1/2 tsp nutmeg, splash of brandy. Instructions: Thinly slice one pear, mix all ingredients in a large pitcher, and chill for at least 4 hours. Serve with pear garnish—star shapes or simple slices.

article_content: A man from New Hampshire fatally shot his wife at Wentworth-Douglass Hospital in Dover early Tuesday morning before taking his own life. The incident occurred around 6 a.m. in the hospital's critical care unit, where both individuals were found deceased. Shortly before the shooting, Mark Lavoie, 50, posted a message on Facebook explaining that he intended the act as a 'double suicide.' He wrote that his wife, Katherine Lavoie, 49, had struggled with mental illness for years and was recently placed on life support, which she disliked. In his post, Mark wrote, 'I am more than happy to sacrifice my life to fix my doing and join her spirit in a happier place.' He expressed that his decision was out of love, noting Katherine did not want to remain on a respirator. Mark stated that he wanted others to understand his reasoning, even if they could not relate. At the time the news broke, authorities had not officially released the couple’s names. Mark’s sister, Dorcas Lavoie, told The Associated Press that her brother acted 'out of love.' The case is being investigated by the New Hampshire Attorney General's Office. Assistant Attorney General Jay McCormack stated the investigation would be thorough and include a review of social media. 'While the investigation is still in its early stages, the two deaths appear to be the result of a murder-suicide,' McCormack noted. The circumstances leading to Katherine being placed on life support remain unclear, but Mark mentioned in his post that he blamed himself for calling 911, offering no further details. His Facebook post also discussed funeral arrangements and dividing assets. In his message, Mark wrote, 'Please don’t mourn for me, my spirit will be in a much better place with my soul mate; you may even catch a glimpse of us from time to time.' Friends attempted to reach out to Mark after his post appeared online, but the tragedy had already taken place. Other friends later expressed their condolences and shared memories of the couple online. Wentworth-Douglass Hospital, which has 178 beds, remained open following the incident. Officials confirmed that patient care and services continued without interruption. Autopsies are scheduled to be conducted by the Office of the Chief Medical Examiner.

بتایا کہ ان کے بھائی نے 'محبت میں یہ قدم اٹھایا'۔ اس کیس کی تحقیقات نیو ہیمپشائر اٹارنی جنرل کے دفتر کے سپرد ہیں۔ اسسٹنٹ اٹارنی جنرل جے میک کورمک کا کہنا ہے کہ تحقیقات میں سوشل میڈیا کا جائزہ بھی شامل ہوگا۔ 'اگرچہ تحقیقات ابھی ابتدائی مراحل میں ہیں، دونوں اموات بظاہر مرڈر-سویسائیڈ کا نتیجہ معلوم ہوتی ہیں،' میک کورمک نے کہا۔ یہ واضح نہیں کہ کیتھرین لائف سپورٹ پر کیسے پہنچیں، لیکن مارک نے اپنے پیغام میں لکھا ہے کہ اس نے 911 پر کال کی تھی، جس کو وہ اپنی غلطی سمجھتے ہیں، تاہم بطور وضاحت مزید کچھ نہیں لکھا۔ مارک کے فیس بک پیغام میں تدفین کے انتظامات اور جائیداد کی تقسیم کا بھی ذکر تھا۔ اپنے پیغام میں مارک نے لکھا، 'میری خاطر غم نہ کریں، میری روح اپنی شریک حیات کے ساتھ بہتر مقام پر ہوگی؛ ہو سکتا ہے کبھی کبھار ہمیں محسوس بھی کریں۔' مارک کے فیس بک پیغام کے بعد دوستوں نے انہیں روکنے کی کوشش کی، لیکن افسوسناک واقعہ ہو چکا تھا۔ دیگر دوستوں نے بعد میں جوڑے کے لیے تعزیت اور یادیں آن لائن شیئر کیں۔ وینٹورتھ-ڈگلس اسپتال، جس میں 178 بیڈز ہیں، واقعے کے بعد بھی کھلا رہا۔ حکام نے بتایا کہ مریضوں کی دیکھ بھال اور خدمات متاثر نہیں ہوئیں۔ چیف میڈیکل ایگزامینر کے دفتر کی جانب سے پوسٹ مارٹم کیا جائے گا۔
